entries.question: Correct or re-read, wave 2: Sanskrit and Arabic

Before any correction is applied, correct.mjs needs a guard that refuses a 'corrected' text whose body has almost no letters next to its draft. Cost of the correction per 1K pages: about 5% of a Claude account-week in each language. The Flash re-read costs about 1.05 agy calls a page.

entries.question: Read or recall? Vision models on famous vs obscure pages, with and without the image
entries.verdict: With the page image, both models read famous and obscure pages about equally well (Opus 0.91-0.99 accuracy on both; famous minus obscure between -0.05 and +0.04), so memory does not visibly inflate reading at full resolution. Without the image, Opus reproduces famous pages measurably better than matched obscure ones in Latin (R 0.15 [0.04, 0.28], all from canonical works: 0.31; RECITATION-refused pages 0.00), Hebrew (0.28 [0.12, 0.44]) and Sanskrit (0.14 [0.04, 0.24]), and in Greek once 4 mislabelled 'obscure' pages it recites are set aside (0.25 [0.08, 0.42]). Gemini 3.8 Flash low does so only in Hebrew (0.21 [0.08, 0.36]). Opus's Chinese 'gap' is an artefact of the cross-edition e-text key. 5 of 81 'obscure' pages are texts Opus recites from the name alone.
entries.decision: The preregistered rule says the full 10 x 50 run is justified (Opus shows a measurable gap in >= 2 scripts). Run it only redesigned: one key type for every page, an obscure label confirmed by a no-image probe as well as lookups, n-gram recall as the memory measure, and a degraded-image arm. At this pilot's cost it needs about 20x the Opus calls, so several account-weeks: Derek decides when (#7570).

entries.verdict: Applied: 2,805 Yigdzin (vLLM 0.29) page reads written to 40 held Tibetan books under the #4523 write rule; by eye 20/20 drawn text pages and 5/5 live pages clean (0 invented, 0 off-leaf). entries.decision: Pages written, books stay held (specialist-ocr-lane-4523); no translation queued. The reader's blank marker is not evidence of a blank leaf; withhold it.

entries.question: Flash-low correction across 20 Kangyur volumes: span gate, audit first
entries.verdict: The span gate PASSES across books. 20 visible manuscript Kangyur volumes were drawn across Thadrak, Neyphug and the EAP310 'Kanjur' set and across sections. 2 seeded changed pages a volume were corrected by agy Flash-low (CORR request) and judged by judge B. Result: 1 of 38 pages worse (by-book 95%: 0.000-0.079), 35 better, 2 same; no volume with 2 worse. The leaf shows the correction at 334 of 364 decided spans (92% [89, 94]); controls 71/76 (93%). On the 36 two-leaf (seam) frames: 0 worse. One volume (Thadrak 'Bum Ja) gave no writable page: all 6 candidates were held by the ya-btags guard or the 25% cap. Contrast: the split-leaf tantra volume Neyphug rGyud Tsha failed the same gate on the same day (10/40).
entries.decision: Derek 2026-10-26 23:15Z: apply under the fixed-vs-introduced rule. 19 volumes, 7,287 pages written on 2026-10-27; then a diff-QA pass put risky spans the leaf does not confirm back to Yigdzin (runs diffqa-6740-*)

entries.question: Flash-low correction, one split-leaf Kangyur volume, gated write
entries.verdict: NO-GO for writing the agy Flash-low correction over the Yigdzin read of Neyphug Kanjur rGyud Tsha (962 split leaves). The pre-registered gate was at most 2 of 40 pages worse at span level and controls at least 90%. Result: 10 of 40 pages worse and controls 67/80 (84%); both fail. Judge B saw the correction at 95 of 120 decided spans (79% [71, 85]). Whole page, the correction moves leaves toward Derge: +0.0054 identity on 907 leaves with a parallel (486 better, 147 worse). This is the second tantra volume to fail the span gate by the same margin (Thadrak rGyud 'bum Kha, 2026-10-15: 10/40).
entries.decision: Nothing written to pages; the volume keeps its Yigdzin read (#6740, #6560 gate)

entries.question: Do full-page SigLIP2 vectors retrieve well enough to embed ~21M pages, and can the fetch keep the card busy?
entries.verdict: SigLIP2-so400m vectors of full archived page masters retrieve well enough to embed all of them. On the 100K pilot, top-5 is right by eye 35/75 (P@5 0.47 strict) and related 49/75 (0.65) over 15 queries. Misses are subjects the 100K sample does not contain, plus text pages that carry the query WORD. Blank pages, covers and colour cards do not dominate: 1 blank page, 1 colour card and 1 bookplate in 75, and 2 hubs in 700 top-10 slots. Reading R2 over the S3 API from worker processes lifts the run from 15.8 to 43.7 img/s (GPU busy 0.33 → 0.95–0.98), so 21.55M pages take about 5.7 GPU-days.
entries.decision: Full run queued on gex45 as 16 chunks of 1.5M rows (zz-siglip2-full-c000…c015), with no manifest filter. Live books run first (13.53M rows), then hidden (8.01M). About $7.76 of R2 Class B reads and no Worker requests. Serve-time filters (one hit per book, bookplate/blank near-duplicate suppression) go to the serving PR.

entries.question: Router tests on idle quota: six test-next cells, judged against the image
entries.verdict: Six of the router table's test-next cells, 30 pages each, one page per book, judged by the one Opus judge against the image. No cell switches under the 2% absolute wrong-text bar. Chinese Paddle dice < 0.90 goes from UNTESTED to HOLD → Paddle > Opus: as judged 29/30, 26/30 after a name check against Kanripo (the judge accepted 五殺大夫 where the leaf prints 五羖大夫), agy Flash high 17/30, Paddle alone 14/30. German Flash-Lite OCR keeps lite > Opus (28/30, 1 wrong text); lite > agy Flash-low ties at 28/30 with 2 wrong text. German 3 Flash OCR: the draft alone 29/30 with 0 wrong text, Opus 29/29. Latin lite > agy Flash-low 24/30 against Opus 30/30 on the pilot's pages: keep Opus. Latin 3 Flash is HOLD (3 Flash 21/30, agy Flash-low 23/30). French Flash-Lite > agy Flash-low 27/29 switches only under the relative wrong-text bar. German translation, 30 more pages: Opus CLI 23/30, 3 Flash 19/30, Flash-Lite 11/30; still HOLD. Tibetan did not run (no Derge index on gex45).
entries.decision: Proposals only: router table rebuilt as scripts/eval/estimator/router-table/2026-10-26-router-tests.md/.json (before: 2026-10-26.md). No routing-table edits (#6740)

entries.question: Router table: acceptance against the image as the decision-maker, Beta-binomial per cell
entries.verdict: The router's decision-maker is now one table per cell with Beta-binomial posteriors on acceptance against the image (route-judge pilot, #7376), with v1/v2 worth at most 5 pages of prior. Under the stated rules, Latin lite keeps its Opus correction (30/30, P(acc >= 0.8) 0.96). Tibetan, German translation and the served Chinese corrections are HOLD at n = 30: the best route in each (Flash-low 26/30, Opus CLI 26/30, Paddle > Opus 24/30) does not reach P(acc >= 0.8) >= 0.9. The 2% wrong-text bar passes only a route with 0 wrong-text pages in 30. v1's P(floors) is not acceptance: it gave lite Latin 0.04, and the judge accepted 17/30. The queue's next three tests are Chinese Paddle dice < 0.90, German lite OCR and German 3 Flash OCR.
entries.decision: Proposals only: scripts/eval/estimator/router-table/ (rules.json, build.py, 2026-10-26.md/.json). No routing-table edits (#6740)

entries.question: Can a cheap classifier predict a page's script, kind and leaf count from the image alone, before the read?
entries.verdict: From the page image alone, on gex45 for $0, script and leaf count are decision-grade: where a SigLIP2-so400m probe and Qwen3-VL-8B agree, script is right on 93/93 check pages and 1,852/1,853 held labels, leaf count on 94/94 and 1,392/1,395. Chinese tables are usable (agreement calls 239 pages table, 236 of them table/mixed/diagram). Music is a VLM-only call (75/78). Date-dense is NOT readable before the read: the best arm finds 62% of the #4763 date-dense pages at 75% precision, and 91 date-dense pages are called prose.
entries.decision: Owed: whether to adopt the proposed `pages.page_class` field (a data write, Derek) and feed the router's script / split / table / music cells from it. Number-dense stays a post-read cell (numeral census of the first read).

entries.question: Can a fixed order catch wrong table cells without an image or a model?
entries.verdict: A text-only check that planetary-hours columns follow the fixed Chaldean order flags 71 pages in 46 books across the 2026-10-26 corpus mirror. By eye, 5 of 14 readable flags in a random 15 were real transcription or translation errors (36%), 2 faithful, 7 detector artifacts. On the Book of Wonders all 3 of its flags were real errors.
entries.decision: Use the 71 as a by-eye review list, not an automatic correction; artifact fixes from this sample are in the detector.

entries.question: Kraus 1935: 25 more pages so the router can route the cell
entries.verdict: On 25 more pages of Kraus's 1935 print edition (29 with the gate's 4), every reader gives a usable page almost every time. Opus 5.5: 25/25, 0 misleading. agy Gemini 3.8 Flash low: 23/25; the other 2 were cut by Gemini's filter (fixed message, the retry cut too). Flash-Lite (production prompt): 20/25 under the stricter judge; 3 of its 5 MISLEADING grades rest only on a repeated page number. Refit with the new rows, the pooled OCR estimator now routes the cell: Opus is the only route that clears the CER bar (P = 1.00; agy 0.16, Flash-Lite 0.02). agy's P(not read) on Kraus is 0.16 [0.04, 0.40]. The router leaves the cell at 'test', because an Opus image call is still unmetered.
entries.decision: Kraus 1935 (582 pages): Opus 5.5 via claude -p, one read per page (about 1.7–8.5 weekly points of one account, by the gate's points range). The cheaper alternative the data supports: agy 3.8 Flash low, falling back to Flash-Lite on the filter's fixed message. That chain was usable on 29/29 pages, but it does not clear the router's CER bar. It strips Flash-Lite's vowel marks on the cut pages (marks CER 3.9% against 0.6%). Releasing the hold is Derek's call.

entries.question: Do estimator routes pool reads made under different prompts?
entries.verdict: With the prompt in a route's key, 8 of 36 production routes split on recorded prompts (14 if the top-level prompt_version labels are taken at their word), and 136 of the 2,090 did-not-read cells pooled more than one recorded prompt (72 of the 86 material ones are Flash-Lite OCR, v16 against v19.1). 85% of the pages in those cells have no prompt recorded at all.
entries.decision: Estimator rows now carry provenance (provenance.mjs); v2/v3 adopt routeKey = engine x prompt id@version x read mode. No routing change, no production write.

entries.question: Untested language cells: flash-lite (and agy Flash) OCR and flash-lite translation, judged by Opus against the page image
entries.verdict: First numbers for 36 untested language cells, one page per book, Opus as the judge (not a human reference). Flash-lite reads Italian, Spanish, Russian, Danish and Polish print at a median CER of 2% or less. It is poor on Korean (classical Chinese woodblock, 11.5%; agy Flash 5.9%, better on 24 of 27 pages), on Ottoman/Arabic-script Turkish (15–18%), and on manuscripts in Middle English, Middle High German and Middle French (about 21%). Russian translation scores a fidelity mean of 4.5 (n=30), Portuguese 3.9 (n=18). Samaritan, Yiddish and Avestan are not measured: the judge could not read most of those pages.

entries.question: /26 · Same-judge, image-grounded read of production routes: the pilot, run
entries.verdict: One Opus judge read 290 route outputs against the page image, with no Opus text as the key. Every correction route a reader would accept more often than its draft: Latin lite 17/30 to Opus correction 30/30; Chinese Paddle 3/30 to the served Opus correction 24/30; Tibetan Yigdzin 17/30 to Flash-low 26/30 or Opus 25/30. In German, Opus CLI English scores 26/30, against 3 Flash 22/30 and Flash-Lite 15/30. Kanripo agrees with the judge's order on 16/16 Chinese pairs and Derge on 25/27 Tibetan ones. The judge caught 8/10 planted Tibetan syllables and agrees with by-eye reads on 28/30. It missed one confident wrong name inside an Opus correction. Two served wrong-leaf finds were contained.
entries.decision: Proposed, per cell: Latin, the Opus correction of lite pages (#5924). Chinese, Paddle not served raw; the correction stays and the tables question stays open (#6871). Tibetan, a Kangyur-volume gate for the Flash-low correction (#6560). German, Opus CLI replaces Flash-Lite English, not 3 Flash (#7263). Derek decides.

entries.question: Route census: what production's routes already did, as estimator evidence
entries.verdict: Production's own record now gives the OCR estimator input rows in its existing formats: 2,261 did-not-read and guard k-of-n rows over 30.5M live pages, 596 accuracy rows scoring production's stored reads of 545 reference pages, 671 draft-to-replacement cells (change rates, not accuracy), and 60 days of pages delivered per route. Only the Gemini API writers stamp a failed read; the other routes (Paddle, Yigdzin, Kraken, the CLI lanes, Claude) leave no stamp, so they get no did-not-read row.
entries.decision: Rows for estimator v2/v3 to ingest (#6740). No routing change and no write to production.

entries.question: OCR estimator v1 with Arabic charts: does the pooled posterior agree with the Jābir gate?
entries.verdict: Pooled with every other chart, the Arabic-manuscript posterior agrees with the #7341 gate: Opus 5.5 is the only route that clears the bar (P = 1.00; next best agy 3.8 Flash high at 0.36), P(lowest CER) 0.56, and agy 3.8 Flash low loses 0.57 [0.32, 0.82] of alchemical manuscript pages to the CLI filter. Before the gate the pooled model got the engine order right (Opus < agy < Flash-Lite) but put every level 2–6× too high, and it predicted 1 [0, 3] filter-cut pages where 16 of 26 were observed. For Kraus's print edition the pooled posterior does not support the gate's agy-first route: the filter term learned on the manuscripts carries to Kraus (P(not read) 0.28 [0.07, 0.63]), and with 4 pages agy and Opus are both below the router's 5-page floor.
entries.decision: Jabir manuscripts: Opus, as the gate decided (the pooled fit agrees). Kraus 1935: test agy 3.8 Flash low on ~25 more Kraus pages before routing it there; the router cannot route that cell from 4 pages (#7341).

entries.question: How well does the production lite lane read the unread Latin print backlog, by typeface, and does the long-s pass help?
entries.verdict: On the UNREAD Latin print backlog, flash-lite on the live production prompt (v19.1) reads roman, italic and mixed roman/italic type at a median 1.2–1.8% CER (view N) against a blind single Opus read, but gothic type at 12.2% (CI 9.2–14.6), with 45 of 49 gothic pages judged misleading and 8 of 100 gothic pages looping to the token cap. The long-s pass changes nothing measurable at the median under the production prompt (Δ 0.00, CI [0,0]): that prompt already writes 78% of ſ as plain s. Measured price is $3.07 per 1,000 pages synchronous, about 2× the figure the $5.4K estimate used.
entries.decision: Derek (#5924): the ~$5.4K lite lane. Gothic: do not buy lite. Roman/italic: lite is a usable first draft (about 30% of pages carry at least one meaning-changing error); re-cost the lane before deciding.

entries.question: Does Greek translation leave the paid API for a CLI reader?
entries.verdict: Gemini 3.8 Flash (agy) beats the served Greek English under both judges: Gemini judge 14 of 18 pages, +1.11 fidelity points (1-5) [0.39, 1.72]; Opus judge 12 of 18 (5 old, 1 tie), +0.39 [0.00, 0.78]; both judges passed both wrong-page controls; two-judge mean +0.75. The rule passes and Greek / Ancient Greek move to the agy CLI lane (row greek-cli-gemini38). Re-reading the minor-stale pages changes the meaning on 19 of 20, but 16 of 17 change on a re-read where the OCR did not change at all: the change comes from the reader, not the OCR edit.
entries.decision: greek-cli-gemini38 row added to scripts/lib/translation-routing-table.json above flash-measured (#7075)

entries.question: Estimator v2: chained routes (draft → corrector → translator) routed on quality, cost and time
entries.verdict: Correction is now a stage of a route: pages made worse and made better per draft engine x corrector x language x page kind, from 115 committed counts in 13 experiments. With Opus as the assumed reference (Derek, 2026-10-25), no cheaper corrector yet matches Opus at P >= 0.9 in any of the 12 cells not held, so every cell routes to Opus and the free half of four Claude accounts binds: 78 weeks for lite Latin, 104-130 for Chinese and Tibetan, while agy sits idle for correction. Eleven 30-page tests (0.04 account-weeks + 307 agy calls) would decide whether agy can take part: if they confirm, lite Latin drains in 43 weeks and Tibetan in 21. Held out one experiment at a time, the correction rows land inside their 90% interval 87/99 times but re-reads 2/12. A prompt x language-family term fixes v1's #4780 miss (0/6 -> 12/12 languages covered). On #7341's extended v1, NUTS widens the accuracy intervals by 1.15x (median; not converged) and not the did-not-read ones (0.79x). With absolute floors, six v1 cells answer HOLD (Hebrew, Rashi, Chinese print, both Syriac, non-alchemical Arabic print).
entries.decision: Proposals only: allocation and proposed routing rows in scripts/eval/estimator/chain/results/ for #7170; #5924, #6560 and #6561/#6871 answered in capacity terms below (#6740)

entries.question: Does classical spelling in early Latin OCR betray a paraphrase? No
entries.verdict: The rate of classical 'ae/oe' spellings in the OCR of pre-1520 Latin does not find pages the OCR paraphrased: two of three by-eye paraphrased Bracton pages score 0, and a well-read 1498 print has pages as high as the worst.
entries.decision: No detector built. Paraphrased medieval Latin goes to the stronger-reader lane (#6056), not a model-free screen.

entries.question: Book of Wonders: does Opus correcting the stored text match a fresh Argon read?
entries.verdict: On 10 pages of the Book of Wonders manuscript (5 known-error, 5 random), Opus correcting the stored Gemini 3 Flash text made 84 spans better and 9 worse, but where it disagreed with a fresh Argon read a blind Opus judge sided with Argon 89 to 46. On the random pages most of the serious stored errors (a planetary-hours table with 10 of 12 Friday planets wrong, a copied digit row, dropped section numbers) were fixed by Opus correction; Argon's remaining wins there were mostly the scribe's spelling. On the known-error pages Argon's wins include whole words and clauses.

entries.question: Arabic manuscript OCR gate: which reader gives the Jābir books a usable page at the lowest cost?
entries.verdict: On 26 pages from 13 Arabic alchemical manuscripts (14th–20th c.), Opus 5.5 via claude -p is the only reader that gives a usable page most of the time: 22 of 26 usable under the stricter of two judges (85% [65, 100] by book), 0 failed. Flash-Lite (production prompt) reads every page but 15 of 26 are misleading (58% [35, 81]), with wrong words throughout. Gemini 3.8 Flash low on the agy CLI is cut by Gemini's safety filter mid-page on 16 of 26 (62% [35, 85]), across 9 of the 13 books; 8 of its 10 finished reads are usable. On the Kraus 1935 print edition (4 pages, 1 book), all three readers are usable on every page.
entries.decision: Route the 13 Jābir manuscripts (2,252 pages) to Opus 5.5 via claude -p, one read per page. Estimated cost: 6–31 weekly points of one Claude account, about 6 h of wall time at 2 calls in parallel, with a by-eye sample of BnF Arabe 4709 (its hand is where every reader failed most). Do not send them to Flash-Lite (58% misleading) or to agy Gemini (62% filter-cut on alchemical content). Route Kraus 1935 (582 pages) to agy Gemini 3.8 Flash low, falling back to production Flash-Lite on a filter cut. The cut is detectable by its message, it has not hit Kraus yet, and both readers are usable there. Releasing the hold is Derek's call.

entries.question: Which stored pages would the write-time truncation + tag-balance guard refuse, and is it right about them?
entries.verdict: The write guard (scripts/lib/write-text-guard.mjs) refuses 2 of 5,000 stored OCR pages and 2 of 2,018 stored translations as truncated; all 4 are real truncations, read from the text. Of the 20 hand-read #5055 truncation flags, it fires on 2: 1 real, 1 unclear, 0 false. Seven of the 10 'real' ones are not short at all once their notes are counted: their body sits inside <note>/<margin> (hidden text), which is a different defect from truncation.
entries.decision: Wired into every OCR and translation writer (PR for #5055): a cut read is refused, re-read once, then recorded

entries.question: Does guard v3 fix the wrong dates on a FRESH draw?
entries.verdict: Guard v3 on a fresh 100-book draw: date precision 94.5% (52/55, 95% CI lower bound 85.1), against 91.8% (56/61) for guard v2 on the same replies. Title precision 95.8% (68/71), against 86.2% (69/80). The 95% gate is still not met for dates. The day-and-month rule removed 2 wrong dates and 4 right ones (disputation dates, which are the edition date when no imprint year is printed). The series-label rule removed 8 wrong titles and 1 right one.
entries.decision: Keep guard v3 for the proposal queue. No imprint writes without a by-eye check. Whether the ~$85 full read runs at all is a spend decision above the $10 floor and stays Derek's.

entries.question: Stopping new seams at write time: the guard on Sonnet, majors with bigger edits, drift-only skip
entries.verdict: The write-time seam guard finds 23% of new joins defective on replay and 39–52% on the two lanes that wrote during the 48 h window. Its accepted Sonnet repairs on Gemini-translated joins are preferred by the blind Opus judge in both orders 68/75 in replay (0 worse) and 56/60 live (2 worse); majors 28/28, 0 worse. On joins with an Opus-translated page it is preferred only 7/16, so the guard no longer touches them. The apply bar (≥ 90% and 0 worse) is not met: the lanes stay SEAM_GUARD dry. A wider placement bound for majors (lean.mjs --majors-wide) placed 56 of 110 refused majors, 55 preferred, 0 worse. Drift-only joins are now skipped.
entries.decision: Guard on in every lane as dry (box file /etc/sourcelibrary/seam-guard); not apply. SEAM_GUARD_APPLY=major is built for a majors-only switch. --majors-wide shipped off by default, recommended on in the cron. Drift-only skip merged (#7118)

entries.question: Can an open engine on the GEX45 read the hidden Sanskrit backlog as well as agy Flash?
entries.verdict: On printed Devanagari, Surya 2 on the GEX45 is within agy Flash's error under the preregistered gate. Median CER: Surya 1.9%, Flash 1.6% (paired Δ +0.2 points, CI −0.15 to +0.85, n = 30 books). Surya had 0 unread or catastrophic pages; Flash had 3, two of them Gemini filter blocks. On pages at severity ≥ 2 or unread, Surya was 47% and Flash 67%. On manuscripts no open engine passes: Surya 27.6% vs Flash 18.2%, n = 10. Chandra 2, dots.ocr, Qwen3-VL-8B, PP-OCRv5 and PaddleOCR-VL all fail both cells. A third of the backlog's pages are Śāradā, which no tested Devanagari engine covers.
entries.decision: Recommended: a decision-grade confirmation of Surya 2 on ≥ 50 more print books, then route printed Devanagari (~109K backlog pages) to Surya on the GEX45. Manuscripts and Śāradā stay on agy Flash. Derek decides (#7243).

entries.question: Can Opus (subscription claude -p) translate the untranslated Tibetan and Sanskrit pages, gated by a blind image-grounded audit?
entries.verdict: Gate failed, nothing written. A blind image-grounded Opus audit (15/15 controls caught) rates 35% of Tibetan and 38% of Sanskrit Opus pages bad, against a 5% bar. Most Tibetan bad pages come from the Yigdzin transcription (seam lines invented or duplicated, truncated lines: 18 of 28); 10 have a translator-side error, 5 of them a meaning reversal or mistranslation.
entries.decision: No write; the Opus lane over the 78.7K-page Yigdzin frame waits on an OCR fix at the leaf seams (#5320/#5771) or an image-grounded translation lane (#6948)

entries.question: OCR estimator v1: which route gives each kind of page a usable reading at the lowest cost?
entries.verdict: A hurdle term for 100%-error reads cuts the OCR estimator's in-sample level bias from 0.063 to 0.007 CER (same rows, same inference). The did-not-read model reproduces the #4763 gate (agy 3.8 Flash 31/122, fitted 0.24; S4 14/34, fitted 0.39; lite S4 7/34, fitted 0.18), but held out it predicts 8/122 where 31 were observed: refusals on a new kind of page cannot be read off the other charts. On English 1880–1930 prose the Archive's text clears the bar at $0. On 1880–1930 number-dense pages no measured route clears both bars.
entries.decision: Route proposals in results/ocr-v1-routes.{json,md} for #7170 to consume; nothing routes from them until a held-out check passes for the cell (#6740)

entries.question: Notes as their own layer, tried two ways: parse today's markup into anchored annotations, and ask the translator for text + annotations directly
entries.verdict: Notes can be a separate, anchored layer. A tolerant parser splits 3,000 stored pages into text + annotations byte-exactly, and its anchors re-find their words in the page's next stored version with 0 misplaced after a by-eye read. Asked to return text + annotations as JSON, Opus is not less faithful than today's inline prompt (S−T +0.13 [−0.05, +0.30], 40 pages); 40 of 40 replies were valid JSON and 367 of 367 anchors resolved. It costs 2.6× the output tokens.
entries.decision: Preregistered rule met: adopt S for new translations on the Opus CLI lane once the notes-layer storage (step 2) exists; not yet for Gemini lanes (not measured). Default prompt unchanged (#5942)

entries.question: Can gemini-3.1-flash-lite, given a GPU engine's draft and the page image, correct the draft?
entries.verdict: gemini-3.1-flash-lite is not a correction route in either language tested. On Paddle's Chinese drafts it makes pages worse with both prompts. On 40 table pages, median CER goes from 6.4% to 50% with the set's prompt (32 worse, 2 better) and to 15% with the production-shaped prompt (28 worse). It rewrites pages as markdown tables, which drops, duplicates and reorders columns. On Yigdzin's Tibetan drafts it gains as much identity to Derge as Pro or Flash low (+0.020 [0.012, 0.027]). But it gains the same with no image at all (+0.019), and with each prompt one folio in 30 gets whole lines invented or duplicated (by eye). The no-image result and that invented text show its gain is recall of the canonical text, not reading.
entries.decision: No lite corrector cell for Paddle Chinese or Yigdzin Tibetan; routing unchanged (#7263)

entries.question: Opus correction of the lite text vs the Flash re-read, on the same 250 lite-read Latin pages
entries.verdict: We had Opus correct the stored lite transcription in place (correct.mjs, #6694 arm B) on the same 250 lite-read Latin pages as the Flash re-read test. Blind Opus readers called 31/250 corrected pages misleading, against 111/250 for lite. 25 of those 31 are the wrong-leaf book, and the corrector put all 25 of its pages in CONTAIN, so the page served is still the lite text. On the other 9 books the counts are 6/225 corrected vs 86/225 lite. One page was worse than lite: lib. 2 → lib. 1, the same misread the Flash re-read made on that page, confirmed by eye. Flash had 7 worse pages. Head to head with the Flash re-read, the readers preferred the correction on 131 pages and Flash on 43, with 76 ties. Misleading counts were 5 for the correction and 28 for Flash on the 225 pages outside the wrong-leaf book. There were no line drops, no refusals and no false contains. Every judge was an Opus reader, from the same family as the corrector, so self-preference is not ruled out.
entries.decision: No production write. The strict bar ('no page worse') fails on 1 page, so as registered no plan is adopted. Correction beats the Flash re-read on every measure here. If Derek accepts it as the upgrade path for lite Latin, it costs about 1% of one Claude account-week per 250 pages, so about 18 account-weeks for the 444K lite pages (meter granularity puts it between 9 and 27). That is Claude subscription time, not agy, and it adds the same ~$450 of gap-fill retranslation as any OCR write.

entries.question: Flash-low correction of the lite text: the fourth arm, and the second-family check on Opus correction
entries.verdict: We had agy Gemini 3.8 Flash (low) correct the stored lite transcription, one page per call, on the same 250 lite-read Latin pages as the Flash re-read and Opus correction arms. Blind Opus readers called 30/250 Flash-corrected pages misleading, against 100 for lite. That is as low as Opus correction's 31 and passes the halving bar. But 11 pages came out worse than lite, against 1 for Opus correction and 7 for the Flash re-read. Head to head, the readers preferred the Opus correction on 163 pages and the Flash correction on 37, with 50 ties. The Flash correction lost meaning that Opus kept on 48 pages, and Opus lost meaning that Flash kept on 13. Placed next to the Opus text, the Flash correction was called misleading on 65 pages (48 outside the wrong-leaf book), against 30 for Opus. Its typical defects were the long s read as f, wrong expansions of abbreviations, ℞ given as ♃, and lost negations. A second-family judge, agy Flash-low, ruled out self-preference behind #7258's result: on 59 seeded pairs it preferred Opus correction over lite 56–3, where the Opus readers had 58–0.
entries.decision: No production write. Flash-low correction does not stand in for Opus correction: it fails bar (b) on 11 pages and bar (c) at 37–163. It costs about $0.61 per 1K pages at the agy plan fee (1.02 calls a page), against roughly 1% of a Claude account-week per 250 pages for Opus correction. On the 444K lite pages that would use the whole agy week for about 6 weeks. Opus correction stays the recommended upgrade path; the second-family judge removes the main caveat on it. The Flash correction is a cheaper fallback that removes most misleading lite pages but introduces its own; it is not recommended as served text without a guard for ſ/f and negations.

entries.question: Is the new output better than the stock, and can the spot-check rates be trusted?
entries.verdict: Last week's new output carries a serious error on 1 of 30 pages (3%, CI 0–10) against 27–30% in the library's stock; a second Opus reader confirmed 35 of 35 serious calls from rounds 3–4 as real and serious, reclassifying 6 (mostly 'invented' to misread or omitted).

entries.question: Continuation probe: do the models know the texts Gemini refuses as recitation? No
entries.verdict: A RECITATION refusal does not mean the models know the page: neither Opus nor Gemini 3.8 Flash can continue any of 20 lite-refused pages (longest shared run ≤ 14 words), while Opus continues 4 of 20 matched never-refused pages near-verbatim. The probe passed both control gates.
entries.decision: Do not use Gemini RECITATION refusals as a per-book 'the models already know this text' score; read them as 'a long copy is in Google's citation index' only (#7271, #6740)

entries.question: Classical Chinese: does a cheap-model cascade (DeepSeek/Qwen + mechanical gates → Flash) match Flash at lower cost?
entries.verdict: The cheap cascade fails all three preregistered conditions: cascade − Flash −0.31 [−0.48, −0.17] fidelity, 12.5 vs 4.7 reversals per 100 pages, $0.00131 a page against a $0.00107 limit, with 53 % of pages routed. No cheaper arm matches Flash. DeepSeek scores 3.11, Qwen 2.95, Lite 3.56, Flash (3.8, via agy) 4.29.
entries.decision: Proposed: translate the 890K Siku pages with gemini-3.8-flash-low through agy ($0, CLI quota-bound); if bought, Flash Batch ≈ $1,600–1,700. No cheap-model cascade, no Lite.

entries.question: Is the fresh read stable, does another model do better, is the good result memory, and do the reads make sense?
entries.verdict: Reading the same Whish 147 leaf three times gives very different results, for Opus and Fable alike: on most verse leaves at least one read is close to the published text (best of three: CER 0.18 Opus, 0.17 Fable) and another is near chance (worst of three: 0.44, 0.49). Sonnet, with a row-count scaffold that held, stays near chance (0.60). Painting over the middle third of a leaf shows no recitation: Opus and Sonnet mark the hidden rows illegible, and Opus's accuracy on the visible rows holds on 3 of 4 leaves. Agreement between reads predicts accuracy only where it is high and rare, and picking the most central read selects the poor mode.
entries.decision: Not adopted yet. The useful signal is the good read among several, not the majority read: a blind Opus judge rated the good reads as sensible Sanskrit and the poor ones as gibberish, so best-of-N with a sensibility pick is the next test (#7119). On commentary leaves the reads stay near 0.45–0.69, and at least one commentary leaf (20-b) has Malayalam in it, so its score against a Sanskrit edition is not meaningful.

entries.question: Do altered images help a single read, and do reads of different images merge better than repeat reads?
entries.verdict: On 9 verse leaves of Whish 147, no preprocessing beats the plain colour crop for Opus 5.5. With one read per variant, pooled per-row CER is: best single channel 0.32, string holes masked 0.37, per-row crops 0.41, CLAHE grey 0.48, Sauvola binarised 0.59. The plain-crop baseline is 0.34, and a variant had to score under 0.23 to count as better. Reads of perturbed images (shifted, rescaled, gamma) do not err more independently than repeat reads of one crop. Merged akshara by akshara, 5 perturbed reads give 0.29 with the best channel as fifth member and 0.38 without it. Perturbed reads land in the good mode less often than plain ones (17 of 45 against 13 of 27).
entries.decision: Not adopted. The rollout (#7119) keeps the plain colour column crops and the J-text pick over 4 candidates (0.17 pooled, best-of-3 job). Replacing a plain re-read with a perturbed or preprocessed one would lower the share of good candidates. Letter-level voting loses to picking a whole read. Agreement of 4 or 5 of 5 perturbed reads marks text at CER 0.13 (a third of the text), but 3 of 3 same-crop reads already give 0.13 (30%), so it adds no new confidence signal.

entries.question: Can a Kraken model trained on our own edition-aligned lines read Whish MS 147?
entries.verdict: A Kraken line model trained on 881 edition-anchored lines of hand A reads the 9 held-out verse leaves at CER 0.236 (floor 0.748; per leaf 0.15–0.33, no bimodality). That beats Opus pooled (0.34) but not Opus best of 3 (leaf mean 0.18). As a voter it picks Opus's best draw on 8 of 9 leaves (leaf mean 0.178, the oracle's). It does not transfer to the dense hand B (0.62–0.65, floor ~0.72). Learning curve: 100 lines 0.671 (chance), 300 lines 0.315, 881 lines 0.236.
entries.decision: No page writes. Proposed use: a per-leaf selector and gate over Opus/Fable draws, and a placer for hand-A-like leaves in the unplaced stretch (9 of 91 placed in the Tattvakaumudī print, in scan order). Not wired into the book.

entries.question: Can a judge pick the good read among several?
entries.verdict: On 9 verse leaves of Whish 147, a blind Opus judge that sees only the candidate texts (no image, no edition) picks a read as good as the oracle best: CER 0.20 from 3 Opus reads (oracle 0.22) and 0.17 from 3 Opus + 1 Fable (oracle 0.18), against 0.34 for one read. A judge that also sees the leaf does worse (0.25). On the 206 edition-anchored leaves of the rollout the pick helps the kārikā leaves (0.42 → 0.31) but barely moves the commentaries (about 0.54 → 0.52).
entries.decision: Every written leaf page of Whish 147 now carries the J-text pick of 3 Opus reads (4 with a Fable read on 9 leaves); on fresh-read pages it is the OCR, on edition-anchored pages it is the <note> (PR for #7119).

entries.question: Can flash-lite read a book's imprint off its opening leaves well enough to catalogue it?
entries.verdict: flash-lite reading the imprint off the opening leaves FAILS the 95% gate. Date precision is 85.8% (91/106, 95% CI lower bound 78.0) and author precision is 79.4% (123/155; 28 of the 32 misses are role errors, and only 4 names are not on the page). Where the date would CHANGE the catalogue, it was right 9 times in 15.
entries.decision: No full run that writes imprint fields. A full read (~$85 at Batch rates, not ~$600) is only worth running as a review queue: the ~8% of books whose read date differs from the catalogue, each checked by eye before setCatalogueFields(). Guard v3 (reject bracketed, handwritten and day-and-month dates; flag show-through leaves) needs a FRESH draw before any claim.

entries.question: Could a Qwen model on our own GPU translate the Chinese/Japanese print pages instead of Gemini Flash?
entries.verdict: A local Qwen on the GEX45 does not translate Chinese/Japanese print as well as the stored gemini-3-flash: in the gated 10-page pilot Qwen3.6-27B (4-bit) made 3.9 accuracy errors per page against Flash's 1.6 (paired Δ +2.3 [1.0, 3.9]) and was preferred on 25 % of pages, so the preregistered STOP rule fired. Qwen3-14B also fails the judge-free bar (6/57 pages capped, errored or untranslated), and Qwen3-32B-AWQ does not serve on the 24 GB card.
entries.decision: Chinese/Japanese print translation stays on Gemini (Flash via agy/Batch); no Qwen translation lane (#6101)

entries.question: Does Opus translate Pali better than 3 Flash, before the Pali row moves to the CLI lane?
entries.verdict: Opus beats the stored 3 Flash English on Pali under both judges: Opus judge 15 of 16 pages, +1.06 fidelity points (1-5) [0.56, 1.56]; Gemini 3.8 Flash high judge 13 of 16, +1.13 [0.38, 1.81]; both judges passed both wrong-page controls; by eye 3 of 3 Opus reads faithful. The rule passes and Pali moves to the Opus CLI lane (row pali-cli-opus).
entries.decision: pali-cli-opus row added to scripts/lib/translation-routing-table.json (#7075)

entries.question: Can the long-s pass be written to stored OCR, flash pages included, with no meaning changes and no stale translations?
entries.verdict: Applying the #7174 long-s pass to stored Latin OCR needed a stricter rule than the measured pass: on flash pages, by eye, the raw pass made 8 meaning changes in 756 edits (fit → ſit, fi. for figura). After three rounds tightening the rule (act only where the f-spelling is not a word), round 4 was 787/787 right with 0 meaning changes. Written through an orthographic-only path that leaves ocr.updated_at alone; the canary changed 0 stale flags.
entries.decision: Long s restored in stored lite and flash Latin OCR, ≥ 1501, by scripts/maintenance/longs-pass-5924.mjs with the final rule (PR on #5924)

entries.question: Does the English/OCR character ratio predict a serious error?
entries.verdict: The English-to-OCR length ratio is a weak screen for translation failures on alphabetic pages (AUC 0.68) and none for OCR errors (0.48) or CJK pages (0.41); it cannot see the errors that matter most, which begin in the OCR.

entries.question: Can an open engine on the GEX45 replace flash-lite for 1500s and 1600s Latin print?
entries.verdict: No open engine is ADOPTABLE for Latin print in either century under the brief's bar (median CER within 0.2 pt of flash-lite, no more catastrophic pages). GLM-OCR and olmOCR-2 have lower medians than raw lite, but they loop on 1–4 pages where lite has none. Against lite + the long-s pass (0.66% / 1.49%), every engine is 1.6–9 points behind. A second temperature-0 read gives the same verdict for every engine.
entries.decision: No GPU lane for Latin print. Latin stays on flash-lite + the long-s pass (job longs-apply-5924). No production lane changed; adopting one is Derek's call (#6871 row 2)

entries.question: Books catalogued Latin whose pages are another language, text-only
entries.verdict: Function-word share on stored OCR, gated on agreement with the OCR <language> tags, relabels books catalogued Latin right on 20 of 20 by eye; 254 written (110 flips, 144 mixed).
entries.decision: 254 books relabelled in production (sweep relabel-latin-5924, undoable); 709 review rows and 48 manuscript-filed-as-print rows reported, not written

entries.question: Image gain, amendment 6871a: phrase plants, SKQS, span recall at precision 0.5
entries.verdict: Preregistered amendment 6871a (phrase plants, a Chinese SKQS cell, span recall at precision ≥ 0.5): no real-error cell clears any of the three bars. On the full #6420 set image gain has R@P50 0.00 (CI 0.00–0.00): at no threshold are half the flagged words wrong. SKQS real errors: gain AUROC 0.53, R@P50 0.03. Planted phrases from another page of the same book are found (AUROC 0.94, R@P50 0.98). The detector sees text swapped in from elsewhere. It does not see the wrong words a reader meets.
entries.decision: No image-gain pre-screen in front of agy/Opus review on #6420 (confirms 2026-10-22-image-gain-full-run-6871.md). Row A of #6871 is closed.

entries.question: How often does the OCR drop the 丨 headword mark in Chinese reference works?
entries.verdict: PaddleOCR-VL drops the 丨 headword mark on about 46% of 佩文韻府 pages (≥100 Han), against 13% of Opus-read pages; the per-page rate is bimodal, so a zero page in a high-median book is a free flag.

entries.question: Burst 2 scored: the Greek-manuscript LoRA invents fluent Greek and is not a lane
entries.verdict: FAIL by the preregistered rule: GLM-OCR + LoRA trained on 619 Grec 1839 pages does not read other Greek manuscripts. On T2 its median page CER is 100 % (189/199 pages catastrophic) against 28.6 % for the served text and 35.7 % for flash-lite, and it loses every page to the served text. Its Greek is fluent invention in Proclus' vocabulary, often looping to the token cap. Not a lane.

entries.question: Does a Flash re-read halve the misleading pages of lite-read Latin books?
entries.verdict: A Flash 3.8 re-read (agy) of 250 spread body pages from 10 fresh lite-read Latin books cut the pages a blind Opus reader called misleading from 102 to 20 (41% → 8%). Readers preferred Flash on 201 pages, lite on 23, with 26 ties. The preregistered bar FAILS on its second half: 7 pages are worse. 3 of those are Flash reads cut off by Gemini's recitation filter, which the existing cli-ocr guards already refuse to write. 4 are genuine Flash misreads: a dropped printed line, 4 dropped lines, intelligentem → intelligibilem, lib. 2 → lib. 1. Against them, lite is misleading where Flash is not on 89 pages. All 10 books fail the 25-page check, and one book (69bd9d05…) serves the next leaf's text on every page; it was contained.
entries.decision: No production write. As registered the test fails, so no plan is adopted. Whether a net bar (4 worse vs 89 better, guarded) should replace 'no page worse' is Derek's call. The price if it does: the 25-page check flags every lite-read book in the frame, so the rule reduces to re-reading all 992 books (444K lite pages). That is about 467K agy calls, about 85 days of the account's whole Flash quota, plus about $450 of lite Batch retranslation from gap-fill.

entries.question: Does reading Whish 147 one text row at a time beat the half-leaf read?
entries.verdict: Reading Whish 147 one row at a time does not help: scored row by row against GRETIL, single-row strips give CER 0.60 (Fable 5.1) and 0.65 (Opus 5.5), against 0.51 and 0.54 for the half-leaf reads of the same 9 leaves (noise floor 0.70). Re-scored the same way, the half-leaf reads are clearly above chance but differ from the published text in about half of all characters. A single earlier Fable read at CER 0.09 did not repeat: a fresh read of the same crop scored 0.52.
entries.decision: Line strips are not adopted; the best-attempt job (#7119) keeps half-leaf crops. Its free-read warning was rewritten to the per-row figure (about half of all characters differ, 7 leaves), replacing both the old 'at chance' sentence and an interim '9 in 100' figure.

entries.question: How far does locate-then-collate reach across a whole palm-leaf manuscript?
entries.verdict: Leaf-by-leaf locate + collation with Opus placed 209 of the 304 non-blank leaves on pp. 4–159 of Whish MS 147 in a published text, in unbroken sequence through the Sāṅkhyakārikā, Jayamaṅgalā, Dīpikā and Tarkasaṃgraha. It placed none of the 91 leaves of pp. 66–111 (a denser 11–12-row hand), at half- or quarter-leaf resolution; Fable free reads of those found connected words on 27 of their 182 half-leaves.
entries.decision: The 159 pages were written with per-page warnings (#7119). For dense-hand palm leaf, locating needs something other than a whole-leaf view; the planted-error rate still covers only the verses.

entries.question: Claude tiers for seam repair: Haiku screen, Sonnet repair, Opus verify
entries.verdict: Haiku cannot screen page joins for the Claude seam lane: its best recall on Opus's 47 major defects is 68% (32/47, passing 42% of joins), 91% only at p≥1, which passes 86%, and the screen then costs more than sending every join to Sonnet. Not installed. Sonnet as the repairer: 98.8% of placed repairs preferred by the blind Opus judge, 0 worse, but verified yield 27.3% against Opus's 36.3% and Gemini's 36.7%. The whole Sonnet lane (repair + 7% Opus sample) measured 4 weekly points per 1,000 joins. On 1,000 nightly joins the placement checks refused 120 of the 183 majors Sonnet found.
entries.decision: Haiku screen not installed; the Claude lane for Gemini-locked nights stays #7120 Sonnet fallback, unscreened (#7118)

entries.question: Screening the OCR queue for copies we already hold, by page images
entries.verdict: First full pre-OCR duplicate screen: 167 queued copies of a printing we already read (or are reading) held, 47,696 unread pages; 23 holds checked by eye, 2 wrong (both reissues with a different imprint year, now excluded). Two instrument faults found and fixed: provider watermarks and reissued sheets.
entries.decision: Hold same-printing unread copies before paid OCR (reason same-edition-copy-unread); never across differing imprint years.

entries.question: Does PaddleOCR-VL read woodblock print as well as Gemini once its page-level failures are removed?
entries.verdict: PaddleOCR-VL 1.6 on split leaves (NDL label strip cropped, right leaf then left, layout off) passes the preregistered bar for Chinese/Japanese print: median Han CER 0.061 vs Flash-Lite 0.067 (paired Δ −0.014 [−0.020, −0.003]), catastrophic 3/198 = lite's 3; still behind Flash (Δ +0.006 [+0.002, +0.010]). All 3 failures are blank leaves (2 loops, 1 invented from show-through).

entries.question: Is NDLOCR (modern print) worth a scored prereg as a second lane for Meiji typeset Japanese?
entries.verdict: On 20 frozen Meiji typeset pages, NDLOCR-Lite and stored flash-lite agree at median bigram Dice 0.88. None of the three preregistered triggers fired (Dice < 0.6 on 2/20, needs 5; lite loop/textless 0, needs 2; N right over a 10+ char span 1/5 by eye, needs 2), so no scored prereg for a second NDL modern-print lane.
entries.decision: Per the prereg: lite stays the Meiji typeset reader; no NDL modern-print lane is pursued (#5100)

entries.question: Is the NDL full run's text the page? A by-eye check of 10 written pages
entries.verdict: The 2026-10-01 NDL古典籍OCR v3 full run (96 books, 6,148 pages written) gives the right text of the page on 10/10 pages read against the image, 0 invented. Errors are kanji substitutions (0–7 a page), lines read off seals or the neighbouring leaf, and furigana promoted to a line.
entries.decision: The NDL readings stay. The 116 books stay HELD (ndl-koten-lane-4925) until re-translation of the stale pages is approved as a separate priced go; this check clears the 'by-eye check before any hold is released' step from #4925

entries.question: What do readers see on Latin print pages, and can we remove facing-page bleed cheaply?
entries.verdict: By eye, 5 of 36 served Latin pages (14%, Wilson 6–29%) would mislead a reader. The cause is OCR on all 5: an abbreviation expanded wrongly, a passage omitted, a misread variant, facing-leaf fragments served as a side-note. On 2 of them the translation then made the error worse. Facing-page bleed reached the text on 1 of the 36 pages, although a strip of the facing leaf was visible on 18. Flash left the strip out on all 11 of its pages that showed one, and lite read it into the text on 1 of 7. On the 99 references, bleed is in 12 of lite's reads. Neither preregistered fix passes. (a) The text-only deletion fixes 4 of 12 pages and harms 1 by eye. (b) Cropping to the leaf and re-reading fixes 11 of 12 but crops 25 clean pages and harms 4 of them, plus 2 of the fixed ones.
entries.decision: Apply neither fix as built. The next test is a gated re-read: crop only when the edge detector fires AND lite's read shows a bleed shape (a column-break tail, or ≥ 3 margin tags), with the cut kept ≥ 2% clear of the text block. Post hoc, gating alone gives 8/12 fixed with 1/87 clean pages worse. Re-reading those pages with a stronger engine on the uncropped image is the alternative to test against it (stored 3.8-flash reads: 11/12 S pages better, no crop). Either one has to pass a fresh prereg on new pages.

entries.question: Can we fix the Latin OCR we already have, programmatically? Do 25 pages decide the book?
entries.verdict: From stored text alone, two defect classes can be found and fixed: long s read as f (8.9% of pages; 14.1% on flash-lite books, 4.1% on flash-preview) and facing-page strips filed as side-notes (2.0% flagged, 8 of 14 confirmed by eye, and a floor). Truncation, column read-across and empty-page detectors all failed the by-eye check (0/4, 0/4, 1/4). The re-read class (wrong leaf, omitted passages, a lost column) cannot be seen in the text at all. 25 pages spread through the book predict the whole book (Spearman ρ 0.76–0.82); the first 25 pages do not (ρ 0.25–0.30), because only 55% of them are text.
entries.decision: Decide per book from 25 pages spread evenly through the body, never the first 25. A text-only repair applies in place for long s (lite-read books) and for margin strips. It is not applied here, because an OCR write triggers gap-fill retranslation. Re-reading a whole book needs an image check on the 25 spread pages, since no text signal sees it. The GPU arm (does 25 pages predict 'can go to GPU OCR'?) is queued as a follow-up (#5924).

entries.question: Can a CPU pass over flash-lite's text put back the long s well enough to read Latin print like Gemini 3.8 Flash?
entries.verdict: A text-only long-s pass on flash-lite's Latin (CPU, 8 ms/page, no model calls) passes the preregistered bar in both centuries: view-N median CER 4.2% → 0.66% (1600s) and 5.6% → 1.49% (1500s), within 0.1–0.13 points of Gemini 3.8 Flash (0.56 / 1.36). ſ written as f falls from 4,851 to 84. It over-corrects 37 true f (names like Offa, fine/sine), and Flash still wins more pages head to head (19/34, 12/26).
entries.decision: Derek: (1) apply the pass to the 1.07M Latin pages stored as lite (writes to pages: separate PR); (2) read the unread Latin print backlog as lite Batch + pass (1500s+1600s 7.6M pages ≈ $5.4K). Both DECISION on #5924

entries.question: Do 25 spread pages predict whether a Latin book can go to GPU OCR?
entries.verdict: Under the preregistered bar (median disagreement with stored OCR ≤ 2 points, no catastrophic page), no whole book is GPU-OK. The 25-spread verdict therefore matches the whole-book verdict on 20 of 20 books, but every match is a fail, which says nothing. Read as numbers, the 25 spread pages predict the book: Spearman ρ 0.89 for median disagreement, a median gap of 0.8 points, ρ 0.75 for the catastrophic share. The first 25 pages predict it less well: ρ 0.46, a gap of 4.0 points. Post hoc, at a bar some books pass (median ≤ 5 points, catastrophic pages ≤ 4%), the spread verdict matches on 20/20 (3 OK, 17 fail) and the first 25 on 17/20. Gothic, two-column and side-note books disagree 3–4× more than plain roman, and one Greek book plus one two-column book loop on 55–74% of their pages. By eye, the stored text is right on 3 of 6 disagreement pages and GLM on 3. Two of GLM's three wins are pages where the stored text is another leaf's.
entries.decision: Decide GPU eligibility from 25 pages spread through the book, never the first 25. Measured against stored Gemini text, stock GLM-OCR 0.9B does not reach a 2-point bar on any whole Latin book here: no Latin GPU lane on this evidence. The distilled adapter agrees more with the stored text (it was trained on it) but loops more. Two wrong-leaf stored pages were found by eye and reported on #5924, not contained (this job was read-only).

entries.question: Image gain as a guessed-text detector: the full preregistered run
entries.verdict: Full preregistered run, all 2,178 Opus-adjudicated stored reads: image gain (log p | image − log p | no image, Qwen2.5-VL-7B AWQ) ranks the words Opus marked wrong at unit AUROC 0.58 (95% CI 0.56–0.60) against a bar of 0.75. No language clears it; Chinese is below chance (0.44), where text-only perplexity scores 0.68. Gain does not beat perplexity pooled (paired CI −0.02 to +0.06). At a 10% flag rate precision is 2.6% on a 1.4% base rate. It does see text that is not on the leaf: 41 planted controls 0.95, invented spans 0.82. The repeat pass is deterministic (r 0.9999), so this is not noise.
entries.decision: No image-gain pre-screen in front of agy/Opus review on #6420: it neither replaces nor pre-filters a round, in any language. The amendment cells (phrase plants, SKQS, span recall at precision 0.5) score themselves in gex45 task 55-grounding-6871a and post to #6871; the real-error cells cannot change this verdict unless they clear all three bars

entries.question: How many live books hold a scan of a different book than their record says?
entries.verdict: 8 of 13 suspects are real record/scan mismatches (6 hold a wholly different book); extrapolated about 14 (95% 6–27) across the 42,291 live books with OCR, a FLOOR since recall is not measured.
entries.decision: scan-title-mismatch.mjs repaired (PR for #7146); the 8 records are listed, not fixed

entries.question: Is "harmony = diversity in wholeness" (harmony-kb ideas/01) earned across the definitions our books give, and how did five resonance/sympathy topoi travel?
entries.verdict: Diversity-in-a-whole is a real but minority strand of harmony definitions: 15% of 3,933 definitional sentences (ratio/consonance 32%), flat from the 9th to the 20th century, and half the time it sits inside a ratio definition (Boethius' plurimorum adunatio et dissentientium consensio). The five resonance topoi each have a traceable chain, with older witnesses than the issue named for the wolf drum (Bodleian MS. Barocci 50) and a Chinese strings chain that names number, not spirits, as the cause.

entries.question: Burst 2: can a reader trained on one Greek manuscript read others?
entries.verdict: Preregistration only, no result: training burst 2 trains GLM-OCR + LoRA on 619 Grec 1839 pages labelled from the Schneider edition fit, and is decided on 307 pages of two alchemical codices from other libraries (Marcianus gr. 299, Ars sacra) against served text and flash-lite. Queued on gex45.

entries.question: Does retrieval by meaning find pages about harmony that never use the word?
entries.verdict: 48 probe sentences for eight kinds of harmony retrieved 19,487 translated pages; 58% of the 28,287 matches name neither harmony, sympathy, concord nor consonance (ratio 37%, balance 74%).
entries.decision: Semantic map and theme river views on /explore/maps/harmony (#7129)

entries.question: Can a prompt make flash-lite read long s on Latin print?
entries.verdict: No prompt arm passes the preregistered bar. The live prompt already writes long s as f far less often than the generic prompt PR #6912 measured (413 vs 2,566 in the 1600s). LONG_S_LINE cuts the median CER by only 0.08 points, with a CI ending at 0. Thinking makes it worse. Prompt + the sibling CPU pass clears the bar in both centuries (secondary); the pass alone clears it in the 1600s.
entries.decision: Recommended: the CPU pass (longs-pass-5924) first, since it fixes stored text with no re-OCR. Leave the default prompt unchanged. Revisit LONG_S_LINE in the default prompt for pre-1800 Latin only together with the pass, as a separate PR and decision.

entries.question: Can Opus or Fable read a Malayalam-script Sanskrit palm-leaf manuscript well enough to OCR it?
entries.verdict: Neither Opus 5.5 nor Fable 5.1 (claude -p, subscription) can read Sanskrit in Malayalam script on palm leaf. Both decline the whole page without inventing text. On crops, Opus scores CER 0.71–0.75 against the GRETIL Sāṃkhyakārikā, at chance (0.74–0.78); Fable is at chance on quarter-leaf crops and 0.64–0.71 on half-leaf crops, slightly above chance and far from usable.
entries.decision: Collation against the edition is the only arm with signal. On 36 planted errors over 9 leaves, Opus caught 69% and Fable 61%, and none of their certain substantive flags was false; about a third went unflagged, 5–6 by copy-through. Usable as a variant finder (trust certain flags only), not as a transcription. Book stays held (malayalam-palm-leaf-lane). No Opus lane for Malayalam palm leaf. Gemini CLI arm pending its quota reset (~2026-10-23).

entries.question: Which Philolaus and Archytas attributions in Source Library have an ancient source behind them?
entries.verdict: No new Philolaus or Archytas fragment. Two known witnesses confirmed (Barocci 41 = Wallis's Porphyry codex D; Boethius' Philolaus sentence identical in the 9th-, 12th- and 13th-c. copies). The residue is late misattribution, led by a quartan-fever amulet credited to 'Architas' in ps.-Albertus and copied by Agrippa, and one mistranslation (Cessolis' Agathocles rendered as Archytas).

entries.question: Can page images tell two copies of one printing from two editions, before anything is read?
entries.verdict: Keypoint matching on page images separates same printing (median inliers 56-1,400) from different edition, printing or volume (6-16) on 25 control pairs, with no OCR; whole-page dHash does not (both ~30 of 256 bits).

entries.question: Can Yigdzin read the 5,132 Tibetan pages its leaf worker refused as "guttered"?
entries.verdict: Round 1 (every read scored): page-mode Yigdzin recall 0.979 but 1 of 30 pages loops and invents a line — fails. Round 2 (fresh 30, #4523 write rule preregistered): 15 of 29 text pages written, 0 invented, line recall 1.00, 15/15 clean — passes; the guard withheld both looping pages.
entries.decision: Read all 5,132 pages to FILES with HF Yigdzin page-mode (gex45 queue 80-tib-gutter-full-a, ~9 GPU-days in 24 h chunks); applying them under the #4523 write rule is a DECISION for Derek (#6871 row 4)

entries.question: An offline fixer that reads the finished answer and the whole pages
entries.verdict: Registered gate not met: G4 adjacent 72.5% (8 of 40 plants sat on caption lines the rule leaves alone). Amendment 1 (a caption whose image URL names another page goes through the fixer), tested on a fresh planted draw: gate met. Sonnet with span-checked moves cuts wrong-page links 410 → 182 (−56%); 4 of 2,294 links made wrong by a move; 30 of 1,781 correct links dropped.
entries.decision: Dry-run worker on l7a writes proposed edits to librarian_citation_fixes only (scripts/workers/librarian-citation-fixer.ts); nothing applies them to embassy_messages. Applying them is a separate decision (#6946).

entries.question: Can a distilled GLM-OCR read Latin print well enough to replace flash-lite?
entries.verdict: GLM-OCR + a LoRA on 1,982 stored flash-preview reads: median CER 1.7% (1600s) / 3.2% (1500s) against lite's 4.2 / 5.6%, keeping ſ 88% of the time, but the paired CI touches or crosses 0. With ſ→f folded, lite is better by 0.9 points in both centuries. FAILS the preregistered bar.
entries.decision: No standing Latin lane on the GEX45 from this student. It learned the teacher (1.8% CER against the teacher on held-out pages), so the ceiling is the teacher: a re-run needs a 3.8-Flash teacher via agy (quota resets ~2026-10-24) and more pages, under a new prereg (#6871 item 2)

entries.question: Which model should embed the ~20M page images for text→image search: CLIP-B/32 or SigLIP2?
entries.verdict: On 60 real search_images queries over 15,000 page images, SigLIP2-so400m finds 2.2x as many relevant pages as CLIP-B/32 (P@10 0.46 vs 0.21, Δ +0.25 [0.19, 0.31]; nDCG@10 0.64 vs 0.20), and beats SigLIP2-base by +0.12 [0.07, 0.17]. Judge re-agreement 0.94.
entries.decision: Per the prereg: if the ~20M page images are embedded for search, use SigLIP2-so400m, not CLIP-B/32 (≈ 5–8 GPU-days on the GEX45). Whether and where page-image hits are shown is a product decision for Derek (#6871 item 3)

entries.question: Three $0 ways to make the Mongolian Kanjur reader ourselves
entries.verdict: Three $0 routes to a Kanjur reader without a Mongolist: cluster-and-vote fails (clusters are 90% pure only for short forms; the LoRA reads one word 6 ways, so votes do not converge: 14% of 4+-letter voted labels hit the lexicon vs 24% for single reads); the Manchu woodblock model reads no better than our LoRA (21% vs 24% lexicon hit on the same crops; 0/31 true 4+-letter words) and the two agree on 2% of crops; Opus recovers 63% of rKTs title words from the Tibetan (shuffled 18%).

entries.question: Result: real Kanjur columns fix the Mongolian reader's letters; meaning is still short
entries.verdict: Real data works: 494 real columns (900 steps) cut v23 real-prose CER from 56.8 % (arm a re-read; 55.5 % realgt) to 23.6 %, clean3 24.2 %, synthetic held-out 4.2 % (no forgetting). Meaning check 8/30 match (from 0), 12 partial, controls 1/30: below its ≥ 18 bar.

entries.question: Preregistration: do real Kanjur columns fix the Mongolian reader? A gated pilot
entries.verdict: Preregistration only: continue the synthetic-trained Kanjur reader on ~500 real columns (B/C/D transliterations), 40 % of a 14,400-row mix, 900 steps; scored on v23 real prose (baseline CER 55.5 %) and the frozen 30-column meaning check (baseline 0/30). No result here.

entries.question: Palenque held-out eval and an offline replay of the candidate-sign suggester
entries.verdict: PALENQUE: neither model reads the Cross Group tablets from the drawing. With the monument named and parallels given, Gemini 4 Argon is exact on 45 of 100 held-out blocks (judged 56–60), but with the crops WITHHELD it still gets 36. On the 90 blocks both arms ran the image adds 3 exact readings (39 vs 36), so the score is memory of a famous text plus context. Opus does better without the image (13) than with it (9–10). From the bare crop, Gemini gets 10–12 exact (almost all dates) and Opus 0. The Opus check of Gemini is right on 74–80% of what it accepts (90% needed). SUGGESTER: no-go. Fused recall@6 of the true sign is 32% on Palenque (80% needed) and 38% on the Dresden codex (50% needed). Even a perfect choice of channel per sign would reach only 51% and 58%. Picture search against the sign drawings is at chance on both.
entries.decision: No suggester UI yet (#6945): the picture channel is the limit. No AI glyph readings shown to readers (#6903): on famous Classic texts the models recite rather than read, and on the codex they cannot read. Next for #6945: a numeral counter and a picture channel trained on confirmed blocks, re-measured with this replay, on texts a model cannot have memorised.

entries.question: Do page links land on the right page if the model cites an ID and the server writes the link?
entries.verdict: Cite-by-ID test on 40 readers' questions. The model cites each page by an ID ([P7]) and the server writes the link; the top 6 search hits are shown whole. Wrong-page links rose 25 → 115 (11.4% → 19.5% of judged links) because the model cited 2.7× as many pages and mixed up IDs the way it mixed up page numbers. Wrong-fact rate fell 8.7% → 3.4%, and the judges preferred B 24 to 15. The same arm on gemini-3.8-flash (C) was worse again: 150 wrong-page links and time to done 1.8× slower. Gate not met.
entries.decision: Both arms land behind flags, off: LIBRARIAN_CITE_IDS=1 and LIBRARIAN_MODEL=gemini-3.8-flash. The default Librarian is unchanged (#6946).

entries.question: Preregistration: does any engine give the Chinese held residue a reader, per class?
entries.verdict: Preregistration only: open OCR engines on the GEX45 (PaddleOCR-VL-1.6 with layout, MinerU 2.5 Pro, Qwen3-VL-8B, Qwen2.5-VL-7B AWQ, GLM-OCR) against gemini-3.1-flash-lite (paid) and Gemini 3.8 Flash (agy) on the 100 Opus reference pages of the Chinese held residue, per failure class. No result here.

entries.question: Does any engine give the Chinese held residue a reader worth applying, per class?
entries.verdict: No engine clears the preregistered bar in any class of the Chinese held residue. The nearest is Paddle as already run in production (PaddleOCR-VL-1.6, layout off): it ties agy Gemini 3.8 Flash on table (7.0% vs 5.8% bag CER, paired Δ 0.0, CI −0.7 to +3.2) and mixed (4.0% vs 4.0%), and beats it on seal gloss text (5.6% vs 11.5%, Δ −3.1, CI −14.9 to −1.5). It fails the hallucination check: it loops 3,983 characters on a blank leaf. It also gets 41% of seal head glyphs right (Flash 65%) and misses the dense ephemeris tables. Layout-on Paddle, MinerU 2.5 Pro, GLM-OCR, Qwen2.5-VL-7B and Qwen3-VL-8B are all worse than Paddle as-is. The held-by-title premise ('Paddle cannot read these') is wrong for gloss and prose text, but right for seal heads, dense tables and blank-leaf loops.
entries.decision: No new reader for any class. Keep the 47,420 pages held. Paddle as-is plus an output-length guard is the candidate to confirm on a fresh draw for table and mixed (see DECISION lines on #6871)

entries.question: Preparing the guarded-Paddle apply on held Chinese tables and mixed pages
entries.verdict: Preparing the guarded-Paddle apply on the 27,048 held Chinese table + mixed pages: three things the confirmation did not measure. (1) The R2 archived copy of these pages is a 1/3-scale JPEG; read at that scale, Paddle collapsed on 5 of 99 pages it reads correctly from the Archive's full-size leaf, so the run reads the Archive leaf (the bar's input). (2) guard.py's LOOP rule cannot judge Flash's replies on numeric tables (it flagged all 3 good ephemeris reads in the confirmation); the reply guard keeps COLLAPSE and OVERRUN, and keeps LOOP only off NUMERIC pages: in-sample 3/3 failed replies caught, 0/7 good flagged. (3) The #6388 table detector, which production withholds served Paddle pages by, flags 73 of 709 guard-passed pages in the first chunk, 72 of them in one calendar-table volume.
entries.decision: None here. The GPU read runs as gpu-queue task 50-zh-guarded-read (files only), Flash and the writer's dry run follow (after-gpu.sh); the apply is Derek's DECISION on #6871

entries.question: Preregistration: does guarded Paddle read held Chinese tables and mixed prose as well as agy Flash, on fresh pages?
entries.verdict: Preregistration only: production Paddle (PaddleOCR-VL-1.6, layout off) behind a frozen output guard, against agy Gemini 3.8 Flash, on a fresh draw of 25 table + 25 mixed held Chinese pages from books not in the first reference set. No result here.

entries.question: Does guarded Paddle read held Chinese tables and mixed prose as well as agy Flash, on fresh pages?
entries.verdict: Guarded Paddle passes the preregistered bar in both classes on a fresh draw of 25 table + 25 mixed held pages, from books not in the first set. Paired against agy Gemini 3.8 Flash: table median Δ 0.0 (95% CI −3.9 to +0.7 pp, noise floor 1.9); mixed 0.0 (CI −0.9 to 0.0, floor 1.8). The frozen guard caught 8 of 8 collapsed or looped Paddle outputs and passed 34 of 35 good pages. Not preregistered: two works have no reader in either engine. Those are 欽定西域同文志 (polyglot glossary: Flash refuses or misreads, Paddle mis-orders the registers) and 琴譜合璧 (qin tablature: both fail).
entries.decision: Apply guarded Paddle to the held table + mixed pages, except 欽定西域同文志, 琴譜合璧 and the 清文鑑 titles, which stay held. That is about 27,000 pages, ≈ 0.33 GPU-days plus ≈ 3,300 Flash calls. Awaiting Derek (DECISION on #6871). The writer, the provenance standard and a routing row come first

entries.question: Can the vector service answer search_within_book's semantic leg?
entries.verdict: The page-vector service answers match_pages_in_books' question with an exact float32 scan of the named books' rows. On 30 real search_within_book calls it takes 14 ms p50 / 28 ms p90 (10 / 21 ms in the server), against the RPC's 215 / 507 ms. It returned the RPC's top 10 on 28 of 30 calls and the same top result on 29. In the other two, and in 2 of 10 twelve-book calls at k=20, the similarity lists are identical value for value: pages with identical vectors tie, and the two systems break the tie differently. Recall by similarity is 1.0. Shared pages agree within 3e-7.
entries.decision: Shipped for search_within_book and the Librarian's scoped page search (semanticPageSearchScoped, English, ≤ 50 books) in VECTOR_SEARCH_MODE=serve, with the RPC as the fallback on any error, timeout, complete:false or a service that ignores book_ids. Deployed to l7a with one restart on 2026-10-18 23:23Z.

entries.question: The two search tools the speed wave did not reach
entries.verdict: search_within_book was slow for two reasons. Its keyword leg asked Atlas a book-filtered $search, which took 0.3–5.7 s cold (p90 4.2 s on 30 real calls), nearly all of it before the first document came back. On top of that, the tool fetched its own route over HTTPS. Asking the keyword page service instead, with the book as the allow-list, takes the route from p50 1,555 / p90 5,299 ms to p50 452 / p90 1,012 ms on the same 30 calls (cloudlayer, both arms in-process). Overlap@10 with today's output is 0.973, with the same top result on 28 of 30. Book-scoped search_translations goes from 561 / 1,477 to 184 / 447 ms, the same single passage on 22 of 25 calls that return one. The differing pages print as much of the query as the ones they replace, with two exceptions that favour the service. What is left of search_within_book's p90 is the semantic leg: the Gemini embedding plus a Supabase RPC, ~0.5–1.1 s.
entries.decision: Shipped in the PR for #2049 for live books. Hidden books, tenants, ?lang= and any service failure stay on Atlas.

entries.question: Which ef serves real reader queries?
entries.verdict: On 38 real reader queries the page-vector service at ef 256 matched match_semantic's mean recall (0.900 vs 0.909 of the exact top-40) but missed two queries almost entirely (0.05, 0.60). ef 1024 lifts the mean to 0.948 with the worst query at 0.85, against match_semantic's worst of 0.55, for ~31 ms p50 / 100 ms p99 live. l7a runs ef 1024 from 2026-10-18; production serves from the service.

entries.question: How short can the original-text lane's grace be?
entries.verdict: The original-text lane's grace cannot be cut much without costing readers its rows. On 60 real global search_translations calls the lane answered a median 1,462 ms after its start (p10 486, p90 3,160); only 7 of 56 answered within 500 ms and none within 100 ms. Today's rule, 500 ms after the English answer, showed its rows on 8 searches (40 rows). Timed from the lane's start, 525 ms keeps all 40, 500 ms keeps 35 (0.875), 250 ms keeps 12 (0.30) and 0 ms none. The grace is now 550 ms from the lane's start: the same output on all 60 searches (overlap 1.000). It shortens the answer only by the English lane's own time (~66 ms p50), or by up to ~500 ms when the English lane falls back to the RPC.
entries.decision: UNTRANSLATED_GRACE_MS = 550, counted from the lane's start (the shared query vector is ready), not after the English answer. Dropping the grace (0) would save ~0.5 s on most searches and lose every original-text row the lane now shows (8 of 60 searches here; ~35% of /api/search calls in production in the 6 h before) — that trade is a product decision, raised on #2049, not taken here.

entries.question: Which translator for the ~85K public Tibetan pages that have a good transcription and no English?
entries.verdict: Gemini 4 Argon low (agy) clears the bar on 60 Tibetan pages: fidelity 4.31, 0.09 below Opus [−0.27, +0.11], 0 reversal pages of 59; 3.8 Flash is 0.40 below with 2 reversals and fails. The withheld production English scores 1.1 (another text). At 500 agy calls a day, 85K pages take about 173 days.

entries.question: Is the Tibetan English already on the site good enough, or must it be re-translated first?
entries.verdict: Stored 3.8 Flash English on the Tengyur Pramāṇa/Madhyamaka (23.6K pages) scores 4.30, 0.13 ABOVE Argon, 0 reversals: KEEP. Stored 3-flash-preview English (21.6K pages) scores 3.58, 0.88 below Argon [−1.15, −0.60]: RE-TRANSLATE. Argon reverses a negation on 4 of the 20 Pramāṇa/Madhyamaka pages.

entries.question: Why the book lane is the slowest stage of /api/search, and the fix
entries.verdict: Production logged the book lane as degraded on 10% of /api/search calls in 7 days, and the regex fallback timing out is the likely cause. The /api/search book lane was slow because of its regex metadata fallback. On 40 sampled reader queries it fired on 16, read every live book from Mongo (42,372 docs) at 0.9–2.2 s, and found a book on only 2 of them. The same RegExp objects run over an in-memory snapshot of the five fields take 27 ms p50 and 34 ms p90, and return the same match set on 40 of 40 sampled queries and 150 of 150 further multi-word queries. With that, the lane goes from p50 385–456 / p90 1,341–1,925 ms to p50 219–260 / p90 386–428 ms, measured from the main box. What is left is single-word queries, about 30% of the sample: books_catalog has no index on language or subject_keywords, so they filter the whole 229 MB heap (p90 656 ms).
entries.decision: In-memory fallback shipped in the PR for #2049. Two GIN indexes on books_catalog are proposed as a DECISION and not applied.

entries.question: Can the reader/refuter flow propose bylines across the remaining printer-dynasty books?
entries.verdict: Of 383 printer-dynasty books with an OCR front-matter window, a claude -p reader plus screens plus an Opus refuter proposes 116 byline corrections; 20 of 20 sampled proposals match the title-page image.

entries.question: Phrase-first for unquoted unspaced-script queries
entries.verdict: Phrase-first for unquoted Han and Tibetan queries finds the page a reader copied 5 characters or 4 syllables from: on the Atlas page lane, unquoted lenient Hit@10 goes from 0.03 to 1.00 (Han, n 40) and from 0.00 to 1.00 (Tibetan, n 30). The quoted arm and the six spaced-script strata do not change. Cost: unquoted Tibetan p50 goes from 420 to 962 ms (p90 from 656 to 1606 ms), and Han p50 from 342 to 516 ms.

entries.question: Score: the synthetic-trained Mongolian Kanjur reader fails the meaning check
entries.verdict: Fails the preregistered bar. The synthetic-trained Qwen2.5-VL-7B LoRA matches 0 of 30 real Kanjur columns against the Derge parallel (3 partial; controls 0 match, 0 partial; untrained base 0/30). Synthetic held-out CER is 3.9% mean, so by the prereg this is a domain gap and the next data must be real lines. It does read shapes: the Sanskrit title is recognisable in 7/10 text openings and the Mongolian title in 10/10 (controls 0/10 and 1/10), but body prose comes out as non-words spelled with loanword letters.
entries.decision: No 11-mongol-read task and no second synthetic round. The next arm needs real Kanjur lines with known text (#5664)

entries.question: Preregistration: can a reader trained only on synthetic columns read the Mongolian Kanjur?
entries.verdict: Preregistration only: a Qwen2.5-VL-7B LoRA trained on synthetic Kanjur-style columns (ManchuAI-OCR recipe) is scored by a text-only Opus meaning check on 30 frozen real columns (one per volume) against the Derge Tibetan, with shuffled-parallel controls. No result here.

entries.question: Real Kanjur ground truth at $0: published transliterations and rKTs titles, aligned to the scans
entries.verdict: No open Unicode e-text of the Beijing Mongolian Kanjur exists, but four open-access publications transliterate five Kanjur texts with folio markers (34 sides). Aligned to our scans, they give 628 Opus-confirmed real columns: 516 for training (3,713 words, 891 distinct) and 112 from a frozen volume, kept for evaluation only. The rKTs title route gives only 30 confirmed columns. 516 is below the 1,000-column bar, so no 10-mongol-real-train was queued. The synthetic reader's CER on real prose is 55 %.
entries.decision: No training queued (516 < 1,000). The aligned columns, the aligner and the trainer flag are ready for when a Mongolist's body columns arrive (#5664)

entries.question: Does the Inner Mongolia University line dataset give a Mongolian Kanjur reader something to train on?
entries.verdict: Gate 1 fails: IMU-MnOCR is not downloadable to us (application + signed agreement, free only to universities and research institutes, no third-party dissemination), and its real lines are modern typeset prose, not woodblock; its training half is text only.
entries.decision: No GPU training started. Whether to apply to IMU, or to commission Kanjur line ground truth instead, is Derek's call (#5664, #6871 row 6)

entries.question: Do reference drawings and retrieved published readings let a model read Maya glyphs, alone or as a Gemini + Opus team?
entries.verdict: Neither lever teaches a model to read Maya glyphs. Zero-shot picture search finds the right sign in an 8-drawing shortlist for at most 28% of sign values (40% needed), so the picture arms were dropped. Retrieved published readings of parallel captions lift Opus from 5 to 12–18 of 70 exact, but every gain is on blocks whose reading was in its context: 0 and 1 of 38 unseen. Opus as checker accepts 52 of Gemini 4 Argon's 70 readings at 50% precision (90% needed).
entries.decision: No AI glyph readings on codex pages, not even 'Opus-checked' (#6903). The #6921 glyph rungs stay learner exercises over the published readings, not machine candidates.

entries.question: Can Opus read Maya glyph blocks from a sign catalogue and published examples?
entries.verdict: Neither model can put glyph readings on the Dresden Codex. Opus with a sign catalogue and 17 published example readings (arm c) leaves 54 of 70 held-out blocks unread and gets 5 exactly right. All 5 repeat readings that appear in its own examples; it reads 0 of the 55 blocks whose reading it was not shown. It invents nothing on 8 illegible controls. Gemini 4 Argon on the same prompt gets 22 of 70 exact and 27 judged correct (9 of 55 unseen blocks exact), but it is confidently wrong on about 20 of its 64 attempts, every wrong answer at confidence ≥0.55.
entries.decision: No model glyph readings on codex pages (#6903). Glyph pages keep describe-or-decline (#5653).

entries.question: Can an open model on the GEX45 replace the agy Flash screener for page joins?
entries.verdict: Qwen3-14B-AWQ on the GEX45 cannot replace the agy Flash screener for page joins: 59% agreement with Opus on 240 real joins (κ 0.17) against Flash's 91% (κ 0.82), Δ −32 points (paired 95% CI −39 to −25); it misses 9 of 30 planted breaks and keeps only 66 of Flash's 110 verified repairs, so it fails as a pre-filter too. Its own repeat agreement is 73% (κ 0.45).
entries.decision: Don't adopt: the agy Flash call stays the seam screener; GEX45 moves to #6871 item 3

entries.question: Can the Librarian answer faster without answering worse?
