entries.verdict: Thinking LOW on the Librarian's tool rounds, plus one parallel-search prompt line, halves time to done (p50 20.5 → 11.7 s) with no quality loss two blind Opus judges can see (B 20, A 18, tie 2 on 40 readers' questions).
entries.decision: Fast tool rounds on by default in src/lib/embassy/librarian.ts; LIBRARIAN_FAST_TOOL_ROUNDS=0 turns them off (PR #6909, #6904)

entries.question: Can the answer model's own instructions put links on the page that says it?
entries.verdict: Rewriting the Librarian's four closing citation lines (link only the page that states the claim; background with no link; one-page blockquotes; captions from the image record) does not cut wrong-page links: 26 → 30 of 168 / 182 judged links on 40 readers' questions (two Opus judges, a third on splits). Gate not met.
entries.decision: Arm B lands behind LIBRARIAN_CITE_PAGES=1, off; the default prompt is unchanged (#6946)

entries.question: Does each Librarian page link land on the page that says it?
entries.verdict: Gate not met. Re-pointing quoted links by the quotation fixes 2 of 25 wrong-page links with no new error; a flash-lite router cuts wrong-page links 25 → 18 / 24 → 21 (two Opus judges) but moves 3 of its 10 links onto a page that supports the claim less.
entries.decision: Deterministic quote re-pointing and caption-number check ON in groundTurn (src/lib/embassy/librarian.ts); the flash-lite router ships OFF (LIBRARIAN_CITATION_ROUTER=1 turns it on) (#6946)

entries.question: Does an open engine on the GEX45 read Latin print better than flash-lite, century by century?
entries.verdict: Under the preregistered bar, GLM-OCR earns the 1500s (median CER 3.1% vs flash-lite 5.6%, paired Δ −1.1 points, CI −2.9 to −0.3) and no open engine earns the 1600s. The whole margin is flash-lite writing ſ as f. With f folded to s (post hoc), lite reads 0.7% / 1.4% and beats every open engine in both centuries by 1–5 points. By eye, lite read better on 10 of the 12 pages checked (1 tie, 1 real Kraken win). Gemini 3.8 Flash (agy) is best overall: 0.6% / 1.4%.
entries.decision: Recommended: no standing Latin lane on the GEX45. Fix ſ on the Gemini side instead (3.8 Flash, or lite plus a long-s pass). The preregistered rule names GLM-OCR for the 1500s; Derek decides (DECISION on #5924). MinerU2.5-Pro and olmOCR-2 are queued behind Mongolian (gpu-queue 20-latin-mineru-olmocr)

entries.question: Does image gain find the guessed spans in a stored OCR read, well enough to pre-screen pages before Opus?
entries.verdict: Interim, on 707 of 2,178 Opus-adjudicated stored reads: image gain (log p | image − log p | no image, Qwen2.5-VL-7B AWQ, teacher-forced) ranks the words Opus marked wrong at unit AUROC 0.60 (95% CI 0.57–0.64). The preregistered bar is 0.75, and no language clears it. It does not beat text-only perplexity (0.54; paired CI −0.01 to +0.14). It does see INVENTED text: 0.86 (0.79–0.90) on invented spans, where perplexity scores 0.25, because invented text is fluent. It is blind to one-letter misreads (0.52). The image-conditioned surprisal alone (0.70) beats both.
entries.decision: No image-gain pre-screen before Opus review, in any language. The full run is queued as gex45 gpu-queue task 50-grounding-6871: the remaining 1,504 items including the 41 plants, and the noise floor. Its numbers land as a follow-up entry

entries.question: Can a check, not a prompt, keep reversed Hebrew column order out of the Rashi re-read?
entries.verdict: An image-anchored column-order check catches every reversed G4L read on Zohar Chadash: of 53 labelled reads (pilot + colfix runs, 30 pages), it called 0 reversed reads 'correct' (24 reversed: 22 flagged, 2 undetermined) and flagged 0 correct reads (22 correct: 17 pass, 5 undetermined). Writing only the reads it passes gives 0 of 18 read left column first (95% upper bound 18%), against the target of ≤ 1 of 23. The 3 pages where it disagreed with the Opus judge were read by eye: the check was right on all 3; the judge had called reversed reads 'correct'.
entries.decision: Wire it into the Rashi lane as a per-page refusal (write only 'correct'), then re-measure on a second Rashi book before row 1 runs (#6769).

entries.question: What can the GEX45 GPU do per hour, and what does each #6871 queue item cost in GPU-days?
entries.verdict: On the GEX45 (RTX PRO 4000 SFF, 24 GB, 70 W), PaddleOCR-VL and MinerU2.5-Pro read ~3,500 pages/h, GLM-OCR 1,460, olmOCR-2 1,090; the 7.5M-page Latin backlog is ~90–100 GPU-days on the fastest, 230 on GLM-OCR. Re-embedding the translated corpus is 1–5 days, CLIP over every page image ~2 days.
entries.decision: None. Prices the #6871 queue in GPU-days; each queue item still owes its own quality gate

entries.question: The Florentine Codex against its published translation and transcription
entries.verdict: Against the published scholarly English of the Florentine Codex's Nahuatl column (the Getty Digital Florentine Codex, used as a private answer key), the two-pass English (a Gemini 4 Argon Low draft reviewed by Opus against the page image, on the new Argon-high transcription) scores 4.39/5 fidelity with 1.32 meaning errors a page, on 38 leaves from Books 1–9. The Opus English it replaces, made on the old flash-lite transcription, scores 3.26 with 4.21 errors. Two-pass beats it by +1.13 (95% CI +0.86, +1.40), winning 29 of 38 pages, tying 9 and losing 0. It beats the Argon draft alone by +0.34 (CI +0.16, +0.53), 13/24/1. On the transcription, 52 leaves scored against the Getty paleographic transcription: Argon-high cuts the Nahuatl character error rate from 0.152 (flash-lite) to 0.061 and is better on 49 of 52 leaves. On the Spanish the two are even at the median (0.118 / 0.120).
entries.decision: Re-OCR with Gemini 4 Argon High and two-pass translation are what the three volumes get (#6865, Derek 2026-10-18); this measures the result. The 20 Vol. 3 leaves of the sample (Books 10–12) are not in the English table: their two-pass waits on the agy weekly quota.

entries.question: Clef audit follow-up: the 45 high books, the offset cause, two batches
entries.verdict: 21 of the 45 high-flag books carry wrong text on a page read by eye. The multi-leaf IA offsets are image-side (#3368 bulk-JP2 numbering, the #4790 image class): the March 2026 text matches the source leaf. Batch XsDsFHKU_8_EOILnWQTS- is one book with ~all 133 pages wrong; the BPH 6988a59* cohort is ~43% wrong pages (CI 21-67%).

entries.question: Can Opus make reference pages for the Chinese pages Paddle could not read?
entries.verdict: Reference set for the 47,420 held Chinese residue pages (recount exact: mixed 17,784, table 15,280, seal 5,878, reverted 372, unclassed 8,106). Two independent Opus reads, with a third resolving disagreements, give credible references for the Chinese text in table (2.0% order-insensitive disagreement), seal (3.2%), mixed (3.3% without 清文鑑) and reverted (3.8% without 清文鑑). There is no credible model reference for 清文鑑 Manchu-Chinese pages (20% disagreement) or for any Manchu/Mongolian script (21/98 transliteration tokens agree). 19/20 unclassed pages are textless.

entries.question: What does a served semantic page search cost once the service supplies the text?
entries.verdict: Serving the page text from the l7a service's own store (with_text, over HTTPS) answers a 45-row semantic page search in 19–41 ms p50 (23–52 ms p90; the spread is whether the 19 GB text file is in the page cache), against 152–168 ms for the phase-3 path (service ids + Supabase hydration) and 985–1,002 ms for match_semantic. All 3,957 rows both returned agree with the RPC on every column. Measured from l7a, 0.7 ms from Hetzner main.

entries.question: Does the page-vector service's filtered path return the rows an exact filtered scan does?
entries.verdict: With the phase-3 filter planner, the l7a page-vector service returns a full page whenever it says its answer is complete (93 of 120 filtered answers; recall@45 0.964 against an exact float32 filtered scan). The other 27 are flagged complete:false, so the app falls back to the RPC. All 27 are a broad Latin filter on a query whose neighbourhood holds no Latin (26 of them Chinese or Tibetan page vectors).

entries.question: What does a reader lose when the vector service freezes?
entries.verdict: A frozen or dead page-vector service costs readers nothing in shadow, and in serve costs ~410 ms per semantic page search with 0 errors and identical rows. Live: a 60 s SIGSTOP of the production service (shadow) logged the 400 ms timeout on every overlapping search, every search answered 200, and rpc_ms did not rise. Preview in serve against a host that drops packets: +412 ms p50 / +443 ms p90 paired, 0 non-200, 0 empty, identical rows. The bar was ≤ 400 ms; the timeout itself is 400. Found on the way: match_semantic fails on 42 of 236 (17.8%) real site searches after 3–15 s, and the service answered 41 of those.

entries.question: Do the vector and keyword services hold a burst, and does a type-check on their box hurt them?
entries.verdict: Both search services hold the 19:55 'plague' burst pattern (7 parallel) with no errors, idle and while sl-tsc runs on their box. The keyword service also holds 20 parallel (p99 ≤ 485 ms against a 1,500 ms budget). The vector service at 20 parallel sends 4.5–9.5% of calls past its 400 ms budget (p99 1.0–1.3 s) while its own handler time stays under 20 ms: a staircase of ~95 ms per request somewhere on l7a, outside the timed handler. The 21:04 memory-throttle condition was not reproduced, because vector-search is still in sourcelibrary.slice at the 20 GiB runtime stopgap.

entries.question: A standing guard on search latency and errors
entries.verdict: A synthetic probe now sends 10 fixed queries through /api/search, /api/search/semantic?level=page and MCP search_library / search_concept every 15 min from the main box. It pages ntfy when a surface's p90 doubles against its trailing 24 h, or on 3 failing runs in a row. It makes no model call of its own and costs ~3,840 Vercel invocations a day. Its first runs showed that the semantic route's edge cache (s-maxage 300 + swr 600) spans the whole 15-minute gap, so the probe now carries a nonce to reach the route.
entries.decision: Installed on main's crontab (infrastructure/hetzner-crontab, 'Synthetic search probe'); log /var/log/sourcelibrary/search-probe.jsonl

entries.question: Can Jev re-rank search candidates against a reader's question?
entries.verdict: On 30 questions written in advance, Jev re-ranking about 300 production candidates puts a relevant page in 98% of top-10 slots (96–100), against 54% (46–61) for search_translations and 70% (63–76) for search_concept, at $0.011 and about 2 s a question.
entries.decision: Recommended: offer the 300-candidate Jev re-rank to the Librarian as a passage tool for question-shaped requests; not in the /search UI yet, and not as a replacement for the untranslated-page lane.

entries.question: Preregistration: can an open model on the GEX45 replace the agy Flash screener for page joins?
entries.verdict: Preregistration only: an open model on the GEX45 (Qwen3-14B-AWQ, vLLM) as the page-join screener, scored against Opus labels on the #6742 300-junction set, with the agy Flash screener's agreement as the bar. No result here.

entries.question: Can a Hetzner BM25 index stand in for the Atlas keyword page lane?
entries.verdict: A tantivy index of the same page text returns 96% of the books and 90% of the pages the Atlas page lane puts in its top 20, every roll-up book, and Atlas's first page every time, on 180 scored logged queries. It answers in 20 ms at p50 and 147 ms at p90 when warm (195 / 491 ms cold, on a network volume). Atlas takes 787 / 2,200 ms for the same lane. SQLite FTS5 was measured out first: 175–978 ms for common words on 8.7% of the corpus.
entries.decision: Serve the /api/search keyword page lane from tantivy, not SQLite FTS5. Shadow first (KEYWORD_SEARCH_MODE=shadow), serve after a shadow week.

entries.question: Does a variant spelling find the canonical name's pages, in the service as in Atlas?
entries.verdict: Typing a variant spelling of a person's name (40 entities pairs: Platone, Salomon, Plinius, Iuppiter …) brings back pages printing the canonical spelling in both the Atlas lane and the keyword service: 40/40 at any rank in both, 39 vs 38 in the top 10, at 587 ms vs 34 ms p50. The service returns twice as many name-variant pages (290 vs 139), because it de-duplicates against the main list before taking 10, not after. That is a behaviour change to decide before keyword serve.

entries.question: Does the keyword service find the page a reader copied a phrase from?
entries.verdict: On 300 random live pages, the keyword service finds a page printing a copied phrase in the top 10 as often as the Atlas lane or more often, in every script stratum, at 1/12 to 1/50 of the time. Quoted: 300/300 for both, 9 ms vs 108 ms at p50. Unquoted, both lanes are weak (0.42 vs 0.43 Hit@10 for a distinctive run), and unquoted Han and Tibetan phrases find nothing in either: the page lane ORs single characters and syllables.

entries.question: Opus, Gemini 4 Argon and Gemini 3.8 Flash on the Florentine Codex's two-column leaves
entries.verdict: On 20 two-column leaves of the Florentine Codex, with the same column instruction for every arm, Gemini 4 Argon Low beats Opus on the Nahuatl column under both judges, order-averaged: +1.18 under a Gemini 3.8 Flash High judge (CI +0.93, +1.43) and +0.20 under an Opus judge (CI −0.07, +0.50). Only the Gemini judge's margin is clear. Opus beats Gemini 3.8 Flash Low under the Opus judge (+0.57) and loses to it under the Gemini judge (−0.42, CI crosses 0). The Spanish column is near 5 for all three, with Argon slightly ahead. The stored flash-lite English scores 1.8/5 on the Nahuatl and summarises it on 7–8 of 40 judgements; none of the new arms summarised.
entries.decision: None taken here; Derek decides. The running Opus re-translation (job florentine-nahuatl, #6865) was not changed.

entries.question: Finding: the updated_at delta misses most new rows
Library-wide: which pages carry text that is not their own image's text?
entries.verdict: About 0.8% of visible books with text (≈250) have wrong-leaf text on 2+ of ~3 sampled pages; by eye 11 of 12 such books checked are real. Random flags are real 8 of 14 times where readable.

entries.question: Does the Hetzner page-vector service find the same neighbours as exact search?
entries.verdict: The l7a page-vector service at ef_search 256 returns 95.6% of the exact top-45 over all 7.63M page vectors, at 8.8 ms p50 / 12.4 ms p90 server time; the default ef 128 falls just short (94.6%).

entries.question: Can Tibetan work dates come from the colophon and BDRC rather than a model?
entries.verdict: Tibetan WORK dates can be sourced for 479 of 2,341 books (BDRC work authors 234, colophon- or title-named authors matched to a BDRC person 159, colophon years 53, one BDRC AuthoredEvent) and given canonical Indian windows for 546 more. A model reading a colophon is a good reader of WHO and WHAT WORDS but not of the arithmetic: in the first full pass it supplied a rab byung cycle number for 20 of the 33 composition years it gave one for, where the quoted words state none, and misread one element-animal pair; on 5 colophons opened by eye the OCR was right every time, the model's interpretation wrong 3 times (author of a reply vs its questioner, a translation colophon called a copy, an appended prayer's author taken for the volume's).
entries.decision: Tibetan work dates written by tibetan-work-dates.mjs (run tibetan-work-dates-2026-10-16, 1,454 books): the model reads, the code converts the cycle year and checks the cycle, element, animal and CE year against the quoted words; a named author needs the model's dates AND exactly one BDRC person whose dates meet them. #6721.

entries.question: Seam repair, lean: rule fixes, Gemini via agy, and a runner that spends Claude only on a sample
entries.verdict: Gemini 3.8 Flash via agy repairs page joins as well as Opus (verified yield 36.7% vs 36.3% on the 300-junction set, 1/118 judged worse), so the lean runner sends the tranche to Gemini and spends Claude only on a 7% blind sample: ≈ $0.12 list (≈ 0.01 weekly points) of Claude per 100 joins vs the pilot's ≈ 0.6 points. Rule-only fixes for catchword echo and dup8 match Opus on 78% and 60%, below the 95% bar; neither is trusted.

entries.question: Can one prompt instruction stop new broken page joins on the production translation lane?
entries.verdict: One added edge instruction does not cut broken page joins on the production CLI lane (3.8 Flash): 15.4 vs 16.2 defective per 100 joins, Δ +0.8 (95% CI −4.7 to +6.3), inside an A-vs-A swing of 6.7. Not shipped. The lane already makes few of the shapes the instruction names.
entries.decision: NO MEASURABLE EFFECT by the registered rule; the v13 default stays (DECISIONS.md)

entries.question: A write-time seam guard, and sending every join of the most-read books to the repairer: dry runs
entries.verdict: Two $0 dry runs. A write-time seam guard replayed over a fresh 39-page CLI translation checked 34 joins with 35 agy calls, 0 lockouts and 0 errors, and would have repaired 3. Every-join mode on the 20 most-read books found 46% of sampled prose joins defective, 88% of them outside the rule tranche; it would write 22% of joins, with the blind Opus sample at 19/20.

entries.question: A Gemini leaf screen in front of Opus correct-in-place writes
entries.verdict: A gemini-3.8-flash-low leaf screen ('is this text the text of this leaf; is any passage not on it?') over 4,714 of arm B's Opus corrections and keeps (queue ranks 301–1000) flagged 18 pages; a sealed Opus settled 16 as false positives (annotation tags such as <vocab>, <warning>, descriptions of blank leaves) and confirmed 2, both arm B's own refusals (a model <warning> in place of a modern preface), not invented served text. On calibration it caught 2/2 whole-page wrong-leaf shifts but only 2/12 stored texts that lane B's Opus adjudicator had judged invented or garbled in place: a pass means 'not another leaf's text', not 'no invention'.
entries.decision: Job opus-screen-6694 (#6694 step 3) ran the screen, Derek's q300 audit rule and cli-ocr.mjs apply on every batch: 3,624 arm B pages written, 150 refused by the shared-words guard, 16 audit-disputed pages withheld from the write; Greek on lane B: 92 written, 48 refused, 31 pages contained in 13 books.

entries.question: Can Gemini 4 Argon or Opus read the Mongolian Kanjur? Same 10 pages as the 2026-10-04 probe
entries.verdict: Neither Gemini 4 Argon (low, high) nor Opus reads the Mongolian Kanjur: 0 of 10 pages match the Derge parallel on any of 8 arm×prompt reads; Argon writes fluent wrong text, Opus declines every page.
entries.decision: No $0 CLI reader for the 83K Mongolian pages; the 2026-10-04 verdict stands, and a trained recogniser remains Derek's separate decision (#5664)

entries.question: Do the English translations of the Yucatec books state the numbers the Maya prints?
entries.verdict: Across 3,932 translated Yucatec pages, the scan finds 4,897 Maya number phrases and judges 1,318 of them. 63 of 190 compound numerals (scores, 400s, catac sums) are not stated in the page's English. The 1846 Coleccion de sermones does not follow Beltrán's 1746 table: wherever the referent is known, it uses lahu oxkal for 30, not 50. So its 'thirty-three years' for Christ is the author's number, not a model error. Five Beltrán-confirmed mismatches were checked on the page images and re-translated.
entries.decision: Keep scripts/audit/maya-numeral-scan.mjs as a read-only lead list for Yucatec books; a flagged numeral is fixed only after a look at the image and the table. Do not rewrite the Coleccion's lahu oxkal pages to Beltrán's 50.

entries.question: Does Gemini 4 Argon, or Opus at one page per call, beat Gemini 3.8 Flash Low on Maya?
entries.verdict: On the same 20 Mayan-language pages as 2026-10-14, Gemini 4 Argon Low (agy, one page per call) translates better than Gemini 3.8 Flash Low under both judges, order-averaged: +0.63 under a Gemini 3.8 Flash High judge (CI +0.13, +1.11) and +0.72 under an Opus judge (CI +0.42, +1.02). On the 15 Yucatec pages alone it leads by +0.63 and +0.57. Opus at one page per call does not close the gap: it trails 3.8 Flash by 2.12 and 0.60, and leads only on the Kaqchikel manuscript under the Opus judge (+0.40).
entries.decision: Yucatec lane: Gemini 4 Argon Low WITH a one-line style prompt (see the addendum: unstyled, it glosses word by word), by the brief's rule (an arm replaces 3.8 Flash only if both judges put it ahead). Kaqchikel stays on Opus: Argon was never judged against Opus, and Opus-1pp leads 3.8 Flash on Kaqchikel under the Opus judge.

entries.question: Gemini 4 Argon low re-read pilots: Grec 1841 and Zohar Chadash
entries.verdict: One-book pilots, no writes. Against the page image, a blind Opus judge prefers the Gemini 4 Argon low re-read to the served text on 29/30 Grec 1841 spreads (0 worse) and on 25/25 Zohar Chadash pages served from flash-lite OCR. It prefers the served text on 5/5 pages whose text was fitted from Sefaria (#5560). As built, cli-ocr.mjs apply would write 5 of 355 Greek pages: the 40% shared-words guard refuses the other 350, because the stored read is that far from the page. On Rashi it would write 121 of 188, 30 of them over Sefaria text. G4L reads the left column first on 6 of 23 two-column Hebrew pages.

entries.question: Does a right-column-first instruction fix G4L's column order on two-column Hebrew pages?
entries.verdict: A right-column-first instruction makes Gemini 4 Argon low's column order on two-column Hebrew pages WORSE, not better: it read the left column first on 15/23 Zohar Chadash pages (65% [45, 81]), against 6/23 (26% [13, 46]) on the same pages without it. Target was <= 1. The text itself still beat flash-lite OCR on 18/18 OCR-served pages and lost on 5/5 Sefaria-fitted ones, as in the pilot. The Rashi re-read lane is blocked until an order check exists.
entries.decision: Do not send this instruction. The Rashi/mixed re-read waits for an order check (#6769).

entries.question: Does Gemini 4 Argon low correct the Yigdzin Tibetan better than 3.8 Flash low?
entries.verdict: Gemini 4 Argon LOW corrects the Yigdzin read slightly better than 3.8 Flash low and meets all three preregistered criteria: 0.972 vs Derge, +0.004 [+0.0003, +0.009] over Flash low (18 / 10 folios), 0 of 30 planted errors left (Flash 3), 8 of 390 toward-Derge changes not on the leaf by Opus (2.1%; Flash 13 of 344, 3.8%). It is 1.7x slower (39 s vs 23 s a page) and made 3 folios slightly worse than the served read (Flash 0).

entries.question: Gemini 4 Argon low correction pass, the same gate volume
entries.verdict: NO-GO for a Gemini 4 Argon LOW correction pass, by the preregistered rule. On the Flash gate volume (435 pages), the tiled Opus judge finds 5 of 40 audited pages worse (bar: at most 2) and the leaf shows the correction at 233 of 297 decided spans, 78% [73, 83] (bar: at least 90% with the lower bound above 80%). Controls pass (72 of 80). G4L is better than Flash on the same gate (Flash: 10 worse, 74% [69, 80]) but not by enough: it substitutes words, splits contracted syllables, normalises particles and mantra, and wrote one Kannada sign into a Tibetan word.
entries.decision: No G4L correction pass; nothing written to pages (#6560 gate)

entries.question: Flash low correction pass, gate volume
entries.verdict: NO-GO for the Flash 3.8 LOW correction pass. On the gate volume (Thadrak Kanjur rGyud 'bum Kha, 435 pages), a blind Opus audit of 40 changed pages, judging each changed span against the leaf, finds 10 of 40 pages worse with full-resolution tiles (the leaf shows the correction at 178 of 239 decided spans, 74% [69, 80]). Pooled over both judges, 6 of 40 pages are worse. The bar was at most 2. The judge without tiles finds 2 of 40, but it abstained on 46% of spans and on 37 of 80 controls. Judge agreement on the decided spans: α 0.44, not settled. The ya-btags guard fired once in 432 pages.
entries.decision: Flash low correction pass not applied; nothing written to pages (#6560 gate)

entries.question: Opus-correct of the high-change stale Siku pages: pilot and the over-correction gate
entries.verdict: NO-GO as written for Opus-correcting the 24,834 stale Siku pages: the over-correction gate (made worse vs the page's own Kanripo leaf by > 0.5 pt on <= 10% of pages) failed. The experiment's prompt (v1) made 9 of 60 Kanripo-scored pages worse (15%, Wilson 8–26%). v1 plus one rule ('keep the page's own character forms; no notes of your own', v2) made 4 of the same 60 worse, but 5 of 40 on a fresh held-out draw (12.5%, 5–26%). Read beside the gate: nearly every 'worse' page is a swap between two forms of one character (髙/高, 㑹/會, 巳/已, 諡/謚) or a printed seal Kanripo leaves out; on the same pages the median Kanripo CER falls 3.5% → 2.1% (v2, n=60) and 3.2% → 2.6% (held-out, n=40). The gate was not moved; Derek decides.

entries.question: How often does a translated page join read broken, can Opus label it, and can flash-lite detect and repair it at corpus scale?
entries.verdict: 31% (25-38%) of served prose page joins are defective by an Opus reference, 11% (6-16%) majorly; flash-lite with thinking detects them at AUC 0.73, but no flash-lite repair is good enough to run unattended.

entries.question: Seam repair pilot, $0: Opus fixes bad page joins on the subscription
entries.verdict: Opus via the CLI repaired 227 of 500 high-precision tranche joins in production (348 pages), each preferred by a blind Opus judge in both orders; the image-grounded judge agreed on 30/30. Sonnet found fewer defects (45 vs 61 verified per 100). Quota, not wall clock, limits the ~330K scale-up.

entries.question: Planner v0: which routing decisions are worth a test, ranked by expected loss per quota?
entries.verdict: Planner v0 ranks 21 routing decisions by expected loss removed per quota cost of a within-round paired test. Fifteen sit above the stop line. The top three are: translate Latin (Flash-Lite vs 3 Flash; the uncertainty is the Gemini judge's view, never measured in Latin); translate German (Flash-Lite vs 3.8 Flash CLI; the evidence already favours 3.8, P 1.00, and only a cross-family round is missing); and read Latin print (Flash-Lite vs 3 Flash vs Sonnet; Flash-Lite is last of the routable readers). Each test costs under 1% of one account-week. Opus leads every language with a reference panel, but Opus can carry only small queues this quarter, so for Latin, German, Chinese and Tibetan the decision is among the Gemini engines.
entries.decision: Three draft briefs attached (briefs/), not dispatched; the session that reads #6740 dispatches them (#6740)

entries.question: Plain translation vs translation with notes, through both subscription lanes
entries.verdict: Asking for notes, summary, keywords, terms and meta does not help the translation body and costs some of it. PLAIN − CURRENT is +0.11 [0.00, +0.21] for 3.8 Flash (Opus judge) and +0.30 [+0.13, +0.47] for Opus (3.8 Flash high judge), 132 pages, beside A-vs-A floors of −0.12 and −0.02. Pages with an omission fall by half in both lanes.
entries.decision: Recommend PLAIN for new translation plus a separate, on-demand notes/summary pass; the default prompt is not changed by this test (#6728)

entries.question: Can paddleTableRisk flag fewer prose pages without missing an invented one?
entries.verdict: Holding recall on the 136 known invented pages at 136/136, a text rule cannot make paddleTableRisk much more precise. The only term that drops no risky page is a ditto term: a page flagged only by short 丨 ditto runs (< 5) on a non-table title. It takes the flagged set from 4,379 to 4,288 pages, of which 86 were prose Paddle read about right and 5 borderline. Precision moves 0.676 → 0.689 (not-false-alarm share) and 0.440 → 0.449 (non-prose share). The large false-alarm pool, 1,098 ditto-only 類書 pages, holds 3 of the 136 (each one extra 丨), so recall decides it. Prose is not a safe negative: 842 prose pages are Paddle text Opus removed ≥ 10 % of (Manchu pages read as Chinese). Shipped opt-in as T_V2; the default is unchanged (not wired).

entries.question: Opus at 10 pages per call against 3.8 Flash, same pages, same round
entries.verdict: On the same 50 pages, in one round, Opus at 10 pages per call beats 3.8 Flash by +0.56 under an Opus judge (book-clustered CI [+0.15, +0.96]) and by +0.33 under a 3.8 Flash-high judge (CI [−0.17, +0.80]). It does not clear the bar under both judges. Opus at 1 page per call beats Flash by +0.71 and +0.78, and both intervals exclude 0. The two judges agree only at α 0.61 on fidelity, so this is not settled.
entries.decision: Opus translation stays at 1 page per call where capacity allows (#6545). Ten per call is not used to stretch Opus capacity: the brief's rule (O10 beats Flash under both judges, CI excludes 0) fails under the Gemini judge (#6690).

entries.question: OCR estimator v0: what does pooling the Pareto charts say about each reader, and how often does each route fail readers?
entries.verdict: OCR estimator v0 fits the Pareto charts' 11,212 scored page × engine reads (1,032 pages, 713 works, 36 engines, 10 script charts) without divergences. Engine differences inside a chart hold (sign right in 732 of 768 in-sample pairs), but levels run 0.064 CER high, because 6.6% of reads score exactly 100% error and a beta-binomial cannot fit that point mass. Flash-Lite is behind Gemini 3 Flash on Latin print by 7 points [5, 10]. The failure-rate model makes three points: reading again from the image is what fails (Tibetan 58–88% of pages not of the leaf); correcting a specialist draft rarely makes it worse (Opus 1–6%, Flash low under 1% on Tibetan); and both write lanes make 0.4% of pages worse [0.0, 2.0] once each judge is read through its controls.
entries.decision: Ready for the planner on within-chart differences; not on levels (a hurdle term for 100%-error reads is the next change) (#6740)

entries.question: Does a write-time leaf-shift gate catch the known shifts without rejecting clean blocks?
entries.verdict: The whole-leaf shift gate in dropDriftedPages catches all 12 by-eye wrong-leaf pages (in 6-8 of their 8 block alignments; the misses are runs cut by a block edge) and rejects 7 of 3,321 single-page-lane blocks (0.21%, 3 of them tier-A strength), each costing a single-page translation of that block.
entries.decision: Ship the gate in all four block lanes through dropDriftedPages (PR for #5021).

entries.question: Does Gemini 4 Argon (low, through the CLI) translate the 365 xl reference pages better than 3.8 Flash and than production?
entries.verdict: Gemini 4 Argon low (CLI) scores better than 3.8 Flash CLI (+0.23 [+0.16, +0.29]) and production (+0.51) on 361 reference pages, with 11 reversal pages against 32 and 46; better than 3.8 in Latin, Greek, Persian, Sanskrit, T4 and T5, the same in German, Hebrew, Arabic, Chinese, Pali and T3. It adds about 3.5× as many unsourced editorial facts.

entries.question: Gemini 4 Argon low vs Opus vs 3.8 Flash, translation, the #6545 panels
entries.verdict: Gemini 4 Argon low (CLI, $0) translates the five hardest languages better than 3.8 Flash (+0.28 Opus judge, +0.49 Gemini 3.8 judge, pooled, both CIs above 0) but worse than Opus under the Opus judge in every language (pooled −0.41 [−0.52, −0.32]); under the Gemini 3.8 judge it is within noise of Opus except in Chinese (−0.38 [−0.64, −0.12]). By the preregistered rule Opus stays in all five. In Hebrew G4L also fills verses the page abbreviates from the canonical text.
entries.decision: Opus stays the hard-language translator (Persian, Sanskrit, Chinese, Greek, Hebrew); G4L neither replaces nor joins it. Where Opus capacity is short, G4L is a better fallback than 3.8 Flash on this evidence (#6729)

entries.question: Gemini 4 Argon on the hardest hands: Greek manuscripts and Rashi script
entries.verdict: Gemini 4 Argon low reads Greek manuscripts better than every engine tried: 3.8 Flash, Opus 5.5, stored production OCR (3 Flash) and Kraken greek-cllg (+6 to +15 points a page, winning on 63-64 of 64 pages). On Rashi-type prints it is better than 3.8 Flash (+24) and production (+35), and the same as Opus 5.5 (30 wins, 26 losses). A no-image recall control scores 15-27 %, so the Rashi scores measure reading, not recitation.

entries.question: Estimator v2: does a judge-family term, and the evidence scored since 12 October, fix v1's misses?
entries.verdict: Estimator v2 adds the first non-Claude judges (Gemini 3.1 Pro and 3.8 Flash High, from #6545, #6559 and #6690) and a judge-family term. Held out, it covers 0.92 of 305 cells on the v1 experiments (v1: 0.92 of 330) and 0.89 of 98 cells on the new ones. xlref-t4 rises from 9 of 16 to 12 of 16, but because of #6545's new Persian data, not the judge term: xlref-t4 had only Opus judges, and with the round × arm-maker term removed it is still 12 of 16. The misses that remain are language-specific (Arabic and Persian in xlref-t4; Hebrew in #6545 stage 2). No Claude self-preference shows: the Gemini 3.1 Pro judge puts Opus further ahead of 3.8 Flash than the Opus judge does.
entries.decision: The planner (#6740 part 3) reads v2 for differences inside one judging round, as v1 allowed; levels across rounds and the router stay out (#6740)

entries.question: Can a lean catalogue-only prompt, and Wikidata, date a library's works?
entries.verdict: A lean catalogue-only prompt (100 books a call, ~30 output tokens a book) dates works as well as the first run's full prompt (Sonnet 85.2% vs 85.4% high/medium, n=318), at 14× fewer output tokens a book; Haiku fails (75.0%). Wikidata alone does NOT date the library's works: an author's lifespan passes on gold (90.1%) but contradicts a model date on 17% of 3,791 library works, mostly because books.author_id names the translator or editor, and a work_id item disagrees on 19% of 276 (it often names an edition item).
entries.decision: Bulk route: edition by rule (now incl. catalogue windows), work by lean Sonnet for every work, a Wikidata work-item date stored only where it meets the model's window, the author's Wikidata window as prompt context and a recorded check. #6721.

entries.question: Yigdzin read of the Tibetan pages the earlier runs missed: 76,197 of 82,193 written
entries.verdict: Yigdzin read 82,193 withheld or unread pages on live Tibetan books; 76,197 passed v4 + first-ocr-guard + 150 syllables and are written, 0 invented in 15 opened against the image, €24.68 GPU.
entries.decision: Scope matcher takes the Gemini Flash family and the gate treats Indic letters as neutral (PR #6709); 76,197 pages served from Yigdzin (run yigdzin-leaf-2026-10-14-rest)

entries.question: Yigdzin read of the hidden Tibetan books: 5,145 of 12,214 candidate pages written
entries.verdict: Yigdzin read 6,933 empty pages in hidden Tibetan books; 5,145 passed v4 + first-ocr-guard + 150 syllables and are written, 0 invented in 7 opened against the image, €1.50 GPU.
entries.decision: Same read and write rule as yigdzin-rest-4523, run on the hidden Tibetan books (DECISION default, parent session 2026-10-14); 5,145 pages served from Yigdzin (run yigdzin-leaf-2026-10-14-hidden)

entries.question: Does Gemini's review pass the Opus-corrected withheld table pages for serving?
entries.verdict: NO-GO under the gate as written: Gemini 3.8 Flash (high) called 23 of 100 Opus-corrected withheld table pages invented (23%, Wilson 95% 15.8–32.2%; gate ≤ 10), and caught 5 of 5 planted duplicated rows. Nothing was served. But the 5 invented calls opened against the image were all wrong: the span it called invented is printed on the page, most often in the rightmost column, which it reads as 'carried over from the preceding page'. The gate measures this reviewer's false alarms as much as Opus's inventions.
entries.decision: Serve nothing (#6561 gate). Whether to re-gate with a by-eye or reference check of the 23 calls is Derek's decision.

entries.question: Which translator for the Mayan-language books of #6559, and where do Sonnet and flash-lite stand?
entries.verdict: On 20 Mayan-language pages (4 books), Gemini 3.8 Flash Low through the CLI translates better than Opus under both judges, order-averaged: a Gemini 3.8 Flash High judge gives +1.60 and an Opus judge gives +0.38. Opus fails on the 1846 Yucatec sermons and leads only on the Kaqchikel manuscript. On the 30 Nahuatl pages of 2026-10-13, Opus and Gemini tie under the Opus judge (−0.07). Sonnet and gemini-3.1-flash-lite trail both by 1–3 points in every language, and lite OCR trails the stored Opus OCR by 1.3.
entries.decision: Maya lane: Gemini 3.8 Flash Low, by the 2026-10-14 brief's rule (Opus only if both judges put it ahead). Sonnet and flash-lite are rejected for these languages.

entries.question: Does Gemini 4 Argon (low, through the CLI) move the needle where our readers fail?
entries.verdict: Gemini 4 Argon low (CLI) beats 3.8 Flash only on Syriac print (+13 points a page), and is the same on Syriac manuscripts, Chinese manuscripts and print, and Greek. It loses to Kraken on both Syriac panels and to Yigdzin on Tibetan. It ties PaddleOCR-VL on Chinese manuscripts with no failed reads. Its Syriac manuscript failures are canonical-text substitution: the right book, the wrong passage.

entries.question: Does more context than the catalogue help a model date a work?
entries.verdict: For the WORK date, catalogue fields alone (85.9%) do as well as adding the opening leaves (85.4%) or a summary/translated pages (84.7%), n=318 Wikidata gold; one alternative wording (conventional year, narrowest window) lowers the mean interval score 824→525 at the same coverage.
entries.decision: No context added for work dates; leaves stay for edition dates (title-page evidence). Route decision pending the paid-vs-CLI question on #6721.

entries.question: Can a CLI model date works and editions well enough to write them library-wide?
entries.verdict: Sonnet 5.5 (agy, low effort, 15 books per call) dates the work inside its window on 87.4% of high/medium rows against Wikidata (n=247 of 318) and reads 94.6% of printed imprints blind (n=130); Haiku 77%, GPT-OSS 64% and the 2026 enrichment rows 67% fail the 85% bar.
entries.decision: Library-wide dating (#6721) runs on agy claude-sonnet-5-5-low, batched 15; Gemini arms pending their quota reset

entries.question: How many books carry a whole-page English shift, and can numbers find it where case cannot?
entries.verdict: Whole-page English shifts are not confined to Śakuntalā: a number-vote detector flags 80 of 5,903 caseless-label books and 19 of 300 other books (6.3%, 4.1 to 9.7), and 12 of 20 flagged pages opened as scans carry a neighbour's English; one was written by the chained Batch lane on 2026-10-05, after the parser guards.

entries.question: Can Gemini 3.8 Flash correct the Yigdzin OCR of the BL Kangyurs?
entries.verdict: Gemini 3.8 Flash LOW corrects the Yigdzin read better than Opus: 0.968 vs Derge (+0.023 [0.016, 0.030] over the served read; +0.008 [0.002, 0.015] over Opus correct), 30 of 30 folios better, 0 worse, 3 of 30 planted errors left (Opus 14). Opus finds 13 of its 344 toward-Derge changes not on the leaf (Opus correct: 25 of 197). The mi→myi recitation that disqualified Pro appears once: 2 changes on seq 23, checked by eye (Pro: 21). Flash HIGH is worse than LOW: +0.008, 4 folios returned unchanged, 17 of 30 plants left.

entries.question: Can Sonnet or Haiku correct a draft as well as Opus, on the #6561 Chinese pages and the #6560 Tibetan folios?
entries.verdict: Neither Sonnet nor Haiku corrects a draft as well as Opus. On the 40 Paddle table pages Sonnet gains half of what Opus gains (mean CER 7.6% vs 5.1%; +2.5 pt [+1.5, +3.6] against Opus) and makes 10 pages worse where Opus makes 1. On the 30 Tibetan folios Sonnet returns the draft unchanged on 29 and leaves 28 of 30 planted errors. Haiku rewrites about a fifth of the Chinese pages into scrambled tables or loops (mean CER 35% on tables) and duplicates text on 2 Tibetan folios. Sonnet costs about half of Opus per page on the subscription, not a small fraction.
entries.decision: table-correct-6561 stays on Opus; Tibetan correction does not move to Sonnet or Haiku (#6667)

entries.question: What share of the pages readers are served carries a serious error, by lane?
entries.verdict: One random served page from each of 184 books, read against the image by Opus: a serious error on 62 (34%, 95% CI 27–41%), 22% frame-weighted; whole passages not of the leaf, confirmed by eye, on 10 (5%, 3–10%), all contained. Manuscripts 64% vs print 22%. Ten books per stratum is too few to rank lanes.
entries.decision: 10 pages contained (held + withheld, #6691); 200 book_checks rows (served-audit v1)

entries.question: Does "short source, long English" find title leaves that were given a chapter?
entries.verdict: A short source with a long English body marks text that is not on the leaf: the rule fires on 7 of 7 Tengyur title leaves withheld by eye, on 5 of 208 short-source pages in a random draw (all 5 wrong by text), and on 537 of 9,474 short-source title pages (20 of 20 sampled wrong by text, 5 of 5 opened wrong by eye).
entries.decision: assessTranslationHealth refuses such a page as `recited` (#6297)

entries.question: Quality sprint round 2: what does a random draw of the public library look like, and which defect classes repeat across rounds?
entries.verdict: Public frame, 10 random books: 4 of 30 pages carry a serious error (3 of 9 served books); nothing invented, no wrong leaf. Misread-carried-into-English (O6) is the one class in 3 or more books across rounds 1 and 2.

entries.question: Is Opus a better translator than Gemini 3.8 Flash Low on the #6559 Nahuatl books?
entries.verdict: On 30 Nahuatl pages (3 books), a blind Gemini 3.8 Flash High judge scored Opus 3.58 and Gemini 3.8 Flash Low 3.95 for translation fidelity (−0.37, 95% CI −0.77 to +0.03), averaged over both A/B orders. Opus is not better under this judge. The judge's position bias (about ±0.6) is larger than the gap, and it is the same family as one arm.

entries.question: Does Opus translation hold its quality at 10 pages per call?
entries.verdict: Opus at 10 pages per call scores 0.30 lower than Opus at 1 page per call (−0.30 [−0.54, −0.08], 50 pages, cross-family judge). It is worse on 23 pages and better on 10. The loss is mostly small omissions, not text moved between pages. It costs about 2.7× less subscription usage per page (list-equivalent).
entries.decision: Keep Opus translation at 1 page per call where it is routed (#6545). Do not use 10 pages per call to stretch Opus capacity unless a same-round check shows it still beats 3.8 Flash (#6690).

entries.question: Does the Opus read pass the calibration gate ?
entries.verdict: Opus reads through claude-ocr.mjs scored 3.80 / 5 mean fidelity from a blind Gemini 3.8 Flash High judge (15 pages, 3 books), just under the 4.0 gate; the judge caught 3 of 3 planted errors, and its one 'invented line' on a real page was a judge misreading, checked by eye.
entries.decision: Applied on Derek's call 2026-10-13: 11,843 Opus-read pages written to pages that were empty, books held (routing row nahuatl-mayan, #6559; gate rule for empty pages changed in PR #6670). Closed in #6688

entries.question: OCR route: does Opus correcting the stored text in place match lane B (Gemini read + Opus adjudication)?
entries.verdict: On 976 pages of 99 most-read non-English books (queue ranks 201–300), Opus correcting the stored text in place (arm B) beat lane B (Gemini 3.8 Flash read + Opus adjudication, arm A) under both blind judges and passed the preregistered rule: B made 1/196 (Opus) and 9/196 (Gemini 3.8 Flash high; 4.6%, book-clustered 95% CI 2.0–7.7%) of its changed pages worse, and was preferred to A 158–6 (Opus) and 148–21 (Gemini). B changes far more pages (809 vs 189). But B's 40-write audit STOPPED: Gemini 3/40 worse (Opus 0/40), so nothing was written.
entries.decision: Derek 2026-10-14 (#6694): B (Opus correcting in place) is the OCR route for the rest of queue-next-1000, Greek excepted (Greek stays on lane A); q300 B applied over the 3/40 audit stop with the 3 disputed Greek pages excluded: 600 written, 17 refused by the shared-words guard

entries.question: Lane B at scale: what does a Gemini second read plus Opus adjudication change on 150 of the most-read non-English books?
entries.verdict: Lane B at scale (main200, 150 of the most-read non-English books, 1,491 pages): a Gemini CLI second read adjudicated by Opus against the image wrote 214 pages (14%) and passed both blind write audits (Opus 0 worse of 78; Gemini 3.8 high 4 worse of 78, each an Opus/Gemini disagreement about the leaf, not written). Opus kept the stored read on 543 pages and left 427 residual, so the second read changed the served text on about one page in seven. 34 pages in 12 books were contained, including a whole book (Vitruvius) serving another leaf's text with a growing offset.
entries.decision: Lane B stays the OCR repair route for the most-read non-English books under Derek's 2026-10-11 default (#6553). Not yet measured, and the next routing question: whether Opus correcting the stored text against the image (one call per page, Gemini blind-checking a sample) matches this two-read lane — #6561 found correct-in-place beat a fresh read on Paddle Chinese, but only there. Run side by side on the same pages before switching.

entries.question: Which printed page-number breaks are missing leaves, which are copies, which are nothing?
entries.verdict: Of 20,933 printed page-number breaks, 2,271 have text missing across them (a blind read, 344 of 350 control calls right), 2,155 are copies the 0.9 Dice missed, 1,452 are misnumbering with continuous text; 9,267 stay unsorted and 4,693 are numbers too far apart to judge.

entries.question: Can Jev rank pages for a topic rubric, as a search engine in front of the judge?
entries.verdict: Jev ranks a topic rubric (animism) against the flash-lite screen + Gemini CLI judge at AUC 0.92 (0.87 on the hard judged set); at 0.5 it keeps 96% of confirmed passages and flags 2.1% of random pages, for $0.00005 a page.
entries.decision: Jev is usable as a cheap topic ranker in front of the two-pass instrument; it does not replace the judge, and its scores are not rates.

entries.question: Can Opus or Gemini 3.1 Pro correct the Yigdzin OCR of the BL Kangyurs, and is correct or redo better?
entries.verdict: Correcting the Yigdzin read helps (Opus +0.015 [0.008, 0.022] syllable identity vs Derge, 0 of 30 folios worse; Pro +0.020 [0.011, 0.029], 5 worse); re-reading from the image is far worse (Opus 0.70, Pro 0.50 vs 0.945): both invent fluent text that is not on the leaf. Opus under-corrects (47% of planted errors survive); Pro writes the reference edition's spelling over the leaf (mi→myi on 2 folios).
entries.decision: Re-reading Tibetan from the image is ruled out (routing rows tibetan, correct-not-redo). For Derek on #6688, default: no Opus correction pass yet (+1.5 points, 47% of planted errors left); spend the Opus quota on the Chinese table pages first

entries.question: Stale Siku retranslation, pilot and 30-page review
entries.verdict: The 300-page pilot of the stale-Siku retranslation (3.8 Flash via the CLI, production prompt, CER < 0.1) wrote 289 pages with 0 failed reads. On 30 random written pages the new English beats the stored English under both blind judges (Opus 0.97 → 0.17 material errors per page, Gemini 3.1 Pro 2.77 → 1.53), but Pro's 1.53 fails the pre-registered GO bar of ≤ 0.5. Most of Pro's material errors cite Chinese the Paddle reading does not have, so they come from the reading, not the translation. The run stopped at the pilot.

entries.question: Stale Siku English: check the new Paddle reading, then retranslate or diff-correct?
entries.verdict: Below an old-vs-new CER of 0.1, the new Paddle reading is usually right (2 of 16 pages have a material OCR error), and a fresh 3.8 Flash translation beats the stored English on every judged page where they differ, under both judges (Opus 1.68 → 0.00 material errors per page, Gemini 3.1 Pro 4.16 → 1.05, n = 19). At CER ≥ 0.1 the Paddle reading itself has a material error on 19 of 24 pages, so retranslating from it would carry those errors into the English. Diff-scoped correction fixed much less than retranslation (Opus 0.95, Pro 2.74), because most errors in the stored English come from the translation, not from the old reading. Both judges caught 16 of 16 planted errors.

entries.question: Do three published LLM transcription results reproduce through our $0 CLI route?
entries.verdict: Greif et al. replicates through our CLI route: Gemini 3.1 Pro via agy reads the 30 city-directory pages at 0.79% normalised CER (their API run 0.77%; paired difference +0.02 points, 95% CI −0.03 to +0.07) and corrects the Transkribus draft to 0.75% (theirs 0.80%). The three Humphries results are not testable: their 50-document set is unpublished. On the nearest public set, Bentham R0 (33 pages), reader disagreement flagged 10% of words and covered 59% of Pro's errors (theirs 4% / 76%). A model resolver did not beat the primary reader except on the one page Pro invented.
entries.decision: No routing change. For #6544: the CLI route costs nothing measurable on Pro; Gemini CLI reads of handwriting need the restart/duplicate check and the view_file log, because 5 of 66 Gemini reads wrote the page twice and 1 was invented without the image being opened.

entries.question: Pro with full thinking, Opus, and correcting the stored English, against 3.8 Flash, in the five lowest-scoring languages
entries.verdict: 3.1 Pro with full thinking does not beat 3.8 Flash given the same prompt (Opus judge −0.02 [−0.23, +0.19], 53 pages). Opus as a translator beats 3.8 Flash in all five languages under the cross-family Pro judge (+0.47 to +0.52). Correcting the stored English helps, but less than retranslating with Opus.
entries.decision: Route Persian, Sanskrit, Chinese, Greek and Hebrew translation to Opus (claude -p) where subscription capacity allows; otherwise keep 3.8 Flash. Not 3.1 Pro. No correction pass (#6545)

entries.question: Paddle Chinese table pages: withhold the detector's 4,379, then can Opus re-read them?
entries.verdict: NO-GO on the pre-set gate. On 100 withheld Paddle table/diagram pages (one per book), the Gemini 3.8 Flash reviewer found invented text in 23 of Opus's 100 reads (Wilson 95% 16–32%, gate ≤ 10%). It caught all 5 planted controls. Where a Kanripo leaf aligns, though, the leaf prints the reviewer's main 'invented' span on 5 of 12 such pages, so the true rate is lower. Two corrected estimates, 18% and about 13%, are both still above 10%. Against Kanripo, Opus over-writes printed characters 91 times where Paddle does 218 (48 pages).
entries.decision: Opus-by-image not adopted as the unattended reader for Paddle table pages; the 4,379 stay withheld (#6388)

entries.question: Paddle Chinese: correct flagged pages or re-read them, with which model, and does it fit the quotas?
entries.verdict: On Paddle's Chinese pages, Opus correcting Paddle's draft beats both Paddle and an Opus re-read. On the 40 withheld table pages: median CER 4.0% against Paddle 6.4% and Opus redo 5.8%, better on 31 pages and worse on 1. On ordinary pages the gain is small (−1.0 pt on 30 random pages, 2 made worse) and sits on the pages the lane's own Kanripo screen already scores below 0.95 dice. Every corrector left at most 1 of 30 planted errors. 3.1 Pro makes 21 of 40 table pages worse. A cross-family read-off disputes 26–36% of every arm's edits toward Kanripo, Opus included, and the two judges agree on only 70% of items, so it does not separate the arms. Opus quota, not speed, bounds the lane: the 4,379 table pages take about 1 account-week, dice < 0.90 (414K pages) about 97, the whole 1.57M lane about 369.
entries.decision: Opus corrects Paddle's draft on the flagged table pages (job table-correct-6561; routing rows chinese-tables and correct-not-redo). Closed in #6688

entries.question: Can a $0 CLI lane read the new Nahuatl and Mayan-language books ?
entries.verdict: Through the CLI, Gemini 3.1 Pro reads Nahuatl and Mayan-language pages better than 3.8 Flash (Opus-judged mean 4.1 vs 3.5 Nahuatl, 4.3 vs 3.75 Mayan, of 5); 3.8 Flash flattens colonial Maya letters (24 normalisations on 8 pages).
entries.decision: The 3.1 Pro CLI lane was not taken (withdrawn from agy 2026-10-12); Derek chose Opus on 2026-10-12 (routing row nahuatl-mayan). Closed in #6688

entries.question: Does a thinking Gemini read manuscripts better than Flash-Lite, and does a second model help?
entries.verdict: On 76 expert-transcribed manuscript pages (Set A), every reader that thinks beats production Flash-Lite, by 4.7 to 6.8 points of mean page CER: 3.1 Pro −4.7 [−6.9, −2.6], 3.8 Flash low −4.7, 3.8 Flash high −5.4, and Opus −6.8 [−9.6, −4.0]. Thinking level does not matter (3.8 high − low −1.8 [−4.1, +0.1]). Opus is the best single reader on Set A (−3.3 [−5.9, −0.9] against Pro), but on our own manuscripts (Set B, 40 pages, model-keyed, DIRECTIONAL) its ranking against Pro flips with the key, and it writes `[?]` across Syriac and Turfan fragments. Pro beats Flash-Lite under all three Set B keys (−21.5 to −33.5 points). No two-model strategy beat the best single reader on Set A: Opus correcting Pro lands where Opus alone does (−1.0 [−2.6, +0.2]), and Pro correcting Opus changes nothing (+0.2). Anchoring is low: about 7% of planted draft errors survive either corrector.
entries.decision: Route manuscript and handwritten pages off Flash-Lite to Gemini 3.1 Pro through the CLI (moderate confidence). It fails least (3/76 restarted, against 9/76 refusals and cuts for 3.8 low) and is the only reader that wins under all three Set B keys. Do not route to 3.8 Flash: no gain over Pro on Set A, more refusals, and thinking level adds nothing. Not yet a two-model pipeline: an Opus correction pass helps only on noisy Pro drafts (−11.6 points on the noisiest tertile, −0.1 on the clean one), so route the pass by draft noise if it is built at all.

entries.question: Failed reads are counted, not scored : the OCR Pareto measures quality only where an engine read
entries.verdict: A read that failed (the copy filter cut it, another refusal, an empty reply, a timeout) is now counted as 'did not read' and not scored, for every engine. On Latin print, 3.7 and 3.8 Flash through the CLI lose 3 of 44 pages to the copy filter; on the 41 they read they are 2.6 to 2.7 points a page better than Flash-Lite. Two rows are flagged partly measured (CLI 3.7/3.8 on German/French, 7 of 22 unread), and DeepSeek-OCR on Greek (41 of 109 empty).

entries.question: Estimator v1: do the four fixes named in v0 make its predictions hold across judging instruments? — for differences between arms, yes; for levels, no: #6545 came in 0.4 below on the best-measured cells
entries.verdict: Estimator v1 (ordinal, round spread per instrument class, four chains) covers held-out experiments at 0.92 (v0 0.90; 330 cells) and held-out packet instruments at 0.85 (v0 0.74; 62 cells). In the preregistered #6545 test it covered 9 of 12 panel means (v0 8) and 7 of 8 differences between arms; the two best-measured cells came in 0.4 below the prediction.
entries.decision: Ready for the planner on differences between arms inside one judging round. Not ready on levels across judging rounds, and not for the router (#6557)

entries.question: Can the translation evidence we already hold be pooled into one estimator that predicts tests before they run? — yes, inside the #6182 setup; not yet across instruments
entries.verdict: A pooled hierarchical model of 19,271 judged scores predicts held-out experiments at 90% coverage 0.90 (330 cells) and the best model per language 61/66 times. It is overconfident across instrument types and for a model seen in one script family only.
entries.decision: Trust enough to extend to OCR. The planner waits until #6545 scores the preregistered prediction (#6557)

entries.question: Can two stored reads of a page by different engines find silently dropped lines?
entries.verdict: Comparing two stored reads by different engines flags a run of 5+ words on 12,431 of 120,577 pages (66 of 990 books at one page per book); 12 of 15 flags judged by eye were real dropped text, 10 of them dropped by flash-lite.

entries.question: Do an Opus reader and a Gemini reader agree, kind by kind, on the same 30 pages?
entries.verdict: Half run: Opus read all 33 pages and caught 3 of 3 planted controls with the right kind. The Gemini half did not run (the agy CLI is on the main box only, and that box took no jobs), so there is no kappa and 'convergent' is still not a validated reliability claim.
entries.decision: none yet: finish with scripts/eval/cross-family-6203/finish-gemini.sh on the main box, then read kappa per kind (#6203, #6420)

entries.question: Fixing the Gemini CLI OCR route by iteration : markers + a tool gate put 3.7 / 3.8 Flash where the model is
entries.verdict: Through the CLI, 3.7 and 3.8 Flash were losing Latin and Early English pages to the route, not the model. Two changes fix it: an answer between markers, and a hook that refuses tools with a reason. On held-out pages, 3.8 low goes from 14 of 157 pages over half wrong to 1 of 161, and 3.8 high from 25 to 2.

entries.question: What does the served-text CER say once digits count? The 90 panel pages re-scored
entries.verdict: Keeping digits moves no panel stratum by more than 0.2 pt and 1 of 90 pages by more than 1 pt; the new digits-only channel finds 5.5% of 397 key digits wrong in Latin print and 0.8% of 4,370 in English print.
entries.decision: normalizeForScript v4 keeps digits in Latin-script text; the dashboard reports failures, median CER on pages with text, and a digits channel (#6203)

entries.question: Re-reading the 6,494 not-applicable Tengyur pages with a one-turn nudge, checked by two blind readers
entries.verdict: Re-read with the stage-1 call plus one nudge in the same conversation, 6,492 of the 6,494 not-applicable Tengyur pages passed the stage-2 gates and were applied (3,324 through the nudge). On 40 applied pages, two blind readers from different families (Opus; Gemini 3.7 Flash) each found fewer serious-error pages in the new English than in the old (Opus 3 vs 6, Gemini 3 vs 11 of 40). After Opus adjudicated the 8 split pages against the image, the new English was preferred on 35, the old on 4, and 1 was a tie. Both readers preferred the old on 2 of 40 (5%; stop line 10%), and those 2 pages got the old English back.
entries.decision: Applied (Derek, 2026-10-10, #6420: convergent AI check in place of a human read for a month).

entries.question: Is Syntagma musicum I really one leaf off between image and text?
entries.verdict: The Praetorius p.72 reference was pinned one leaf off; images were always correct, and after the 2026-10-01 re-OCR it belongs on page 130.
entries.decision: latin-la-praetorius-syntagma1-p120 re-pinned from page_number 131 to 130; it can rejoin cross-engine rollups (#4732)

entries.question: Paddle Chinese table and diagram pages: can a text rule find them, and which backup reader should read them?
entries.verdict: A text-only rule (strict loop screen or repeated-line run, AND a run/duplicate-line/low-diversity/table-title shape) flags 136 of 136 known invented Paddle table pages and 4,379 of 1,568,108 Paddle-written pages (0.28%). As a backup reader, Opus by image over-writes printed characters 39 times where Paddle does 145 (19 Kanripo-aligned pages) at equal CER; Gemini 3.1 Pro on agy is slower, emptier and worse ordered.
entries.decision: The table rule is in use: the 4,379 flagged Paddle pages are withheld (ocr.unreadable, paddle_table_6388) pending Opus correction (routing row chinese-tables, #6561). Closed in #6688

entries.question: Should the stale English on the Paddle-read Siku books be retranslated?
entries.verdict: Half or more of the stale English pages on the Paddle-read Siku Quanshu volumes carry a material error that the old OCR caused: 30 of the 44 resolved random books (68%, 95% CI 53–80%), and at least 30 of all 60 (50%) even if the 16 unresolved books are all clean. The two reviewers caught 5/5 planted errors each. The pre-registered rule (≥ 15%) says retranslate every stale page (75,701). Separately, 30% of the resolved random pages also carry a material error that a correct reading would not have prevented.

entries.question: Do our quality measures agree with a careful read of the image?
entries.verdict: The dashboard's served-text CER ranks catastrophes right (empty, truncated, invented pages) but below about 10% it ranks conventions, not errors (Spearman with a by-eye read 0.64 Latin, 0.40 Chinese MS, 0.47 English; 3 of the 9 worst-3 slots are exact pages), and it is blind to numbers: the Latin-script normaliser drops digits, so a table with 22 wrong cells scores 0. The #5826 gate held up (10/10 pages agree, 13/16 claims confirmed, 0 refuted; it under-calls dropped list entries). #6420 adjudications agree on 8/10 (Opus on Opus), with one missed set of invented plate labels.
entries.decision: Verdicts per measure in .claude/docs/measurement-validity.md and a validity field in src/data/quality-methods.json (#6203). No pipeline change.

entries.question: Is invented text the dominant failure a reader meets? A by-eye re-check of the cited pages and a uniform 40-book draw
entries.verdict: Invented text is not the dominant failure: 0 of 40 uniformly drawn served pages were invented (Wilson 0-8.8%); misread or mistranslated words in fluent English were on 12 of 40.
entries.decision: 29 pages in 8 books withheld by eye (#6420); measure notes posted to #6203

entries.question: Can the stored Gemini CLI outputs be rescued by cutting alone, and what does that do to the scores?
entries.verdict: Of 3,652 stored Gemini-CLI outputs, 591 fail the CLI checks. A cut-only rescue recovers 481 (461 by the deterministic extractor, 20 by a text-only CLI pass); 110 stay failed (87 empty or nothing left, 23 rejected by the verbatim guard). No translation arm needed rescue, so nothing is rejudged. On OCR the rescue lowers the 3.6 CLI CER on EEBO 0.325 → 0.068 and on Greek-ext 0.225 → 0.142, and does not fix 3.8: its failures are empties and recitation cuts.
entries.decision: Rescued records committed beside the raw outputs (results/cli-rescue-6523/); 6523c folds them into its single ocr-pareto.json rebuild. 3 Tengyur CLI pages cut; the write door refuses an announcing line that echoes the request.

entries.question: Is the CLI re-translation of the Tengyur Pramāṇa + Madhyamaka volumes safe to write over the stored English?
entries.verdict: Gemini 3.8 Flash via the CLI had half the stored English's serious errors on 21 pages read against the image (7 vs 14; reversals 2 vs 5), but two of seven volumes had a serious error the stored English lacks, so the preregistered gate stopped the apply. 23% of 'staged' replies were plan-mode chatter, not translations.
entries.decision: Derek waived the per-volume stop rule 2026-10-10; the 17,135 gate-passing pages were applied with provenance (scripts/maintenance/tengyur-cli-6361/apply.mjs, #6361)

entries.question: Does a re-run fix the 6,494 Tengyur pages the CLI run could not apply, and does a simple mode or prompt change?
entries.verdict: Re-run in the same mode and prompt, 53 of 100 not-applicable Tengyur pages failed again (40 denied tool, 13 plan replies), so a page's failure is per call, not per page. Without plan mode, or with an 'output only the translation, use no tool' suffix, 100 of 100 passed the stage-2 gates, but neither is the judged configuration: thinking dropped to zero on 94% (no plan mode) and 51% (suffix) of pages, against 35% of the applied pages.
entries.decision: Re-staging the 6,494 pages in arm C (plan mode + suffix) is a decision for Derek (#6361).

entries.question: PaddleOCR Chinese lane, random-sample QA by Opus and Gemini on the subscriptions
entries.verdict: On a random sample of 60 Siku Quanshu pages that PaddleOCR wrote, no page is unusable and none carries invented text. 51% are clean, 27% have minor errors and 22% have material errors (Opus and Gemini 3.8 reviewers, with Opus adjudicating where they disagree). Opus transcribing from the image cannot be told apart from Paddle against Kanripo; Gemini 3.8 Flash is 4 points worse.

entries.question: Three OCR routing questions on a random sample of our own books, provisional AI-consensus key
entries.verdict: Provisional (AI-consensus key): PaddleOCR beats flash-lite on Chinese manuscripts by 24.5 pts CER; on Latin print no engine can be told apart from flash-lite; on English print nothing beats it.
entries.decision: No routing change: the provisional verdicts agree with routing rows chinese-siku-manuscript (Paddle) and latin-script-print (Flash-Lite); the human key was not run. Closed in #6688

entries.question: #6388 Q1–Q3 again, on a model-adjudicated key (Amendment 2)
entries.verdict: Model-adjudicated key (no human), re-scored 2026-10-14 under normalizeForScript v4. Chinese manuscripts: Paddle over flash-lite (switch, unchanged). English: no change (unchanged). Latin: Sonnet vs flash-lite cannot be told apart on the adjudicated spans (v3 digit handling), but reads switch (+2.2 [+1.1, +3.4]) under v4, where 71 digit-bearing Latin spans have no adjudication yet.

entries.question: Can a Gemini CLI second read, adjudicated by Opus against the image, safely repair the OCR of the most-read non-English books?
entries.verdict: On the 50 most-read non-English books, Opus reading the image judged the served OCR seriously wrong on 121 of 283 adjudicated gate pages (43%, Wilson 37–49%; Greek 38/48, Arabic 14/20, Chinese 19/30, Latin 44/144, German 6/37). A Gemini 3.7 Flash CLI second read is the better text on 51 pages, but the preregistered gate stopped the writes: Gemini 3.8 judged 3 of 40 staged writes worse (Opus 0 of 40), and one of the three is an auditor error checked by eye. CER agreement is not acceptance: 12 of 30 pages with CER < 0.01 still needed a fix.
entries.decision: Nothing written. 19 pages contained (13 gate, 6 calibration), incl. a whole-book wrong-leaf shift (illustrated Tang tales, 10 of 10 pages). Scaling lane B and applying the 51 staged writes is a decision for Derek (#6420).

entries.question: What did applying the read-time leaked-markup repair to stored translations change?
entries.verdict: The read-time leaked-markup repair was applied to the stored English of 72,880 pages in 9,244 books; on 300 sampled pages the reader output is identical before and after.
entries.decision: applied to Mongo and the Supabase pages mirror with page_revisions undo rows; search snippet column left out (Derek, 2026-10-10, #5700)

entries.question: Can Gemini through the CLI do the shelf reviewer's job? A 16-page feasibility pilot : it runs, one page per call
entries.verdict: Gemini through the CLI can run the shelf-reviewer brief: 16/16 pages per arm, no empties, blocks or schema failures; one call per page, since the four-image book call thins the reading.

entries.question: OCR Pareto, Part A: Gemini 3.8 Flash through the CLI on the 908 preregistered pages — it beats Flash-Lite on Greek, Chinese and Syriac manuscript, never 3 Flash; the CLI fails ~6 % of pages in ways the API arms don't
entries.verdict: 3.8 Flash through the CLI beats Flash-Lite on Greek, Chinese and Syriac manuscript, never 3 Flash; about 6% of CLI pages fail in ways the API does not (empties, blocks, prose refusals).

entries.question: OCR Pareto, Amendment 2: Gemini 3.7 and 3.6 Flash through the CLI on 555 pages — 3.7 reads as well as 3.8 and ties 3 Flash; 3.6 is worse; no decision changes
entries.verdict: 3.7 Flash CLI beats lite on Greek, Chinese and Syriac manuscript and ties 3 Flash, as 3.8 does; 3.6 is worse than 3.8 on four charts and loops; the CLI adds a third failure, the plan note.

entries.question: OCR Pareto, Amendment 3: is 3.8 Flash CLI's gap to 3 Flash on Latin and Early English the model, or the route? — mostly the route: a second read at the same low level closes most of it, high effort does not help
entries.verdict: 3.8 Flash CLI's gap to 3 Flash on Latin and Early English print is mostly the CLI route's failed replies, which vary run to run; a same-level repeat closes most of it and high effort does not help.

entries.question: Latin OCR backlog: Gemini 3.7 Flash through the CLI against production flash-lite on 299 queue pages
entries.verdict: On real Latin queue pages readers prefer 3.7 Flash CLI over flash-lite on 14/15 gothic and 17/22 roman pages; lite loops on 4/46 gothic and reads long-s as f; gothic is about 7% of the queue.
entries.decision: No routing change. For Derek on #6688, default: Latin print stays on Flash-Lite (routing row latin-script-print); gothic type is re-tested on 3.8 Flash CLI with the fixed route (#6523) before any move, since 3.7 was withdrawn from agy on 2026-10-12

entries.question: Does a Sonnet check-and-revise flow beat one-shot Gemini 3.8 Flash (CLI) on the canon set, and at what subscription cost?
entries.verdict: No verdict: the re-judged C38 anchor moved −0.12, past the 0.10 tolerance. Descriptively a Sonnet check on a Gemini draft adds +0.10 [+0.05, +0.16] fidelity and almost never worsens a page.

entries.question: Which right-to-left and CJK books are stored in the wrong page order, and what would a repair move? — 50 of 60 confirmed by image
entries.verdict: 50 of 60 flagged right-to-left and CJK books are confirmed out of reading order by image (26 whole-book descending, 17 one part, 6 pair-swapped, 1 swap); 10 are false positives.

entries.question: Printed Syriac on the Pareto page: which reader, and is the Kraken text good enough to translate from? — directional; translations stay withheld
entries.verdict: Kraken OmniSyr reads printed Syriac best (CER 0.130), but translating its text costs 1.33 fidelity points and 12 vs 5 reversal pages: keep those translations withheld; OCR lever is a Kraken fine-tune.
entries.decision: Kraken-read English stays withheld (no change); the Kraken fine-tune spend (#5730) is unjudged, for Derek

entries.question: Printed Syriac: Gemini 3.7 Flash and 3.6 Flash through the CLI, and 3.8 Flash's full repeat read — directional; neither decision changes
entries.verdict: On printed Syriac, 3.7 Flash CLI reads at CER 0.426 and 3.6 at 0.520 against the Kraken lane's 0.130; Kraken-text translations stay outside the floor under every tier; neither decision changes.

entries.question: Can the second-reader harness be trusted before it reads a real page?
entries.verdict: A synthetic 40-book run found four harness bugs (matching, planting, sealing, blinding), fixed before any real read; --allowedTools does not restrict a headless reader, --restricted does.
entries.decision: Harness fixed, synthetic suite runs in CI (35 tests); the calibration runner refuses a CLI without --restricted (#6338)

entries.question: Pareto charts: do the sampled pages suit the measure?
entries.verdict: 43 Pareto panel pages (21 translation, 22 OCR) do not suit the measure; without them order and frontier hold in 21/25 translation and 10/13 OCR panels; Chinese #6182 and print OCR unfit to rank.
entries.decision: The 43 pages are dropped from /quality/pareto with limit notes on each panel (PR #6309); T5 bar now holds for 3.8 Flash, not 3.7

entries.question: Does the Antigravity-CLI arm match the API outside Tibetan? 365 reference pages, 14 languages — gate FAILED (reversals), fidelity the same
entries.verdict: Gate failed: CLI fidelity equals the API's (pooled −0.02 [−0.07, +0.03]) but the CLI reversed sense on 26 pages vs 19; Greek, T4, T5 and the pool fail, Latin and T3 pass.
entries.decision: Preregistered gate failed on reversals: the CLI is not declared equal to the API outside Tibetan (#6331)

entries.question: Can the Tengyur re-translation run through the Antigravity CLI (subscription) instead of the API? — gate PASSED
entries.verdict: The CLI arm cannot be told from the API on 58 Tengyur sides: C38 − G38 +0.06 [−0.10, +0.23], inversion sides 2 vs 3; both beat production by about 0.4–0.5; gate passed.
entries.decision: Tengyur re-translation runs through the CLI, not the API (Derek 2026-10-08, #6361); writing it to pages is still gated

entries.question: Does the Antigravity-CLI arm hold up on the 113 fresh 84000 Tengyur sides? — gate PASSED
entries.verdict: Gemini 3.8 Flash through the CLI matches the API on 113 fresh Tengyur sides against 84000: C38 − G38 +0.03 [−0.13, +0.18], inversion sides 3 vs 2; gate passed.
entries.decision: Tengyur re-translation runs through the CLI, not the API (Derek 2026-10-08, #6361); writing it to pages is still gated

entries.question: Translation on subscriptions only: Claude Sonnet (subagents) or Gemini 3.8 Flash (Antigravity CLI)? — Gemini, in every pool
entries.verdict: Claude Sonnet on the subscription scores below Gemini 3.8 Flash in every pool (pooled −0.16 [−0.22, −0.09]; Tengyur −0.35) with 2.6x the reversal pages; Haiku is far worse.
entries.decision: No Claude translation route; subscription routing goes to Gemini 3.8 Flash CLI (#6331, PR #6350); panels published in PR #6349

entries.question: Which subscription route translates the typed Chinese canon, Sanskrit and Pali well enough to run the canon gap on?
entries.verdict: Gemini 3.8 Flash via the CLI is the route for Chinese, Sanskrit and Pali and clears the good-enough bar (fidelity 4.31 / 4.39 / 4.67); Sonnet is never shown better.
entries.decision: Route recommended in the #6331 decision table (PR #6350); running the canon gap on the CLI waits on the subscription-plan decision

entries.question: Chinese canon reference set and the Sanskrit/Pali extension — set built, Sonnet arm run, nothing judged yet
entries.verdict: Built a 138-unit reference set (75 typed Chinese canon passages, 23 Sanskrit, 40 Pali pages), each with a fit-checked open English (132 same, 7 minor); Sonnet arm run, nothing judged yet.

entries.question: Verse memory, round 2: whole verse blocks only — gate FAILED, no write
entries.verdict: Whole-block verse memory qualifies on only 12 pages; the 8 fresh ones read by eye against the Tibetan: 6 better, 1 same, 1 worse, so the gate (0 worse) failed and nothing was written.
entries.decision: No write: the verse-memory gate failed twice and --round=2 --apply throws (#6141, PR #6166)

entries.question: Does a tradition-aware re-rank put more traditions in the first ten results without losing known items?
entries.verdict: A quota-2 re-rank with a 0.02 margin raises relevant traditions in the top 10 from 1.68 to 1.88 (production families 2.84 to 4.16) with known-item recall@10 unchanged.
entries.decision: diversify (src/lib/search/diversity.ts) shipped in concept and Librarian search with the default policy (#3514, #3895)

entries.question: Tengyur weak sections (Pramāṇa, Madhyamaka, Vinaya, Jātaka): does context or a stronger model fix the reversals?
entries.verdict: Neither context nor Gemini 3.1 Pro clears the bar: context lowers reference fidelity (-0.14); Pro's reviewer gain (38 vs 63 per 100) came from a failed gate and the references do not confirm it.
entries.decision: No context and no Pro re-translation; instrument failed its gate (#6121)

entries.question: Tengyur: what does each section read like, and can one reviewed rendering per much-quoted root verse replace the scattered page-by-page ones?
entries.verdict: The verse memory failed its gate: of 20 proposed replacements read against the Tibetan, 15 were better, 2 no better and 3 worse (bar 18 and 0), all from span mapping.
entries.decision: No write; round 2 (whole blocks only) also failed its gate (#6141)

entries.question: Tengyur: does gemini-3.8-flash's gain replicate on fresh texts, and where does each Gemini model sit on cost × fidelity?
entries.verdict: G38's gain replicates on 113 fresh 84000 sides (+0.15, p = 0.0005) and 70 fresh weak-section pages (findings 61 to 29 per 100); +0.23 over production misses 0.25, so no default switch.
entries.decision: Pramana + Madhyamaka re-translation recommended, pending Derek; CLI run gated, nothing written (#6361); Tibetan default unchanged

entries.question: Tengyur weak sections, round 2: do newer models (Gemini 3.8 / 3.5 Flash, Opus) fix them?
entries.verdict: gemini-3.8-flash (+0.39) and Opus (+0.64) beat the stored Tengyur English on 58 reference sides and pass the rule on both texts; gemini-3.5-flash does not (-0.01).
entries.decision: Re-translating Pramana + Madhyamaka with G38 is pending Derek; the CLI run's apply gate stopped it, nothing written (#6361)

entries.question: Temperature and best-of-3 for translation, against published references
entries.verdict: No temperature passes the first-draw test (T0.2 +0.10 equals the floor); the two-draw contrast favours 0.2 or 0 by about 0.1 grade; best-of-3 gains +0.06 on the Tengyur at 3.6x cost.
entries.decision: Recommends explicit temperature 0 and no best-of-3; translate-worker.mjs unchanged, pending Derek (#6202)

entries.question: After the first word-form fix, which forms of a word still find a fraction of what their sibling finds?
entries.verdict: After the second word-form pass a typed form finds 0.98 of its best sibling's books, up from 0.54 (24 queries); the 13 non-Latin and control queries return the same ids.
entries.decision: Second-pass folding shipped in src/lib/search/word-forms.ts (#5517)

entries.question: Can a script run the shelf-overview reviewers instead of an interactive session, and how consistent are the reviewers when run again?
entries.verdict: Script-launched reviewers agree with the interactive run (serious-flag kappa 0.85-0.90) about as well as with themselves (0.92) at $0.15-0.20 a page; both preregistered conditions pass.
entries.decision: run-reviewers.sh adopted; shelf-overview skill step 3 now uses the runner (#6174)

entries.question: Do temperature samples find Sanskrit OCR errors as well as a second model family?
entries.verdict: Temperature samples share errors (Flash vs Flash phi 0.55) where Flash vs Pro is 0.09; a 5x Flash T1.0 vote reads 65% of 63 Sanskrit mark slots, 3x Pro 94%.
entries.decision: Temperature sampling not used as a detector or voter; recipe proposed as Pro decides, Flash and lite nominate (#6184)

entries.question: Is Pro's lead on Sanskrit marks the model or the prompt?
entries.verdict: Flash with Pro's plain prompt reads 79% of 63 Sanskrit mark slots against Pro's 90%, under the 85% bar: Pro's lead is the model, not the prompt.
entries.decision: By the preregistered rule 'Pro decides' stands for the Sanskrit tie-break; a Devanagari prompt clause is proposed for A/B (#6203)

entries.question: Which wrong page vectors cost search results, and are the e5 rows gone?
entries.verdict: Exactly 211,377 e5 rows in 1,402 books; after re-embedding 140,965 pages none remain on embeddable pages. Stale and OCR-before-translation vectors lose about 0.2 recall@10.
entries.decision: e5 rows re-embedded ($11.40); stale/OCR-before-translation re-embed deferred to #6221, archived-page rows to #6270

entries.question: Every language but Tibetan: which Gemini model sits on the cost × fidelity frontier, and is any worth a routing change?
entries.verdict: gemini-3.7-flash clears rule B over production for Latin (+0.45), Greek (+0.28) and Sanskrit/Pali/Chinese (+0.26, by 0.01); keep production for T3 vernaculars and Hebrew/Arabic/Persian.
entries.decision: Nothing re-routed as of 2026-10-10 (DEFAULT_MODEL still gemini-3-flash-preview); routing is Derek's call (#6182)
