entries.question: Can an English query find an untranslated Latin/German/French/Chinese page by meaning?
entries.verdict: Stored Gemini OCR vectors reach recall@10 0.93 vs e5-base 0.38 (BGE-M3 0.82 on a 3K sub-pool); the shared index, not the model, drops untranslated pages to 0.10.
entries.decision: No open-model backfill; Gemini OCR-tail embed approved and an original-text lane built behind SEARCH_UNTRANSLATED_LANE (#5729)

entries.question: Do the wave-1 OCR engines hold their place on each chart's FULL page set?
entries.verdict: Wave-1 ranks replicate on the full panels; only DeepSeek-OCR joins a frontier, as the cheapest and worst point. Sonnet 0.940 vs Flash 0.947 on Latin; open engines score 0 on Syriac.
entries.decision: Charts only (src/data/ocr-pareto.json), no routing change; Opus and Sonnet Greek/Syriac wait for credit (#6011)

entries.question: Shelf overview: the Nalanda–Indonesia–Tibet thread
entries.verdict: Frame-weighted, 16% of pages on four Nalanda-Java-Tibet shelves carry a serious error (4 books per shelf); OCR-dropped negations reverse the English in 5 books.
entries.decision: Filed #6184 with a negation-flip detector; Or. 1332 hidden and held; one date corrected

entries.question: Two cheap prototypes on the stored page vectors: does a picture find its passage, and can one page propose the same idea in other traditions?
entries.verdict: A centred emblem image vector ranks the right Atalanta fugiens passage first for 34 of 44 emblems (5 uncentred); a see-also list from a page finds a real parallel only 13 of 75 times.

entries.question: Can Jev, asked one English sentence at a time, screen translations for reversed meaning?
entries.verdict: Sentence-level Jev ranks judge-quoted reversals at AUC 0.84 and catches 21/21 planted flips, but about 96 of 100 flags would be false alarms; page AUC 0.72 at 2.7x D3's cost.
entries.decision: Not adopted; #6062 closed as a null result, reversals stay a task for the reference judges

entries.question: Can Jev screen served translations for omissions (source text left out of the English)?
entries.verdict: Jev is a weak omission screen: live AUC 0.75, and at the control threshold it flags at 68% precision but finds only 51 of 129 judged omissions (40%).
entries.decision: Not adopted as a screen; at most to order a by-eye review queue (#6061)

entries.question: Is each stored embedding the vector of its own text, by the model its row names?
entries.verdict: e5-base vectors stamped Gemini by a column default sit in 2.95% of translated books (about 205K rows); the 0.5-0.9 cosine band is stale source text, not a model fault.
entries.decision: Write-time e5 guard (#6189) and summary-prefix fix (#6194); the repair is logged in the follow-up 6175 entry

entries.question: Does the task prefix earn the $360 re-embed when the baseline is off the ceiling?
entries.verdict: On a 100K pool the prefix on both sides lifts cross-lingual R@10 0.58 to 0.97 but misses the bar on set B by one query (+0.039); query prefix alone and mixed stores lose.
entries.decision: No re-embed on this evidence; re-score with human-written set-B questions before deciding (#6170)

entries.question: Would a different embedding model, or a second original-language vector, find more of the right pages?
entries.verdict: No re-embed clears the bar: dual Gemini vectors gain nothing on B, Qwen3-8B wins A (+0.05) but ties B; 16% of stored vectors drift from their own text (cos < 0.9).
entries.decision: No new model or dual vectors; repair off-space and drifted rows instead (#6175)

entries.question: Which embedding unit, text and ranking put several traditions into the first ten results for a concept?
entries.verdict: A per-page concept abstract lane was the only index change to clear the bar: relevant traditions in the top ten 1.68 to 2.80 (+1.12 [0.60, 1.64]); chunks and query rewriting did not.
entries.decision: Concept lane stage 1 built (1,216 books) and serving search; corpus-wide pass held (#6173)

entries.question: Should page embeddings move to the GA model, the documented task prefix, or more dimensions?
entries.verdict: GA and preview embeddings are bit-identical; query prefix alone loses (B R@10 0.97 to 0.84); prefix on both sides helps but misses the bar at the ceiling; more dims gain nothing.
entries.decision: No prefix, no re-embed, stay at 768 dims; larger follow-up test run (#6170)

entries.question: Does the concept-abstract lane, built on 1,216 books, put more traditions in the first ten results than the page vectors?
entries.verdict: On the same 1,216 books the concept-abstract lane adds +0.60 [0.16, 1.00] relevant traditions in the top ten over page vectors, with no loss of precision; smaller than the pilot's +1.12.
entries.decision: Stage-1 abstract lane serves conceptPageSearch in /api/search; corpus-wide pass (~$530) waits for human-written queries (#6173)

entries.question: Can Clef or Jev decide a one-mark Sanskrit reading, independently of Gemini?
entries.verdict: Neither Clef (61% on 36 disputed one-mark Sanskrit slots, 22% order flips) nor Jev (39%) meets the 80% bar as an independent tie-break reader.
entries.decision: Neither adopted as the #6203 tie-break; it stays a person or a transcribing reader (#6203)

entries.question: Which engine reads Chinese print, measured against CBETA fitted to our own scans?
entries.verdict: Against CBETA fitted to our own scans, Gemini 3 Flash reads Chinese print at median Han CER 0.052 and Flash-Lite at 0.068 on 198 shared pages (54 books); Flash had no catastrophic page (CER > 0.5).

entries.question: Can flash-lite label every book's tradition from its catalogue record?
entries.verdict: Flash-lite labelled the tradition of all 109,006 books for $2.74; 27/30 right by eye, 3 arguable, 0 wrong; same family as the pilot's by-eye labels on every non-European shelf.
entries.decision: books.tradition stored on 109,006 books and used by the search tradition re-rank (#4773)

entries.question: Can the held BL terma and biography manuscripts be scored against a printed e-text? Almost never: 96% of served pages fall off every open reference
entries.verdict: No accuracy figure is possible for held terma/biography manuscripts: 96% of served pages retrieve no open e-text; the 6 on-index pages read at median identity 0.80.

entries.question: The 993 held BL Tibetan books with no reference (ritual, sādhana, astrology, local), read by eye per monastery: 9% serious pages (frame-weighted), 0 "don't show"
entries.verdict: The 993 held no-reference BL Tibetan books read by eye: 9% serious pages (frame-weighted), mostly in the English; 0 wrong leaves, 0 don't-show books, 25 of 28 show with caveat.

entries.question: Re-translating held BL Kangyur pages on the #4523 chained lane: no better than the English readers already have; worth it only where there is none
entries.verdict: Chained re-translation ties the stored flash-v13 English on held BL Kangyur pages (Opus 4.17 vs 4.22, 23 pages) and adds the only inversions; value is in the 26,440 pages with no English.
entries.decision: Do not re-translate the 168,815 pages with English; translating the 26,440 without English awaits Derek (#4523)

entries.question: Run 3: is our text in the public crawl, do models know what it says, and is it already online as text? Mostly not in the crawl; the content test failed its controls; three quarters already exist as raw OCR
entries.verdict: 85.5% of works have no passage of our text in the 2025 public crawls (weak: 64% sensitivity on our OCR); 73.8% already exist publicly as raw OCR; the content-knowledge test failed its controls.
entries.decision: Claim no crawl absence without the sensitivity clause and no content-knowledge claim (#6038)

entries.question: Run 2: can frontier models name the author of our works from the title? About half of distinct works: no. "About a third" is RETRACTED for works and holds only for volumes and pages
entries.verdict: For 52.2% [47.4-56.9] of identifiable works no frontier model names the author from the title; "about a third" is retracted for works and holds only for volumes (38.6%) and pages.
entries.decision: Public wording changed to about half of distinct works, a third of volumes (blog did-the-ai-read-this, #6038)

entries.question: Six untried OCR engines on the Pareto charts' own pages: does any of them beat Gemini?
entries.verdict: No untried engine beats Gemini 3 Flash outside the margin on any script; Qwen3-VL-8B (Chinese MS), Opus 5.5 (Greek), Sonnet 5.5 (early English) beat lite; none near Yigdzin on Tibetan.
entries.decision: No untried engine adopted: Gemini stays the reader for Latin-script and Greek print (routing rows latin-script-print, greek-print); wave 2 replicated it on the full panels (2026-10-07). Closed in #6688

entries.question: How often does a translation carry untagged words of ours, and at which stage do they come in? (source-grounded additions detector, #5982)
entries.verdict: 4.9% [3.3, 7.3] of 450 live pages carry an untagged addition the detector sees, almost all in pre-v10 translations (v13: 0/124); OCR also invents text on 4/86 typed-text pages.

entries.question: How many of our Latin and German pages can be checked against a human-typed text, and against a period English translation? DTA, CAMENA and EEBO-TCP as internal references
entries.verdict: DTA, CAMENA and EEBO-TCP give typed references for 754 of our books (107,252 aligned pages); 35/36 leaves right by eye, 30/38 same-edition claims hold; 211 works get a period English translation.

entries.question: How accurate is our Chinese and Pali transcription against typed editions, and can it be extrapolated to pages nobody checked?
entries.verdict: Typical body CER 3.3% (Paddle, Siku MS), 2.6% (Gemini, CBETA Chan), 4.7% (Pali vs VRI, mostly edition difference); a pooled model extrapolates within Chinese, not across scripts.

entries.question: Can a write-time rule tell a bracketed gloss after a <term> from the translator's supplied words?
entries.verdict: A bracket-after-term rule caught supplied words half the time; cut to brackets the sentence names as a term, it fires 0-2 times per ~12.5K stored pages, all glosses.
entries.decision: bracketDefinitionsToNotes runs in the translation write guard (translate-write, #5902)

entries.question: How many stored translations are the model talking about its job instead of the page? A model-free count
entries.verdict: At least 549 pages in 269 live books carry the model's reasoning or a chat reply as the translation (38/40 by eye); rare, clustered, still being written in Oct 2026.

entries.question: Does the translation get worse when the prompt stops asking for notes? (v13 with the notes instructions removed, #5919)
entries.verdict: Removing the notes instructions from v13 does not lower fidelity (+0.10 [-0.09, 0.29], 40 pages); reversals 1 vs 3 pages, omissions fall, 11% cheaper.
entries.decision: Default prompt unchanged; note-free translation plus a separate notes step recommended, not decided (#5919)

entries.question: How much of our transcription error is the prompt's own conventions, what is the rest, and does the prompt change it?
entries.verdict: Allowing only the conventions the OCR prompt asks for takes early-print CER from 6.6% to 5.5% (Latin) and 6.0% to 5.2% (English); what remains on early English is mostly ſ read as f and refusals, and the long-s retry prompt cuts refusals without adding modernisation.
entries.decision: /quality shows the three numbers per language (this PR); no prompt or routing change

entries.question: Can a model's definition stored inside <term> be moved to a <note> by rule, and what did applying it change?
entries.verdict: After four tightenings the term-definition rule passed 40/40 by eye and moved definitions out of <term> on 207,363 pages in 4,911 books (4.0%); 16 pages later corrected.
entries.decision: Class d_termdef applied with page_revisions undo rows; the same rule now drives the reader (#5901, #5908)

entries.question: Why does site search return so few books for a name, and does RRF fix concept queries?
entries.verdict: Rolling page hits up into books lifts site-search recall@10 from 0.32 to 0.42 and recall@20 from 0.23 to 0.38 on 30 queries; forcing RRF did nothing.
entries.decision: Book roll-up by facet count and kept passages shipped; RRF routing not shipped; the higher-scoring evidence-first ordering left as a decision (#5905)

entries.question: Does search take a visitor to a page they name, and what fixes it: the index or a name match?
entries.verdict: Navigational recall@3 on 42 fixed queries rose from 0.40 to 0.69 with a re-index and to 1.00 with a name match; 0.88 on 25 held-out queries.
entries.decision: Site index rebuilt from a derived page list plus a name match in /api/search/unified (src/lib/search/site-nav.ts, #5945)

entries.question: When several people share a surname, how many mentions sit on the wrong person?
entries.verdict: 56 of 120 sampled mentions (47%) on 12 bare-surname person records belong to someone else, from 0/10 (Gesner, Helmont) to 10/10 (Montanus).
entries.decision: Search name chooser built from full-name records only (src/lib/search/name-chooser.ts); Bacon repair dry-run followed (#5950)

entries.question: With 30 referenced books a language, does the Flash translation routing keep its place under the routing card?
entries.verdict: No language reverses: with 30 referenced books each, Flash beats Lite by +0.33 to +0.57; Hebrew, Arabic, Sanskrit, Pali meet the card; Persian stops at a census of 28.
entries.decision: Flash translation routing (PR #5740) kept; Persian census and Chinese as provisional pending Derek (#5873)

entries.question: What does an uncurated sample of the canon shelves look like, read against the page images?
entries.verdict: On 30 random canon-shelf books, 23% of pages (21/91) carry a serious error, driven by unreadable inputs, broken or misfiled books and modern editions rather than translation of clean prints.
entries.decision: 55 books hidden; arm added to the monthly audit; issues #5913, #5915, #5916, #5917 filed (#5914)

entries.question: Can a page the pipeline could not read be refused before translation, from the page document alone, without refusing legible pages?
entries.verdict: A pre-translation gate (strip shape, CJK/Devanagari density and fragment share, structure) refuses 0.21% of pages; by eye only 0.03% of pages refused are legible.
entries.decision: Gate ON in the translation worker and both Batch lanes, switch TRANSLATE_PRE_GATE=0 (scripts/lib/pre-translation-gate.mjs, #5915)

entries.question: Notes as their own layer, phases 1–2: is the note-free prompt safe on Flash-Lite, and can stored markup be parsed into text + annotations?
entries.verdict: On 40 Lite pages the note-free prompt is not less faithful than v13 (4.38 vs 4.24, P1 and P2 pass); a parser splits 800 stored pages into text and annotations exactly.
entries.decision: Cleared for Lite by rule but not switched (waits for #5942 phase 5); parser in src/lib/translation-layers.ts; phase-3 data model awaits Derek

entries.question: Does a post-generation grounding pass make Librarian answers cite what they claim?
entries.verdict: A post-generation grounding pass cut uncited claim units from 72% to 37%, unsupported quotes 7/81 to 2/64 and caption errors 11/29 to 0/32 at the same cost per turn.
entries.decision: Grounding pass, +/-1 neighbour pages and tool URL fixes are live in the Librarian (src/lib/embassy/grounding.ts, #5904)

entries.question: How many served translation pages carry each class of leaked markup, and which can a read-time rule fix? )
entries.verdict: A read-time repair changes 72,191 of 5.18M served translation pages (1.39%, 9,002 books); by-eye precision was 37/37 to 40/40 per class.
entries.decision: repairLeakedMarkup runs in the reader, stripEditorialWrappers and the EPUB/HTML export; the stored-text (A2) apply is proposed, not run

entries.question: Latin print on the GEX45: does an open engine beat flash-lite by century? Round 4 of #5660, random books: no. The flash models win, and lite plus a long-s post-pass is close behind
entries.verdict: No open engine beats the flash models on Latin print: 1500s lite+longs and flash+cal tie (0.076), 1600s flash+cal and 3.8-flash (0.068), lite 0.093; GLM trails.
entries.decision: No open engine adopted for Latin print and Latin stays off the GPU box (routing row latin-script-print, not-adopted list). The long-s post-pass is part of the one Latin decision for Derek on #6688

entries.question: Can Kraken fill the English pages Gemini refuses as RECITATION?
entries.verdict: Kraken reads the English pages Gemini refuses at median CER 0.009 but reproduces only 78.5% of digit strings (bar 90%), so the gate stopped and nothing was written.
entries.decision: Gate stopped; Derek chose option (b), GLM digit repair, re-gated in 2026-10-06-glm-digit-repair-4686.md

entries.question: Can Jev screen translated pages for untagged additions, in front of the Gemini detector?
entries.verdict: Jev separates planted additions (AUC 0.96) but real ones less well (AUC 0.81); as a pre-screen halving Gemini reads it keeps 16 of 22 true additions (73%).

entries.question: What happened when the lite-read printed Greek pages were re-read on Flash in production ?
entries.verdict: Flash re-read 110,164 of 119,978 lite-read Greek print pages at $0.0030 a page; 7.8% refused (RECITATION); by eye 2 inventions, diacritics lost on 1% (4% pre-1600).
entries.decision: Re-read kept in production, 11,608 pp retranslated; collectors join text parts (#5930); 25K-page retranslation and 1450-1599 release pending Derek

entries.question: Greek manuscripts: full Kraken read + edition fit on the five public-domain-edition codices
entries.verdict: Full Kraken reads carry both Proclus In Timaeum codices past the 80% bar (97.7% and 98.7% located against Schneider); the alchemical codices plateau near 48%, limited by the edition.
entries.decision: Nothing written. For Derek on #6688, default: do not write the two Proclus codices from the fitted edition; Greek manuscripts follow routing row manuscripts (Opus) once that is routed

entries.question: After gate 0: do Paddle (SKQS Chinese) and Yigdzin (Tibetan) invent text on the page TYPES a random gate under-samples, and can a $0 rule screen catch it?
entries.verdict: Paddle invents on table pages, so the Chinese lane stopped; a $0 first-OCR guard cuts served Yigdzin invention from 28% to 3% of a random one-per-book draw (by eye).
entries.decision: scripts/lib/first-ocr-guard.mjs shipped (PR #6007); Paddle's table invention is handled by the table rule and Opus correction (routing row chinese-tables). Closed in #6688

entries.question: Can the GPU OCR backlog (SKQS Chinese on Paddle, Tibetan on Yigdzin, Japanese on NDL) be run with quality gates, and which engine should read the SKQS manuscripts?
entries.verdict: Paddle reads SKQS manuscript pages best (median CER 0.132 vs Qwen3-VL 0.205, flash 0.304, lite 0.372); the Tibetan woodblock canary passed, and gate 0 stopped both backlog lanes.
entries.decision: PaddleOCR-VL over Qwen3-VL, Flash and Flash-Lite for Siku Quanshu manuscript pages (routing row chinese-siku-manuscript); Yigdzin stays the Tibetan reader (row tibetan). Closed in #6688

entries.question: Can GLM-OCR's numbers repair Kraken's read of the pages Gemini refuses?
entries.verdict: GLM-OCR digits lift Kraken's digit strings from 78.5% to 89.2% (body text 95.6%) with no CER loss, one number under the 90% bar, so the gate stopped.
entries.decision: Nothing written and #5969 stays blocked. For Derek on #6688, default: leave the 715 pages empty until the running heads pass 90%; they are refused pages (routing row refused-pages) and MinerU does not read pre-1820 print

entries.question: Which books in Eternity's traditions can we show a scholar today? A hand-picked curation check, not a rate
entries.verdict: Of 107 hand-picked books across nine traditions, two pages each: 43 show, 30 show with care, 34 fix first; a curation worklist, not a rate.
entries.decision: 3 books hidden, 4 records relabelled, translationReasoningLeak detector added (#6056)

entries.question: What does dropping role words from the edition_key surname do to the corpus?
entries.verdict: Dropping role words from the edition_key surname changes 1,275 keys (805 live), merges 5 same-printing pairs and splits none.
entries.decision: editionSurname drops role words (#6069); edition keys re-stamped 2026-10-06 with materialize-edition-keys.ts (4,283 books rows)

entries.question: How many duplicates do we still hold, where does the dedupe process lose them, and is the e-rara merge worth doing? (dedupe process review, #6019 part 3)
entries.verdict: About 1 live book in 13 (6/80, 7.5% [3.5-15.4]) has a same-edition copy the import keys miss; the e-rara merge is 13 groups, not 1,146.

entries.question: Moving "Bacon" mentions to Roger and Francis: applied, and how good each evidence tier was
entries.verdict: Read in full, the same-book tier was right on 143 of 163 Bacon moves (88%) and the note tier on 61 of 63; with by-eye fixes 340 mentions moved to Roger or Francis.
entries.decision: 340 mentions moved in production; by-eye verdicts outrank the tiers and every same-book and note proposal is read before an apply (#6024)

entries.question: Is "~40% of our books are new to AI" still true? About 45% of distinct works (a third of books) are not recognised by Gemini 3.1 Pro; the May self-familiarity detector does not survive its own controls
entries.verdict: Gemini 3.1 Pro does not recognise 45.0% [40.7-49.4] of 500 random works (about a third by books); the May self-familiarity detector fails its own controls.
entries.decision: Run 2 (PR #6089) retracted the works figure: quote 52.2% of works not named by any frontier model, about a third only by volumes

entries.question: Can an open OCR engine replace the Flash re-read, judged on the English?
entries.verdict: No script moves off the Flash re-read: Kraken on Greek print is undecided (+0.23 [-0.32, 0.73], n 11) and too slow; OpenITI models lose on Persian/Arabic print (-1.33).
entries.decision: Kraken and OpenITI base models not adopted; Flash re-read stays in the A5 plan; Sanskrit Vision arm needs a key (pending Derek, #5870)

entries.question: Did this week's quality decisions have enough evidence? An audit against the decision cards
entries.verdict: Every keep-what-we-have decision stands; the Flash translation routing (#5740) is under 30 referenced books in six of seven languages and the A5 re-OCR plan rests on 5-14 pages a script.
entries.decision: No routing change; proposed a reference top-up (run as 2026-10-06-reference-topup-flash-translation-5873) and a human calibration set (#5406)

entries.question: Served English against published human translations in 14 languages: what the five tracks say together
entries.verdict: Served English across 14 languages scores 3.86 vs published translations (71% of pages at 4+); OCR misread is the primary cause of 47% of low pages; Flash beats Lite in most languages.
entries.decision: Greek, Hebrew/Aramaic, Arabic, Persian, Sanskrit, Pali, Chinese translate on Flash (PR #5740); Latin and vernaculars stay on Lite

entries.question: Can an open 8B model trained on our own Latin translations translate as well as flash-lite?
entries.verdict: A Qwen3-8B LoRA student trained on our Latin translations scores 0.83 below flash-lite [-1.06, -0.59] on 71 referenced pages and reverses meaning on 27% of pages vs 6%.
entries.decision: Preregistered stop: no GEX45 run, no routing change (#5793)

entries.question: Do typed notes and a stance (prompt v17) make the translation's apparatus more honest than v13's single <note>?
entries.verdict: v17 not established: the study stance lifts transparency +0.57 but costs 1.1 readability and fails typing (85%) and alternatives (33% real); the reading stance changes nothing.
entries.decision: v13 stays the default; v17 study and reading rows seeded is_default:false (#5698)

entries.question: On the same held Tibetan pages, how often do Gemini 3.1 flash-lite and Yigdzin agree, and which one reads the Kangyur?
entries.verdict: Flash-lite and Yigdzin rarely agree on held Tibetan pages (median syllable agreement 0.11, n 494); on the Kangyur control Yigdzin matches Derge 0.962 vs lite 0.149, 23 of 23 pages.
entries.decision: Yigdzin read applied to the held books (job yigdzin-527); any future Yigdzin lane needs a script gate in front (#4523)

entries.question: Tengyur stored draft vs 84000: is the English the library holds as good as the test arm?
entries.verdict: Stored Tengyur English matches the test arm against 84000: 6.2 reversed statements per 100 pages by either judge, 3.4 by both; label should read about 3-6 per 100 pages.

entries.question: Tengyur draft on an unbiased random sample: two blind reviewers, three kinds of control, corpus detectors and a by-eye check
entries.verdict: On 150 random Tengyur draft pages, 75% need only light edits; reversal or wrong-agent errors run about 38 per 100 pages (spot-check adjusted), worst in Pramana and verse.
entries.decision: Recommended label sentence not applied; #5788 and #5806 decide; 180 reviewer fixes listed, not applied

entries.question: Do folio markers go on in the chained translation lane, and is the page-break defect the model or the markers?
entries.verdict: Folio markers on Lite cut seam defects 26 to 19 per 100 breaks (p 0.105, misses the 0.10 bar; omissions rise); the defect is the model: Flash 16, Flash + markers 11.
entries.decision: TRANSLATE_FOLIO_MARKERS stays OFF by the registered rule; result used as evidence for Flash routing of the chained lane (#5678)

entries.question: Does #5795's Persian verdict survive a rule with a margin? (replay through the routing-eval tool, #5828)
entries.verdict: Replayed #5795: the registered rule reproduces every stored verdict; with margin-v1 Persian flips to route to flash (1 discordant page in 30), nothing else changes.
entries.decision: No routing change; supports Derek's Persian override (#5812); margin-v1 is the default rule file for new routing evals

entries.question: Does re-OCR actually lift the English, and where per dollar?
entries.verdict: A Flash re-read of Lite-read pages lifts Lite English +0.75 [0.51, 0.99], about half the by-eye ceiling; re-reading Flash-read pages buys nothing (+0.08, inside the floor).
entries.decision: Flash OCR for Persian, Sanskrit, Pali, Arabic visible and new books (FLASH_OCR_FROM, PR #5760); Lite-read backlog re-OCR pending Derek (#5700)

entries.question: Does re-reading distressed pages from the upgraded master fix them?
entries.verdict: Flash re-read from upgraded masters: palm-leaf Pali 6 wins / 1 loss but 12 of 31 reads loop; Chester Beatty Arabic 3 wins / 1 loss. Blanket Pali re-OCR not justified.
entries.decision: No blanket re-OCR of upgraded palm-leaf Pali on Flash; nothing written to pages (#3186)

entries.question: Correcting books.language where the page shows another language
entries.verdict: Four agreeing page reads relabel books.language right on 40 of 40 fresh gate books (58/58 overall); 683 relabels written, 616 of them Greek to Latin.
entries.decision: 683 books relabelled in production (sweep relabel-4884, undoable); Javanese, translation-edition and bilingual patterns left unwritten

entries.question: If GLM-OCR reads the text, how much Gemini do we need to get the page-structure tags back, and what does it cost?
entries.verdict: A tags-only Gemini pass over GLM-OCR text recovers every tag but marginalia (margin F1 0.64) at $0.43 per 1,000 pages, 47% of a full lite OCR ($0.91); $0 rules give only language and script.
entries.decision: No tags-only pass: it was a recipe for an open-engine print lane, and no such lane was adopted (routing row latin-script-print, not-adopted list). Closed in #6688

entries.question: Which open engine should read our English and early-Latin print? Round 3 of #5660: GLM-OCR beats lite on English 1600–1699 and 1700+; Latin still cannot be called
entries.verdict: GLM-OCR beats lite on English 1600-1699 (CER 0.034 vs 0.053) and 1700+; five other open engines do not; Latin stays directional (40 library pages).
entries.decision: No routing change; the whole-book GLM pilot (2026-10-04-does-glm-ocr-hold-up...) found word swaps and modernised spelling, so English stays on lite

entries.question: Can any engine read the Mongolian Kanjur (BDRC W4CZ5370) well enough to be worth a scored reference?
entries.verdict: No engine reads the Mongolian Kanjur: Flash read 0 of 285 columns on 10 pages (called it Manchu); hinted Flash loops on-genre invented text; CrossLing-OCR-Mini emits Tibetan.
entries.decision: No character-level reference commissioned to score Flash; a trained Mongolian recogniser is a separate decision for Derek (#5664)

entries.question: Latin print by century: does flash-lite read well enough, or should early Latin go to flash? 1600s: keep lite. 1500s, 1700s, incunabula: not enough references
entries.verdict: 1600s Latin print: rule says keep lite (flash 0.3 pp better, under the 1 pp margin, 50 books); 1500s, 1700s and incunabula lack references; lite misreads long s.
entries.decision: Latin print stays on Flash-Lite (routing row latin-script-print): the 1600s rule says keep it, and the other centuries lack references. The gothic and long-s question is one decision for Derek on #6688

entries.question: What script and language are the 1,670 books with no language?
entries.verdict: The 1,670 no-language books are 892 Latin-script, 211 Arabic, 110 Turfan, 79 Hebrew, 72 Armenian...; script label held 28/30 by eye outside Turfan; 14 scripts lack a lane.

entries.question: Does a Kraken model fine-tuned on our own corrected early-print pages read Latin 1500–1699 better than flash-lite?
entries.verdict: Kraken fine-tuned on EEBO-TCP beats lite on Latin 1500-1699 (median dCER -0.026, 46/13) but only on EEBO microfilm; it ties lite on 21 other-library pages.
entries.decision: No routing change: the gain does not carry beyond EEBO film and Kraken takes 166-271 s/page on Hetzner (#5730)

entries.question: Where does a second published translator land on our fidelity scale, and how much of that do Flash and Lite reach? Greek and Latin
entries.verdict: A second published translator scores 4.21 (Greek) / 4.14 (Latin); Flash reaches 87% / 105% of that ceiling, Lite 74% / 98%; the Greek gap is wrong OCR.

entries.question: How far apart are two human transcriptions of the same printed page, and where does our OCR sit against both? English, Greek, Chinese
entries.verdict: Two human transcriptions differ by 0.14% of letters (English), 0.43% (Greek), 0.28% (Taisho Chinese after glyph folding); our English OCR's median page is at that floor.

entries.question: Should the hidden OCR backlog of Persian, Sanskrit, Pali, Arabic, Ge'ez read on flash?
entries.verdict: No family passes the preregistered rule: Sanskrit, Pali, Arabic fail the label check (69-77%); Persian fails by one flash loop while flash wins 9-0 by eye.
entries.decision: Derek override: Persian hidden backlog to flash (FLASH_OCR_INCLUDES_HIDDEN); the other four stay lite, Sanskrit/Arabic to relabel #4884

entries.question: Does GLM-OCR hold up when it writes whole English 1600–1699 books? No: by eye it swaps plausible words and modernises spelling, where lite keeps the print
entries.verdict: GLM-OCR writing whole English 1600s books makes about one meaning-changing word swap and three silent spelling modernisations per page, where flash-lite keeps the print.
entries.decision: GLM-OCR is not routed English print from 1600 on; any GLM lane needs a by-eye spelling-fidelity check first

entries.question: Can we read our Coptic books? CER of stored / Lite / Flash against Coptic SCRIPTORIUM on 15 pages, and the served English against WEB/Brenton on 6
entries.verdict: Flash reads Coptic at 10.1% CER against SCRIPTORIUM, Lite 32.2% (wrong alphabet); served English on 3 Nag Hammadi pages is recited from other sayings.

entries.question: Is Cloudflare's Clef a substitute for Jev as a page screen?
entries.verdict: Clef ties Jev as an instruction-page text screen (rubric AUC 0.944 vs 0.943 on 519 pages) at 5x the price; Jev stays the default.
entries.decision: Jev stays the default text screen: same AUC at a fifth of Clef's price

entries.question: Which page-image questions can Clef answer well enough to use?
entries.verdict: Clef answers text-to-image match well (AUC 0.996, 60/60 next-page texts caught) and beats Gemini flash-lite on real pages; script class, blank and date screens fail.
entries.decision: Clef chosen for the leaf-match screen; it ran the #5803 corpus screen

entries.question: Across the whole visible corpus, how many books carry another page's text beside an image?
entries.verdict: 151 of 41,096 visible books (0.37%) show a clean one-page text/image shift on the sampled page; 86 are e-rara PDF archives (10.7% of e-rara screened).

entries.question: Handwritten, printed or mixed, plus script family, for every book
entries.verdict: 96,198 books classed: 68,170 printed, 21,700 handwritten, 1,015 mixed, 5,313 unclassified; 38 of 40 correct by eye; the Greek manuscript list is 360 books.
entries.decision: Classes written to books.book_class with one sweep_log row per book (#5768)

entries.question: Which of the $0 translation cleanups (A2/A3) are safe to apply, and what did applying them change?
entries.verdict: Three cleanup classes passed the by-eye gate (40/40 each) and were applied to 277,832 pages in 14,931 books; a_scan (~29/40) and b_original (~27/40) failed.
entries.decision: a_initial, c_tags, c_visible applied with page_revisions undo rows; a_scan and b_original not applied (#5700)

entries.question: How faithful is the served English for Sanskrit, Pali and classical Chinese against published human translations, what causes the bad pages, and which lever helps?
entries.verdict: Served English scores 3.63/5; Flash beats Lite by +0.40 [0.22, 0.58], reversals 15.4 to 5.9 per 100 pages; OCR is the primary cause on 30% of low pages.
entries.decision: Flash routes Sanskrit, Pali and Chinese translation (PR #5740)

entries.question: How faithful is our served Latin English against published human translations, and which lever helps?
entries.verdict: Served Latin English scores 4.16/5 (incunabula 3.55, OCR-bound); Flash beats Lite by +0.22 beyond the A-vs-A floor; context and negation check do not.
entries.decision: PENDING Derek in DECISIONS.md (default: keep lite until the dial rises)

entries.question: Against published human translations, how faithful is the served English for German, French, Italian, Dutch and Spanish, and which lever helps?
entries.verdict: Served vernacular English scores 4.39/5 (92% of pages at 4 or more); Flash beats Lite by +0.21 (German +0.39); thinking adds nothing, dropping context costs 0.21.
entries.decision: PENDING Derek in DECISIONS.md (default: keep lite until the dial rises); Flash for German proposed

entries.question: How faithful is the served English for Hebrew/Aramaic, Arabic and Persian against published translations, and which lever fixes it?
entries.verdict: Served Hebrew/Aramaic/Arabic/Persian English scores 3.44/5; OCR is the primary cause on 14 of 23 low pages; corrected text +1.4, Flash over Lite +0.53.
entries.decision: Flash routes Hebrew, Aramaic, Arabic and Persian translation (PR #5740), provisional pending the #5873 top-up

entries.question: Smoke run of the translation-vs-reference judge harness: do the controls pass on six Pali pages?
entries.verdict: The translation-vs-reference harness passes its controls with two blind Opus judges on 6 Pali pages (weighted kappa 0.90); an instrument check, not a finding.

entries.question: Do the seam lines alone cut page-boundary invention on the chained lane's page breaks? Confirmatory
entries.verdict: Seam lines alone do not cut page-boundary invention on block-door page breaks: 19 / 19 / 19 pages (v13a / v13b / seam), p 0.60. Rule output FAIL.
entries.decision: FAIL: seam lines not flipped (PR #5675, DECISIONS.md)

entries.question: Does v16 (v15 + one sentence scoping the OMIT rule) keep v15's verified original-notes without losing interpretive notes?
entries.verdict: v16's scoping sentence still cuts interpretive notes 28.7% (fails the -15% floor); verified original-notes 88.0 to 91.3%, not decisive. Not established.
entries.decision: Not established: keep v13 (PR #5703); a v17 typed-apparatus candidate is next (#5698)

entries.question: Tengyur quality levers on the 84000-referenced pages: a Sanskrit parallel, a glossary, a negation check with a Pro second pass, Flash thinking, and an Opus ceiling
entries.verdict: No lever beats the B-vs-B noise floor (+0.093): glossary raises both-judge reversals 2 to 7, thinking doubles omissions; only Opus gains (+0.5 fidelity on 40 pages).
entries.decision: Adopt no lever; the full Tengyur runs arm B as is (PR #5713)

entries.question: Is the Tengyur pilot English good enough to run on all 213 volumes?
entries.verdict: Tengyur pilot English is draft-grade: 33 of 40 sampled pages at fidelity 4+, 4 of 40 reversed, 16 of 40 seam shifts; no loops or truncation on 1,269 pages.
entries.decision: Full run approved, but on one page per request rather than the chained pilot lane (PR #5717)

entries.question: Tengyur draft English against 84000's published translations: the chained lane (neighbour context, 8-page blocks) vs one page per request with no context
entries.verdict: Against 84000, one page per request matches the chained lane on fidelity (4.54 vs 4.48) and cuts wrong-span sides from 15 to 1 of 113; seams come from 8-page blocks.
entries.decision: Full Tengyur draft runs one page per request, no context (PR #5717)

entries.question: Which English translations carry a script that belongs to neither the source nor the book?
entries.verdict: 4,913 of 5.4M English pages carry a stray script; Hangul (mostly a 그 for 'that') on 2,689, 2,677 of them from gemini-3-flash-preview, across all source languages.
entries.decision: 2,083 pages repaired; write-time stray-script guard added at every translation writer (Derek, 2026-10-03)

entries.question: Page breaks where the sentence runs on: is the chained lane's defect the model or the forcing, and do folio markers fix it on Lite?
entries.verdict: Registered rule unresolved (literal marker parse failed); read positionally, seam defects per 100 breaks: Lite 21/26, Lite+markers 15, Flash+markers 8.
entries.decision: Flag stays off; the confirmatory run found markers NO, attribution MODEL

entries.question: Can a reference-free check find the pages the reference judges marked as reversed, omitted or invented?
entries.verdict: No reference-free screen works: the best detector (D3, Flash-Lite contradiction check) finds 83% of judged reversals but flags half of all pages at 18% precision.
entries.decision: Not used as a library screen; D3 as a QA sampler and a Latin negation hold-out were proposed, not implemented

entries.question: How many served translated pages would each text-quality backfill touch? A1 census, $0
entries.verdict: A deterministic $0 cleanup (A2) would touch about 479K served pages (9.8%); off-page original: notes about 173K; reader-visible markup leaks about 22K.
entries.decision: A2 cleanup approved by Derek 2026-10-04 and applied (2026-10-04-a2-cleanup-applied-5700.md)

entries.question: Can a per-book fit of the OCR's page numbers give the printed page of a scan?
entries.verdict: A per-book fit of OCR page numbers labels 51.5% of visible OCR pages (3.24M of 6.29M) with a printed page; 20 of 20 correct on an image-read control.
entries.decision: pages.printed_page backfilled (PR #5687); citations cite the printed page (PR #5688)

entries.question: Can an open engine on our own GPU replace flash-lite for the Latin-script and Greek print backlog? PaddleOCR-VL-1.6: no, in every cell
entries.verdict: PaddleOCR-VL-1.6 routes no print cell to the box: worse than flash-lite on Latin, German and early English, catastrophic on Greek print (58 of 114).
entries.decision: Latin-script and Greek print backlog stays on flash-lite; no routing change (DECISIONS.md, #5660)

entries.question: Does tighter tag wording (v20) improve the OCR prompt's page numbers and language labels? — No: v19.1 already reads them well
entries.verdict: v20 tag wording does not beat v19.1: page-number exact .865 in every arm, language match unchanged, show-through 9 better and 10 worse of 69.
entries.decision: Not adopted; v19.1 stays the OCR prompt (PR #5681)

entries.question: Which untranslated pages sit on OCR we already know is bad, and can a cheap page signal find the rest?
entries.verdict: 10,005 untranslated pages in 703 books sit in the bad-OCR strata; no cheap page signal reaches precision 0.8 (best: Greek dictionary miss P 0.80, R 0.24).
entries.decision: No page-level gate; the per-stratum OCR trust gate at every translation enrol was merged instead (#5761)

entries.question: Does a grounded Gemini verifier find the wrong translation notes the $0 table cannot?
entries.verdict: Grounded Gemini verifier caught 48 of 49 planted seeds but only 4 of 15 known real note errors; 3 of its 11 'wrong' verdicts held; $22.62 for 3 repairs.
entries.decision: Not scaled as a corpus lane; reseed from real error shapes if retried; 9 notes repaired (DECISIONS.md)

entries.question: the second open engine: olmOCR-2-7B-FP8 passes English 1600–1699 and loses every other cell
entries.verdict: olmOCR-2-7B-FP8 beats flash-lite on English 1600-1699 (CER 0.036 vs 0.053, routes to box) but keeps lite elsewhere; Greek catastrophic on 55 of 114 pages.
entries.decision: olmOCR not adopted: English 1600-1699 stays on Flash-Lite and no open-engine print lane runs (routing row latin-script-print, not-adopted list; GPU lanes stopped at gate 0, #5660). Closed in #6688

entries.question: Does moving the own-text continuity-meta payload into the body put the page's own text back?
entries.verdict: Moving the own-text continuity-meta payload into the body was right on 18 of 20 pilot pages, under the 19/20 bar; both misses carry a lead-in from the previous page.
entries.decision: Full apply (9,582 pages) not run; options (a) all, (b) headInPrev < 0.3, (c) second pilot await a decision (#5376)

entries.question: Ancient and Byzantine Greek: how faithful is the served English against a published translation, and where do the bad pages start?
entries.verdict: Served Greek English scores 3.64/5 against published translations (manuscripts 2.54); OCR misread causes 16 of 22 low pages; Flash beats Lite by +0.32.
entries.decision: Greek translation routes to Flash (PR #5740); Greek MSS and 1450-1599 print gated on OCR trust (#5761)

entries.question: Folio markers read by position: how many of the seam A/B marker defects were the parser's?
entries.verdict: Reading folio markers by position cuts parse failures 17 to 1 (Lite) and 11 to 0 (Flash); real seam defects per 100 breaks fall 28 to 15 and 18 to 8.
entries.decision: Positional parser merged into the lane code (#5719); TRANSLATE_FOLIO_MARKERS flag stays off

entries.question: Does continuous English with <pb n="N"/> page markers put each Tengyur page's words beside its own woodblock?
entries.verdict: Folio markers put Tengyur page turns where the source turns: median placement error 0.51% vs 1.02% served; 3 real misplacements in 26 turns read by eye.
entries.decision: Not adopted: TRANSLATE_FOLIO_MARKERS stays off (#5682); the Tengyur draft runs one page per request instead (PR #5717)

entries.question: What the audit judge calls "invention"
entries.verdict: Of 45 pages the audit judge flagged for invention, 21 are added notes (Flash 17 vs Lite 4), 14 page-boundary text and only 6 fabricated fill of unreadable source.

entries.question: Does the v14 candidate translation prompt cut invention, cross-page bridging and seam duplication without raising omission? With a Tibetan multi-leaf stratum
entries.verdict: v14 prompt fails its rule: judged invention 38.3% vs 47.7% (p 0.13, needs <0.10) and controls breach +12 pp; it halves page-boundary invention; Tibetan leaf lines unsupported.
entries.decision: Not flipped: v14 failed its rule; its seam items re-tested alone also failed (2026-10-03-translation-seam-confirm-5305.md)

entries.question: How many served translations carry text from the adjacent page, and which lane writes it? 2.4% of pages, every lane
entries.verdict: 2.44% (1.83-3.27) of served translated pages carry or lose text across a page boundary, in every lane (chained Batch 1.6%, pre-fix realtime 2.7%); about 116K pages corpus-wide.

entries.question: Should Sanskrit, Pali and classical Chinese translate on flash instead of lite? Blind A/B against published English, with an A-vs-A floor
entries.verdict: Flash beats lite beyond the A-vs-A floor for Sanskrit (p 0.009); Pali ahead but fragile; Chinese ahead (p 0.002) but lite's run-to-run instability exceeds the margin.
entries.decision: Absorbed by #5695 T5; flash now routes Sanskrit, Pali and Chinese translation (PR #5740)

entries.question: Does the OCR's own "this page is blank" tag find invented pages corpus-wide?
entries.verdict: The self-declared-blank rule flags 166,077 pages corpus-wide but 0 of 20 read by eye are invented text on a blank leaf (Wilson 0-16.1%); use it as a ranking signal, not a quarantine list.
entries.decision: Not used to quarantine; kept as a supporting signal in detect-fabricated-ocr.mjs (PR #5652)

entries.question: Is the language picture really a manuscript/print picture, or a holding-library picture?
entries.verdict: Manuscripts rate faithful less often (66% vs 88%) but are tangled with script (adjusted OR 0.48, CI spans 1); holding library mostly stands in for script; Chinese tables 47.6% CER.
entries.decision: One-pager now names manuscript status as partly confounded with script (#5623)

entries.question: Does page quality move with the book's date, the amount of text on the page, or the scan's resolution, once script is accounted for?
entries.verdict: Script is the only covariate tied to translation quality (non-Latin OR 0.20); for OCR, date matters within a script (Greek 1500s CER 17.1% vs 1800s 0.8%), resolution above 1,500 px does not.

entries.question: Which PaddleOCR-VL-1.6 serving configuration reads the held Siku Quanshu cohort cheapest without reading it worse?
entries.verdict: PaddleOCR-VL-1.6 with no layout stage reads the SKQS manuscripts no worse than with it (fresh 95 pages: median dCER -0.007, 0 catastrophic): PASS by the pre-registered rule.

entries.question: Do OCR prompts v18 / v19 stop invented text on white and show-through leaves without declaring real pages blank? Screened, labelled by eye, four arms, Batch, k=3
entries.verdict: By the pre-registered rule v18: white-leaf fabrication 0.91 to 0.29; v19 cuts fabrication most (0.78 to 0.35) but fails the over-decline guard (S3 0.381 vs limit 0.372).
entries.decision: Led to v19.1, which was promoted instead of v18 (PR #5661)

entries.question: Does OCR prompt v19.1 ("a stamp on a show-through leaf is text") keep v19's blank/show-through gain without v19's over-decline? Two new arms on the v19 run's labelled pages, Batch, k=3
entries.verdict: v19.1 passes all five pre-registered clauses and beats v18 on invented pages (15 vs 4, p 0.019), at the cost of more real pages called blank (S3 0.360 vs 0.299).
entries.decision: v19.1 is the production OCR prompt (PR #5655, promoted in PR #5661)

entries.question: Does OCR prompt v18 (blank narrowing + <insert>) stop invented text on blank leaves without declaring real pages blank? Three arms, Batch, k=3
entries.verdict: Not established: v18 stops invented text on clean white leaves but not show-through; pre-registered S1 (5 better vs 2 worse, p 0.45) and S2 blank-recall clauses fail.
entries.decision: Not promoted on this evidence; re-run with by-eye labels (#4195)

entries.question: OCR benchmark: what changes in the headline numbers when a refused page is counted as a refusal, not a blank read?
entries.verdict: 26 meter-recorded refusals across 10 strata plus 7 inferred; only EEBO-TCP's headline moves (flash mean CER 0.133 to 0.054 on answered pages), and flash still beats lite.
entries.decision: Benchmark scorer and dashboard now score refusals apart (PR #5605); refusal fix itself is the recitation retry (#5521)

entries.question: Every candidate note in the Tibetan run, fact-checked
entries.verdict: All 359 candidate notes in the Tibetan run checked: 18 (5.0%) wrong or partly wrong, 11 (3.1%) strictly wrong, mostly Sanskrit equivalents and identifications; the sample's 15% was high by chance.
entries.decision: 18-row corrections list; the corrections were later applied (seen in #5647); prompt line still pending (#5624)

entries.question: Can a $0 reference table settle translation-note facts before a model is paid to?
entries.verdict: A $0 Tibetan-Sanskrit table never matched a wrong note (0 of 18) and all 6 conflicts were wrong notes, but it settles only 11% of candidates and finds 3 of 18 known wrongs.
entries.decision: Stage-3 grounded verifier (~$20) run next on the 885 no-entry notes; no note corrected here (#5647)

entries.question: Loghi (GLOBALISE model) vs Gemini on 17th–18th c. Dutch handwriting
entries.verdict: On held-out VOC Dutch handwriting Loghi beats Gemini by best-line CER (0.161 vs flash 0.252, lite 0.305), on its home ground; a Laypa line-count screen flags omissions but misses some.

entries.question: What should the translator output for a page nobody could read? A pre-model gate: right on 26 of 30 held-out fires (precision 0.87), 0 false withholds on clean audit pages. It does not reach garble
entries.verdict: A pre-model illegible-source gate is right on 26 of 30 held-out fires (precision 0.87) with 0 false withholds on clean pages, but catches 1 of 29 judged garble pages; a prompt clause does nothing.
entries.decision: Gate shipped behind TRANSLATE_ILLEGIBLE_GATE (PR #5638), switched on for production 2026-10-03 (count audit #5685)

entries.question: Greek manuscripts: can an open published edition be fitted to the scans instead of re-OCR?
entries.verdict: 90 of 316 Greek manuscripts locate in an open edition, but no pilot book reaches the 80% write bar: Grec 1841 76.5% located (only Kraken verifies spans), Marcianus 46.5%.
entries.decision: No write proposed; next step a full Kraken read of Grec 1841 (#5619)

entries.question: How much of the collection is blackletter? Typeface for every book, from one page each
entries.verdict: Typeface now known for 92% of books: blackletter 10.0% of all 41,555 books, German 83.1%, Dutch 42.6%, Latin 9.7%; most BSB books undescribed after IIIF 429s.

entries.question: What does the collection look like, page by page: printed or handwritten, which typeface, which page type?
entries.verdict: One page per visible book: 7.6% of 41,555 books handwritten plus 2.6% mixed, 86% printed; typeface known on only 17% (blackletter 17.1% there, non-random subset).
entries.decision: Derek approved the typeface pass for every book the same day (#5643)

entries.question: Can open Sefaria text be fitted to Hebrew pages whose OCR failed? For 43 of 808 pages, verified page by page. Licence, edition layout and edges refuse the rest
entries.verdict: Open Sefaria text fitted and verified on only 43 of 808 OCR-failed Hebrew pages; licence, edition layout and unreadable edges refuse the other 765.
entries.decision: 43 pages written from Sefaria; the 765 refused pages go to a loop-guarded re-read (#3878)

entries.question: Are the facts translation notes add right?
entries.verdict: In the Tibetan v13 flash run 6 of 40 sampled factual notes (15%) are wrong or partly wrong, all identifications or Sanskrit equivalents, none dates; audit 'invention' flags are often correct facts.
entries.decision: Prompt not changed; a prompt line for unsure equivalents went to DECISIONS-PENDING (#4523)

entries.question: What kinds of error make up an OCR engine's CER? On early English print, flash-lite's is mostly ſ read as f and flash's is mostly refusal; served OCR keeps its body text but normalises spelling
entries.verdict: On early English print flash-lite's OCR error is mostly long s read as f (57%) and flash's mostly refusals (72%); served OCR keeps body text but normalises spelling.

entries.question: What does a given character error rate or judge rating look like on a real page?
entries.verdict: Read on the scan, most of a low or middle measured CER is the reference's own spellings, edition variants and window spill, not engine misreads.
entries.decision: Error ladder published on /research/quality (ErrorLadder.tsx, #5576)

entries.question: Translation recitation pilot: does a served English page reproduce a published translation instead of translating the page?
entries.verdict: Recitation of public-domain translations not detected: 4/36 served pages share a 12+ word run, below the 20% two-human-translator baseline; 0/5 recited by eye.
entries.decision: None needed; no routing or prompt change proposed (#5523)

entries.question: Tibetan retranslation on the Batch lane: lite vs flash vs a Claude arm, on the CURRENT Yigdzin read, blind vs 84000
entries.verdict: Against 84000 on the Batch lane: Claude 4.71, flash 4.31, lite 4.02 mean fidelity; lite inverts on 9.5%; 190K pages cost ~$114 lite or ~$254 flash.
entries.decision: Kangyur retranslation spend PENDING Derek in DECISIONS.md (#4742); flash already the Tibetan engine for non-held books (PR #5094)

entries.question: Is served Persian OCR accurate enough to OCR and translate the six prose Sufi manuscripts? Measured on classical poetry vs Ganjoor
entries.verdict: Served Persian manuscript OCR scores sequence accuracy 0.41 and line accuracy 0.74 vs Ganjoor, 4/21 pages degenerate; the 0.90 gate is not met.
entries.decision: Stage 2 (OCR and translate the six prose manuscripts on the served lane) not run; needs a different OCR lane first (#5525)

entries.question: Does Gemini flash, or an open-source Kraken model, read Persian manuscripts well enough to OCR the six prose books?
entries.verdict: On Persian manuscript poetry flash beats served lite (seq 0.70 vs 0.41, loops 1 vs 4); no Kraken model is competitive; still far below the 0.90 gate.
entries.decision: Persian OCR moved to flash on 2026-10-04 (PR #5760, hidden backlog #5795); the prose-shelf pilot was not run

entries.question: Kangyur OCR accuracy, confirmatory re-draw: does the 0.95 hold on fresh pages, and how often is a line dropped?
entries.verdict: Fresh redraw replicates Kangyur Yigdzin OCR at median 0.947 identity vs Derge (76/100 >= 0.9); about 5% of pages drop a line.

entries.question: IA candidate dates: which Internet Archive items are actually old?
entries.verdict: Metadata-only date rules (v3) classify IA candidates old vs modern at 65/68 = 95.6% against title pages read by eye, clearing the 90% bar.
entries.decision: v3 rules write classification.date_check on 1.0M IA candidates (scripts/lib/ia-date-check.mjs, #5458)

entries.question: How strong are the /research/quality paper's numbers once agreement is corrected for chance and the screen is scored on held-out pages?
entries.verdict: Corrected for chance the two judges agree at kappa 0.56 on sound vs not, and the two-read screen's recall falls from 74% in-sample to 55% held out.
entries.decision: Quality paper text corrected and reader-panel protocol changed before sign-off (#5495)

entries.question: Text hidden in the continuity <meta>: full-mirror count, classes, live re-check, repair plan
entries.verdict: 92,684 translated pages hide 8+ words in the continuity meta; 10,160 still-hidden own-text pages can be opened for $0.
entries.decision: Write guard PR #5432 and v16 bare marker PR #5433 merged; the tier A-F repair plan on #5376 is not recorded as run

entries.question: Fingerprint test: do models continue our transcriptions with OUR misreads? No signal, and no power to show one: our served text postdates every model's cutoff, and the models do not reproduce even the Archive's pre-cutoff misreads
entries.verdict: No model continues our text with our misreads (0/9 unpredictable), and the positive control does not fire (0-1 of 36 Archive misreads): the instrument is unpowered.
entries.decision: None; no routing, field or publish rule changed (#5549)

entries.question: How accurate is production OCR on English print of the 1600s? 5.3% median CER against same-edition EEBO-TCP; flash reads better but refuses more
entries.verdict: English 1600-1699 vs same-edition EEBO-TCP: flash-lite median CER 0.053, 0/52 catastrophic; flash 0.038 but 5/52 RECITATION refusals.

entries.question: Does the Yigdzin per-leaf crop drop the lower leaf's first line, and should the "lines < book median" pages be re-read?
entries.verdict: The Yigdzin leaf cut does not drop the lower leaf's first line (short pages are symmetric across leaves, 7/7 by eye); the dropped line comes from whole-page reads.
entries.decision: Overlapping leaf crops not built; never-leaf-read pages left to the approved tibetan-step2 job (#4523)

entries.question: Does one long-s line in the OCR prompt fix early-modern English print? Measured against EEBO-TCP same-edition references
entries.verdict: A long-s line cuts RECITATION refusals ~70% (lite 24 -> 7 of 142, p 0.002) with no accuracy loss, but it switches output to the s glyph, so retry-only.
entries.decision: Long-s line used only on RECITATION retry, collector folds the glyph to s (PR #5526, #5521); default prompt unchanged

entries.question: Held Siku Quanshu cohort: can Kanripo's text replace OCR, does the OCR engine show in the English, and does Paddle's output fit the production writer?
entries.verdict: Kanripo aligns 36/40 SKQS pages but 28% have shifted page breaks; Paddle's English beats lite's 20-4 (both orders); Kanripo text does not improve the English over Paddle.
entries.decision: PaddleOCR-VL for the cohort (routing row chinese-siku-manuscript, #5600); Kanripo is a reference, not page text (its licence is still Derek's call, #6688). Closed in #6688

entries.question: Which engine should OCR the 7,894 Chinese books held out of #4719, measured on the cohort itself?
entries.verdict: On the held SKQS cohort (97.7% brush manuscript) lite is catastrophic on 10.6% of pages, PaddleOCR-VL 0.9%, flash-preview 3.7%; Paddle passes the cost-lane rule again.
entries.decision: PaddleOCR-VL reads the Siku Quanshu cohort (routing row chinese-siku-manuscript; lane scripts/lib/paddle-zh-lane.mjs, #5600). Closed in #6688

entries.question: Chained Batch lane: random-sample fidelity of pages the lane wrote
entries.verdict: Chained Batch lane pages: fidelity >= 4 on 85.4% (81.5-88.6), major defect 6.9%; seam pages no worse than seeded; the fidelity-1 page was an echo-shift lane defect.
entries.decision: Echo guard: an echoed entry now discards the whole block (shipped with this row, #4681)

entries.question: Can the Nyingma tantra manuscripts (BL EAP, non-Kangyur) get an accuracy number?
entries.verdict: Served Nyingma SERVE pages score median 0.833 identity vs the rKTs Gpb e-text (a lower bound, different witness); MARK_UNRELIABLE pages 0.249, so the split is real.

entries.question: Can a re-read fix pages whose OCR loops? About two-thirds of them, with lite at temp 0.7 and a flash fallback; production settings re-loop a third
entries.verdict: A lite temp 0.7 re-read with a flash fallback clears 22 of 30 looping pages (realistic about 19-20); production settings re-loop 11/30, and a near-loop passes the gate.
entries.decision: Re-read lane for looping pages: lite 0.7 then flash, with near-loop and script-mismatch checks (PR #5515)

entries.question: Why is Gemini OCR off-leaf on IA bulk_jp2 books, and which pages exactly?
entries.verdict: Off-leaf IA OCR is text stranded by the #3368 image repair: 399 books, 105,316 translated pages flagged needs_reocr that nothing reads; matches 27 of 29 detector books.
entries.decision: Exact list and guard shipped (PR #5401); repair (about $255 on batch) not run

entries.question: Which engine reads printed NUMBERS correctly? Engine disagreements adjudicated blind on the page image
entries.verdict: Against the page image the Archive gets 5.1% of printed numbers wrong vs lite 1.8% (82 books, 5,212 numbers); lite fewer wrong on 39 books, the Archive on 7.
entries.decision: The Archive's text does not replace a Flash-Lite read: it fills empty and refused pages only (routing row refused-pages; Derek 2026-09-26, #5186). Closed in #6688

entries.question: Where does translation invention live, and can a reader see it?
entries.verdict: Major served inventions sit in the body (14 of 15); under the current prompt the continuity meta is the top location (21 of 57) and hides page text on 0.84% of translated pages.
entries.decision: metaPayload detector shipped; led to the write guard (PR #5432) and v16 bare continuity marker (PR #5433, #5376)

entries.question: What does the Internet Archive's OCR get wrong? Class-by-class taxonomy on 4,470 Archive-vs-flash-lite page pairs
entries.verdict: Archive OCR words are fine (1-3 per mille glyph misreads) but numbers are not: 0.7-8.0% of years wrong per book, driven by typeface; flash-lite eye-skips 0.5% of interior pages.

entries.question: Were the bootstrap intervals in this file the right width? The generator cycled; 31 quoted intervals recomputed, no decision changes
entries.verdict: The paired-stats bootstrap generator cycled; of 31 quoted intervals 22 moved, two were a quarter to a third too narrow, and no routing or adoption decision changes.
entries.decision: paired-stats.mjs and three copies moved to mulberry32, pinned by tests/unit/paired-stats-prng.test.ts (#5373)

entries.question: Translation corpus audit: how faithful is a random SERVED translation, by language, model and period?
entries.verdict: 87-89% of served translated pages read at fidelity >= 4 of 5 and 11-14% carry a major defect; non-Latin script 70.8% >= 4 vs Latin 92.9%; top major class is prose over garbled OCR.

entries.question: Syriac per-stratum preprocessing on LIBRARY pages: does the #5250 result transfer? NO
entries.verdict: The #5250 Syriac preprocessing gains do not transfer to library pages: the classifier finds 0/6 dark pages and routed auto vs production is +0.7% letters read, p 0.26.
entries.decision: Preprocess flag ships OFF (--preprocess none); no re-read; #4883 re-translation proceeds on existing reads

entries.question: NDL classical-OCR lane — 20-book pilot, written and read by eye
entries.verdict: On 20 cursive Japanese books NDL and stored Gemini readings barely agree (median Dice 0.067); by eye NDL gives the page's text on 9/10 pages, Gemini was invented or looping on 3 of 4.
entries.decision: NDL classical-OCR lane shipped (PR #5412); 985 pilot pages written, 356 translations marked stale

entries.question: MinerU on the English reference pages: peer engine, tier-3 fallback, or neither?
entries.verdict: MinerU is neither peer nor tier-3 fallback, narrowly: catastrophic 2.6% (bar 2%), refused-page pooled CER 2.25x lite (bar 2x), mostly from dropped footnotes; median delta +0.19 pp.
entries.decision: MinerU is not a peer of Flash-Lite; it stays a refusal fallback only, after the footnote fix (routing row refused-pages, PR #5299). Closed in #6688

entries.question: Lite vs flash on the SAME pages: does the model change judged fidelity, omission or invention?
entries.verdict: On the same pages flash invents more (15.8% vs 8.2%/9.2% for two lite runs); fidelity >= 4 and omission do not differ measurably. Rule output: lite stays.

entries.question: Leaf identity: is the page image a reader sees the page that was translated?
entries.verdict: The shown image is a different leaf from the translated text on 6 of 298 decidable pages (2.0%), all Internet Archive (3.8% of IA pages); the image is right, the Gemini OCR text is shifted.

entries.question: POST-HOC: the same MinerU rule, re-applied with PR #5299's footnote step
entries.verdict: Post hoc, with PR #5299's footnote step MinerU's catastrophic rate falls 2.6% to 0.0% and median delta vs lite to +0.08 pp, so the rule says PEER; lite still wins page by page 34-10.
entries.decision: MinerU with the footnote step is the tier-3 refusal fallback for English print from 1820, not a peer lane (routing row refused-pages; ops default in DECISIONS.md, PR #5299). Closed in #6688

entries.question: How much Gemini OCR on Internet Archive books is a neighbouring leaf's text, as readers see it?
entries.verdict: 3.7% of decidable IA books (29 of 775, CI 2.6-5.3%) show a neighbouring leaf's Gemini OCR beside the page image; projected about 102K pages, repair about $240 (not run).
entries.decision: Detector shipped (scripts/audit/ia-model-ocr-off-leaf.mjs, PR #5398); repair not run

entries.question: Duplicate-run guard grounded in the source : the 57 refrain pages the per-leaf guard refused go 57 → 0, the narrative book and the #5021 fixtures are untouched, 10 of 229 page-level duplicate flags on a 1,000-book mirror sample are released, all of them the source repeating itself
entries.verdict: Checking the source for a repeat across the seam releases all 57 refused Tibetan refrain pages (57 to 0); on a 1,000-book sample 10 of 229 duplicate flags are released, all real source repeats.
entries.decision: sourceRepeatsAcrossBoundary added to block-drift.mjs leaf-drift guard (PR #5306)

entries.question: Does the adopted English Archive cohort (1880–1930, number-free, ≥ 90% Latin) keep the Archive's number errors out, and how much does it admit?
entries.verdict: The 1880-1930 number-free cohort gate admits 0 of 1,241 pages with Archive number errors and 34% of cohort pages; after v2 fixes, 2 letter/Greek number misreads remain in 82 admitted pages.
entries.decision: Cohort page gate v2 (folio and digit-lookalike rules) in ia-ocr-cohort.mjs, IA text-first lane (PR #5361)

entries.question: Does disagreement between two reads of one page find garbled OCR?
entries.verdict: A fresh second read finds most garbled pages but imprecisely (P 0.3-0.45 vs the judge, gate 0.8 not met); the same reads separate wrong-leaf pages cleanly, 7 of 7.
entries.decision: Not used as a reader-note or garble detector (gate P >= 0.8 not met). Disagreement is used only to pick pages for Opus to adjudicate against the image (routing row two-reads-disagree, #6420). Closed in #6688

entries.question: Does a "stop where the page stops" instruction cut invention? Restraint A/B on the audit's own pages
entries.verdict: A restraint block has no measurable effect on judged invention (risk stratum 18.3% to 21.1%, p 0.80, floor 2.8 pp), though it cuts unmarked open ends 22.5% to 8.5%.
entries.decision: Restraint block left out of v16 by the preregistered rule (DECISIONS.md, 2026-09-30)

entries.question: Cursive census of pre-1868 Japanese + the router checked by eye
entries.verdict: 116 of 356 pre-1868 Japanese books are cursive (about 8,210 pages); the flash classifier agrees with eye labels on 57 of 60 fresh pages, catching all 28 cursive ones.
entries.decision: The census classifier is the NDL koten lane's per-book router (scripts/lib/ndl-koten-lane.mjs; 20-book pilot #4925)

entries.question: Chained Batch lane at scale : 154 books at once in shared jobs — $0.00061/page, ~4,700 pages/hour at full concurrency, 5.4% of rounds cancelled
entries.verdict: 154 books at once in shared Batch jobs: $0.00061 per written page, 5.4% of rounds cancelled (vs 16-18% one job per book), about 4,700 pages/hour at full concurrency.
entries.decision: Shared jobs (#5375), one fallback round (#5381) and auto-enrol (#5385) run in the chained cron; tick faults fixed in #5391, #5392

entries.question: Can a $0 per-page garble score find the audit's "fluent prose over garbled OCR" pages? No: precision 0.24–0.60, recall 0.09–0.19; no field written
entries.verdict: A $0 lexicon and repetition garble score reaches precision 0.24-0.60 and recall 0.09-0.19 against the judge's 32 positives; corpus precision about 15-20%.
entries.decision: Gate (P >= 0.8) not met; no ocr.read_quality field written, reader note unchanged (#5313)

entries.question: Round 3 of #5250: do the round-2 Kraken photometric gains hold on FRESH Syriac pages?
entries.verdict: On 80 fresh Syriac folios every prediction held: sauvola -3.8 pp CER on dark spreads, flatten -10.6 pp on clean leaves, unsharp helps both; flatten hurts dark spreads.
entries.decision: No lane change; per-stratum routing was then tested on library pages and did not transfer (#5277)

entries.question: Round 2 of #5250: do tighter band crops help Yigdzin, and do the untested photometric arms help Yigdzin or Kraken?
entries.verdict: Band crops do not beat leafcrop for Yigdzin (identity -9 pp, duplicated lines); photometric arms null for Yigdzin, but unsharp, flatten and denoise help Kraken on Syriac.
entries.decision: Band crops not adopted; the exploratory Kraken gains went to a fresh-page replication (round 3, #5250)

entries.question: Does image preprocessing (binarise / contrast / deskew / upscale / crop) help any OCR engine on our pages? Paired, four scripts, three engines
entries.verdict: Only per-leaf cropping helps (Yigdzin +46 matched Derge syllables per page, 98-2); Otsu hurts every engine; Sauvola, CLAHE, deskew and upscaling are null or harmful.
entries.decision: No preprocessing step added to the OCR path; leafcrop (production since 09-28) kept (#5250)

entries.question: Does a stronger image matcher (DINOv2-small, SigLIP2) beat CLIP ViT-B/32 for /identify, and where does CLIP actually lose?
entries.verdict: The CLIP index at probes=1 hid matches (top-1 21 to 30 of 63 at probes 10); SigLIP2 fp32 beats CLIP on top-1, 59 vs 49 (random pool) and 47 vs 34 (hard negatives).
entries.decision: probes=10 shipped (PR #5256); SigLIP2 as the /identify recall model awaits Derek (#3193)

entries.question: Chained Batch API translation lane, pilot on 5 stalled books : production's prompt one block per round, 847 pages written at $0.00056/pg (4.3× under realtime), median round 2.7 min, 16% of rounds cancelled and all recovered
entries.verdict: Chained Batch lane wrote 847 pages of 5 stalled books at $0.00056/page (4.3x under realtime), median round 2.7 min; 16% of rounds cancelled, all recovered.
entries.decision: Chained Batch lane merged (PR #5267) and runs from the production crontab; seam-repair design (#4912/#4973 arm Et) retired

entries.question: Which cheap model draws ACCURATE picture boxes? Seven arms, boxes graded by eye against the page
entries.verdict: Flash draws 81.6% tight boxes vs 3.1-lite 8-21% (finds pictures but crops them) and Qwen3-VL 63%; flash on the Batch API reproduces realtime boxes at half price.
entries.decision: Extraction stays on gemini-3-flash-preview, routed to the Batch API by default (IMAGE_EXTRACTION_USE_BATCH, PR #5238)

entries.question: Is flash-lite adequate on modern English print, or should it go to flash-preview? Paired on the #5216 references
entries.verdict: Flash beats lite 14-3 (75 ties) on 114 English reference pages but the median difference is 0.00 pp; both fail on RECITATION refusals (lite 14.9%, flash 17.5%).
entries.decision: Lite kept for English print; a refusal-fallback lane is the open item (PR #5248, Derek 2026-09-29)

entries.question: For which English IA books may the Archive's own OCR replace flash-lite? First English reference pages, both engines scored against them
entries.verdict: Against English references lite beats the Archive's OCR on the same page 57-5 (43 ties); the Archive silently misreads about 1.5% of printed numbers, lite 0 of 750.
entries.decision: Archive text admitted only for number-free 1880-1930 Latin-script pages (ia-ocr-cohort.mjs) and as refusal fallback; lite stays default (#5186)

entries.question: Page-break fix, SCOPED and in production's BLOCK shape : device breaks 11–3–10 with defects 7/24 vs 12/24, plain breaks unchanged, floor dead even
entries.verdict: In production's 8-page block shape the scoped fix wins device breaks 11-3-10 (defective 29% vs 50%, duplication 6 to 1); plain breaks unchanged; A/A floor 18-19.
entries.decision: PAGE_BREAK_SCOPED with adjacent-page OCR flipped ON in translateBatch and translatePage (PR #5170)

entries.question: by-eye reference for the free IA text lane (pilot, 9 books)
entries.verdict: Two-leaf by-eye reads accepted 142 of 184 held IA books (3 of 9 pilot, 139 of 175 cohort); the split follows the scan, not the date. CER and paid-gate agreement unmeasured.
entries.decision: ia-ocr-ingest --by-eye fills held books with method by_eye (PRs #5190, #5197); 3,372 pages written

entries.question: Which engine should retranslate the re-OCR'd Kanjur pages: Gemini flash, flash-lite, or the Dharmamitra specialist (MITRA-MT)? Blind A/B against 84000
entries.verdict: Against 84000, MITRA-MT trails Gemini badly (fidelity median 3 vs 5, invention 50%); flash mean 4.79, lite 4.43, and lite is the rule's cheapest eligible engine.
entries.decision: MITRA-MT not used for manuscript-OCR Tibetan; lite vs flash left PENDING Derek, re-measured on Batch 2026-10-01 (#4742)

entries.question: Page-break fix hardened and re-measured on the 24 device breaks : Fs2 vs B 10–5–9, defective 38% vs 58%, duplication 2 vs 6; one seam shape fails on the fix arm in both rounds
entries.verdict: Hardened fix Fs2 beats production 10-5-9 on the 24 device breaks, defective 38% vs 58%, duplication 2 vs 6; one seam shape (syllable catchword on an open sentence) fails in both rounds.
entries.decision: Join guards shipped (PR #5169); PAGE_BREAK_SCOPED flipped ON in both worker paths (PR #5170)

entries.question: Echo gate sized on the local mirror before shipping: 229 whole-page flags in 225,583 judged pages (0.10%), 8 of 20 hand-read real; three exemptions take it to 166 flags and 8 of 11 real
entries.verdict: Echo gate flags 166 of 225,583 judged pages (0.07%) after three exemptions, 8 of 11 hand-read real; about 5% of production blocks return short and now go single-page.
entries.decision: Echo gate and block-shift guard shipped before the page-break flip (PR #5176)

entries.question: RETRACTION of the arm label on both #4681 seam draws: the judges read the plain DRAFT, never the repair
entries.verdict: The harness matched 'repaired' but outcomes say 'repair', so both #4681 seam draws judged the plain draft: the 19-14 tie is plain batch vs production; the repair was never judged.
entries.decision: Harness now imports SEAM_SOURCE_REPAIR and throws when a run with repairs substitutes nothing; repaired arm re-judged in a new packet (#4681)

entries.question: Page-break fix , three arms on the 63 seams, source-grounded fidelity judge — fix preferred 32–15 overall, TIE on the device subset it targets; the lookahead trades omissions for duplications
entries.verdict: Fix with lookahead preferred 32-15 on fidelity (omissions 24 to 11) but only 10-7-7 on the 24 device breaks it targets; the lookahead raised duplication 5 to 12.
entries.decision: Lookahead arm F not shipped; the no-lookahead PAGE_BREAK_SCOPED variant went live instead (PR #5170)

entries.question: Seam FIDELITY judge: source beside both translations, gated lane vs production — production ahead on fidelity; the page break is a defect hotspot for BOTH
entries.verdict: With the source shown, production beats the gated batch lane on seam fidelity 25-18 (A/A 14-14); three in four mid-flow page breaks carry a defect in both lanes
entries.decision: Batch + seam-repair lane not flipped (PR #5104); the page-break device fix followed (#5103)

entries.question: Page-break fix without the lookahead (F0) and with a clause-length one (FC), same 63 seams, same judge — F0 halves the defect rate on device breaks with no duplication penalty; any lookahead is where the duplication comes from
entries.verdict: Page-break fix without lookahead (F0) cuts device breaks carrying a defect from 71% to 42% (15-5, p=0.04) with no duplication penalty; any lookahead adds duplication
entries.decision: PAGE_BREAK_SCOPED (F0) is on in translate-worker since 2026-09-25 (#5103, code PR #5111)

entries.question: Batch + seam-repair lane vs production, judged for REAL this time — TIE on fluency; the repair step has fidelity defects the judge cannot see
entries.verdict: Repaired batch lane ties production on seam fluency (19-18, inside the A/A gap), but the repair echoes untranslated source on 2 of 63 seams and invents bridging text
entries.decision: No flip of the batch + seam-repair lane; echo and omission gates added (PR #5089)

entries.question: What is the efficient pattern for finding "body instruction" pages across 4.5M pages? (Jev, $8.57 total)
entries.verdict: A linear probe on page embeddings distilled from Jev puts 44.5% Jev-positives in its top 1,343 pages vs 0.9% at random and 15.6% for the best Jev-only cascade

entries.question: How often does a translation put text on the wrong page? Intra-block drift and continuity leakage
entries.verdict: About 1-1.5% of in-block boundaries put a clause on the wrong page (2.03% flagged, 9/20 real); context leak is mostly a single-page-era defect; a prompt fix did not help
entries.decision: translate-worker rejects drifted/duplicated block pages and re-translates them single-page; prompt fix not shipped (#5021)

entries.question: contact-sheet screen for illustrated pages
entries.verdict: Contact-sheet vision screen finds illustrated pages at 79% recall (v2 prompt); union of two tilings reaches 93.6% at $0.00029/page, 6.8x cheaper than full-page calls

entries.question: can the Archive's own OCR confidence replace the paid reference? NO
entries.verdict: IA word confidence cannot replace the paid gate sample: rejected books score higher (73 vs 51), r = -0.11; the scale is not comparable between items
entries.decision: IA x-confidence not used to gate free text fills; the paid preview sample stays (#4763)

entries.question: Can Jev (TypeSafe's typed-decision model) screen pages for "this tells a body what to do"?
entries.verdict: Jev with the judge-rubric question screens body-instruction pages at AUC 0.94 vs Sonnet labels (0.99 on confident pages), kappa 0.75, for $0.019

entries.question: Can Jev judge page-break continuity? Pilot against the 48 Sonnet-judged junctions
entries.verdict: Jev side-form agrees with Sonnet judges on 5 of 6 both-decided seam junctions (AUC 0.79, n=15) and ties 15/16 A/A pairs; paired form leans RIGHT

entries.question: Batch + seam-repair lane vs production at MID-FLOW seams: the decisive draw
entries.verdict: Tie at 62 mid-flow seams: production 19, lane 14, tie 29 (share 0.58, CI 0.41-0.73); Jev's continuity screen does not replicate (AUC 0.49)

entries.question: Batch API translation lane, first live shadow run on three books: A/A floor, blind judge vs production, and what the Batch API did
entries.verdict: First live shadow of the batch lane: Batch API cancelled 8 of 15 jobs; judge preferred production 5-1 on 6 decided junctions vs A/A floor 79% ties; too thin to call

entries.question: Are the scans in order, and is every page's translation all there? Five exact page-integrity detectors over the whole mirror
entries.verdict: Exact detectors over 6.78M pages find 30,186 duplicate captures (20/20 real) and 66,525 truncated translations (10 real, 0 false); catchword and partial-echo detectors fail

entries.question: Which engine should read Greek print, per period?
entries.verdict: Flash-preview beats flash-lite on Greek print in both periods (1700s 46W/6L, pre-1700 55W/1L); Kraken matches preview on letters; lite 'inadequate' for 1700s withdrawn
entries.decision: Greek OCR routes to flash for visible/new books (#5575); Kraken greek-cllg stays eval-only (#4744)
