entries.question: Can a vision model read hieroglyphs off a printed edition? (baseline for scripts/eval/hieroglyph-ocr/)
entries.verdict: gemini-3-flash-preview cannot read printed hieroglyphs: median anchored sign error 0.78 over 38 pairs (noise level), 37 of 38 outputs looped into recitation

entries.question: Is PaddleOCR-VL-1.6 an acceptable COST LANE for Chinese pages, decided per observed page class?
entries.verdict: PaddleOCR-VL-1.6 passes the cost-lane rule on SKQS manuscript-regular: median dCER -0.028 vs flash-lite, 57W/10L, 0 vs 14 catastrophic; woodblock and typeset directional only
entries.decision: Siku Quanshu Chinese routed to a PaddleOCR-VL cost lane by rule (#4743); lane writer being built (#5600)

entries.question: Does translation survive the Batch API? The block-boundary continuity A/B
entries.verdict: Unseeded batch loses to chained production at the block seam 41-11 (blind judge); a one-page seam repair ties production 27-27 at +15% cost; prereg rule fired 'do not migrate'

entries.question: Syriac retest: do the Beth Mardutho Kraken models read what Gemini loops on?
entries.verdict: Kraken Sophro Mhiro reads Syriac manuscripts at 19% line CER vs 74-79% for both Gemini arms (40/0 vs lite on 40 published-GT pages); Gemini re-OCR does not fix print
entries.decision: Syriac OCR goes to the Kraken lane on Hetzner, never Gemini re-OCR (#4883, PR #5081)

entries.question: Is our Syriac OCR a reading of the page? Against published Syriac and published English
entries.verdict: Gemini Syriac OCR recites rather than reads: 19% of 350 NT 1905 pages carry the right passage at <=10% CER; Isaac and Narsai have no page under 20% CER
entries.decision: Withdraw-by-book recommendation replaced the same day by a Kraken lane + withhold by page (#4883, PR #4901)

entries.question: Does gemini-3.1-flash-lite read early-modern manuscripts and incunables?
entries.verdict: No: flash-preview beats lite on 11/11 items; lite loops on 5 of 7 manuscripts and a 1472 incunable and renders long s as f on roman print.
entries.decision: 18 books held and re-run on gemini-3-flash-preview; global OCR_LITE_ONLY left alone (#4541)

entries.question: Does any current specialist OCR engine beat flash-lite on our pages? (five strata, one protocol: #4743 #4744 #4745 #4746 #4800, registry #4735)
entries.verdict: Only NDL v3 on cursive Japanese beats lite; elsewhere flash-preview > lite >= best specialist, and Paddle matches flash-preview on Chinese woodblock only.
entries.decision: NDL reads cursive Japanese (routing row japanese-cursive, PR #5412) and PaddleOCR-VL reads the Siku Quanshu (row chinese-siku-manuscript, #5600); no other specialist adopted. Closed in #6688

entries.question: Which model should translate classical Chinese? (樂舞 preview pages, SIX arms)
entries.verdict: No arm displaces lite: preview beats it blind (31-16, p=0.040) at 2.2x cost; Chinese-lab arms write less; the judge's test-retest is only 52%.
entries.decision: Lite kept for the Chinese ritual-dance books; pre-registered rule applied as written

entries.question: Which model should translate classical Chinese? (樂舞 preview pages) — RESULT (three arms; superseded by the six-arm read above, which re-judged these same translations)
entries.verdict: Lite and flash-preview are indistinguishable blind (27:26, p=1.0) at 2.2x the price; 2.5-flash is worse (17:33). Lite stays.

entries.question: Which model should translate classical Chinese? (樂舞 preview pages, N-arm) — PREREGISTRATION
entries.verdict: Pre-registration: nine-arm blind-ranking comparison on 60 classical Chinese pages with a fixed decision rule that keeps lite unless an arm beats it cheaply.

entries.question: How good is the IA OCR text we actually WROTE, and where should the cutoff sit?
entries.verdict: Delivered IA text in accepted bands has median CER 3.9% vs a fresh lite read, degrading smoothly with no cliff at 0.85; 26% of written books carry wrong-leaf text.
entries.decision: Ingester forces offset 0 and refuses non-zero votes (REF_SHIFTED); 236 books to re-pair (#4790)

entries.question: Does translation prompt v15 make original-notes real?
entries.verdict: v15 lifts verified original-note rate 66.7% to 96.3% but cuts interpretive notes by a third and loses 8:1 to a blind judge; not flipped, v16 follows.
entries.decision: v15 not flipped; v13 stays; v16 also not established (PR #5703)

entries.question: Can flash-lite text-only cleanup rescue rejected Internet Archive OCR?
entries.verdict: Text-only lite cleanup raises agreement a little (48/60 improved) but lifts no rejected book over the 0.85 gate, costs 86% of image OCR, and invents on unreadable input.
entries.decision: Not a lane for rejected IA OCR (#4727, #4763)

entries.question: Which languages can OCR on flash-lite? Per-language suitability vs the script-family allowlist
entries.verdict: Of 14 languages with a verdict, German, French and Dutch (routed lite) did not pass and Russian and Armenian (routed flash) did; Latin and Italian were never sampled.
entries.decision: Allowlist unchanged: an agreement score cannot settle routing. German, French and Dutch stay on Flash-Lite (routing row latin-script-print); Arabic, Sanskrit and Ge'ez moved to Flash on judged evidence instead (row persian-sanskrit-pali-arabic-print, #5700). Closed in #6688

entries.question: Music: can a VLM read Shaker letteral notation? (first scored run)
entries.verdict: gemini-3-flash-preview reads Shaker letteral pitch poorly (interval NER 0.19) and rhythm at 0.49; on mensural staff it read the printed syllables, not the staff (0.42).
entries.decision: VLMs not used on score pages; score against ground-truth first (music-notation.md)

entries.question: Google Cloud Vision as a cheaper OCR lane?
entries.verdict: Cloud Vision aligns 37/55 pages vs lite's 52/55, loses where both align, and is the worst Tibetan engine tested; garbles but does not invent.
entries.decision: No routing change; Vision is not a lane for any language

entries.question: How wrong is the ground truth? (Track B item 1, #4523)
entries.verdict: Reference error is 0.07% Greek, 0.06% German, 1.15% Latin; Latin engine gaps sit inside it, and our own reference cleaner cost Greek 6.0% of letters.

entries.question: A fabrication detector that needs no reference (Track C, #4523)
entries.verdict: A reference-free detector flagged 51/51 known recitation pages with 0/5 false positives, but only 56 of 349 pages are judgeable and the highest-risk pages are abstained.

entries.question: Bench 2 first arms (superseded by the entry above)
entries.verdict: Interim: Kraken matches Gemini on Latin and Greek print, loses badly on German Fraktur (72.8-89.1%), and its failures are all guard-visible.

entries.question: Bench 2 (complete): can self-hosted OCR replace Gemini on print?
entries.verdict: Kraken, Surya and CHURRO-3B are statistically indistinguishable from Gemini on pages they read; coverage (25-28 of 56 aligned) is the limit and per-segment n is a pilot.

entries.question: Is a similarity gate a workable way to stop duplicated work?
entries.verdict: No: four rounds of tuning could not get the block rate below about 30% while keeping the true duplicates (0.60 blocks 49%, catching 2/2).
entries.decision: No similarity gate; the prior-art guard was made unconditional instead and the similarity list is advisory only

entries.question: Does OCR prompt v17 reduce fabrication vs v15?
entries.verdict: Inconclusive: the first-pass cut in fabrication was one draw; two k=5 runs put the runaway repetition loop on opposite arms.

entries.question: Does #4195's blank-page narrowing work?
entries.verdict: v17 reads the faint-mark page as text on 5/5 runs where v15 said blank, but over-declines elsewhere: a legible Latin note becomes a lacuna.
entries.decision: v17 not promoted; PR #4605 labelled blocked (#4195)
